    ELSEVIER OFFICIAL TEXTBOOK · CHAPTER 3

    CHAPTER 3 Workplace Settings

    第 3 章：工作场所与执业环境（社区、居家与长期照护）
    LEARNING OBJECTIVES · 执业胜任力标准

    OBJECTIVES

    本章学习与执业考核目标 (5 大核心能力指标)
    After reading this chapter, the learner should be able to do the following:
    完成本章研读后，学习者应当能够达成以下核心专业能力考核目标：
    • • Differentiate between community-based care and facility-based care.
      深入辨析并明确区分“社区型照护（Community-Based）”与“机构型照护（Facility-Based）”的本质分野。
    • • List the work settings where support workers are employed.
      详尽列举支持工作者执业的各类具体工作场所谱系（居家、日托、长期照护、辅助生活、综合医院等）。
    • • Differentiate between live-in facilities and outpatient facilities.
      准确区分集中常住式居住设施（Live-in Facilities）与日间门诊设施（Outpatient Facilities）的运作特征。
    • • Describe the various types of live-in facilities.
      全面剖析各类居住型照护机构（辅助生活公寓、养老院 LTC、退休活力公寓、集体之家、安宁关怀院）的收治标准与服务模式。
    • • Identify the benefits and challenges support workers encounter in the workplace.
      客观辨识支持工作者在不同工作环境中所面临的职业发展机遇、核心优势与执业挑战。
    🌐 Elsevier Evolve 官方教参研习配套资源库： http://evolve.elsevier.com/Canada/Sorrentino/SupportWorker
    p. 35
    GLOSSARY

    KEY TERMS · 本章核心专业术语表

    20 核心词汇
    英文术语 / 国际音标 中文对照 / 出处 教材标准学术释义与职业界定
    acute care /əˈkjuːt ker/ 急性医疗照护 p. 36
    Health care that is provided for a relatively short time (usually days to weeks) to diagnose and treat an immediate health issue.
    在相对较短的时间内（通常数天至数周）提供的医疗救护，旨在紧急诊断并救治突发危急健康问题或进行手术救治。
    acute illness /əˈkjuːt ˈɪlnəs/ 急性疾病 p. 36
    An illness or disability that appears suddenly and lasts for a short period, usually less than 3 months.
    起病急骤、症状剧烈且病程相对短暂（通常持续不足 3 个月）的急性突发疾病或创伤（如急性阑尾炎、肺炎）。
    assisted-living facility /əˈsɪstɪd ˈlɪvɪŋ fəˈsɪləti/ 辅助生活照护公寓 / 支持型住房 p. 39
    A live-in facility where residents live in their own private apartments and are provided hospitality and personal care support services.
    一种集中居住型照护设施：案主在独立的私人居室公寓中生活，由机构提供餐饮配餐、安全巡查及部分日常起居生活照料。
    chronic illness /ˈkrɒnɪk ˈɪlnəs/ 慢性疾病 / 迁延性疾病 p. 36
    An ongoing illness or disability, slow or gradual in onset, that may or may not grow worse over time, typically lasting more than 3 months.
    起病缓慢隐匿、病程迁延日久（通常持续超过 3 个月以上）且可能进行性恶化的慢性不可逆疾病（如糖尿病、高血压、慢阻肺）。
    community-based services /kəˈmjuːnəti beɪst ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/ 社区型卫生服务 p. 37
    Health care and support services provided in a community setting, outside of institutional facility walls.
    在传统集中式医疗机构围墙之外的广大社区环境中直接提供的卫生医疗与生活支持服务（如上门居家照护、日托中心）。
    community day program /kəˈmjuːnəti deɪ ˈproʊɡræm/ 社区日间康乐计划 / 成人日托中心 p. 41
    A daytime program providing recreation, socialization, meals, and basic health monitoring for adults needing assistance while living at home.
    面向在家庭中居住但日间需要照料协助的失能长者或心理健康挑战者设立的日间康乐、社交、营养配餐及基础健康监测计划。
    complex continuing care /ˈkɒmplɛks kənˈtɪnjuːɪŋ ker/ 复杂延续性特护 / 亚急性照护 p. 36
    Comprehensive inpatient care for clients recovering from severe illness, surgery, or exacerbation who no longer need acute care but require specialized therapy.
    为脱离急性抢救期、但仍伴有复杂医疗技术需求（复杂造口、机械通气辅助）或需强化康复训练的病患设立的过渡性病房住院特护。
    end-of-life care /ɛnd əv laɪf ker/ 生命终末期照护 p. 37
    Physical, emotional, social, and spiritual support provided to clients approaching death and to their grieving families, encompassing palliative care.
    为停止治愈性抗肿瘤治疗、面临生命终点的绝症案主及其沉痛家属提供的生理止痛、心理抚慰、社交支持与精神灵性陪伴。
    facility-based settings /fəˈsɪləti beɪst ˈsɛtɪŋz/ 机构型照护环境 p. 36
    Workplaces that provide accommodations and around-the-clock professional healthcare within a centralized physical facility.
    在集中设立的实体建筑大楼内为受助群体提供食宿居住以及 24 小时密集临床医疗照护的工作场所（如综合医院、养老院）。
    group home /ɡruːp hoʊm/ 集体家庭公寓 / 小型共同之家 p. 39
    A residential home in a regular neighbourhood housing a small group of individuals with physical, intellectual, or mental health challenges.
    坐落于普通社区居民住宅区内的家庭式独立房屋，为几名伴有发育障碍、肢体残障或心理康复挑战的年轻成人提供集体生活支持。
    hospice /ˈhɒspɪs/ 安宁关怀院 / 临终舒缓驿站 p. 37
    A specialized facility or dedicated program providing compassionate palliative care to terminally ill clients in their final weeks or months.
    专门面向生命仅剩数周至数月的晚期绝症案主设立的如家般温馨的舒缓疗护机构，核心聚焦于消除剧痛与维持心灵安详尊严。
    inpatient /ˈɪnˌpeɪʃənt/ 住院病患 p. 36
    A client who is admitted to a healthcare facility to stay overnight or longer for diagnostic evaluation, surgery, or treatment.
    正式办理住院手续、在医院病房或照护机构内过夜留宿至少一晚以上接受医疗处置与手术照料的病患。
    long-term care facility /lɒŋ tɜːrm ker fəˈsɪləti/ 长期照护院舍 / 养老院 (LTC) p. 38
    A facility providing 24-hour nursing care, ADL assistance, meals, and accommodations to frail seniors unable to live safely at home.
    为无法在私人家庭中自理安全生存的高龄失能或失智长者，提供 24 小时全天候无间断护士临床特护与贴身起居生活照料的专业院舍。
    mental health care services /ˈmɛntl hɛlθ ker ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/ 心理精神卫生服务 p. 37
    Services provided to individuals and families confronting psychiatric illnesses, substance use disorders, or severe emotional trauma.
    专门面向遭受精神分裂症、双相情感障碍、重度抑郁、物质成瘾或严重应激创伤的个体及其家庭开展的专业医疗与心理干预服务。
    outpatient /ˈaʊtˌpeɪʃənt/ 门诊就诊者 / 日间病患 p. 42
    A client who receives healthcare services, tests, or treatments at a clinic or hospital without staying overnight.
    前往医院门诊、日间微创手术室或专科诊所接受检查与治疗，但在当天即返回家中、不在医疗机构内过夜的受助者。
    palliative care /ˈpæliətɪv ker/ 舒缓疗护 / 姑息医疗 p. 37
    Compassionate care aimed at relieving pain and distressing symptoms to optimize quality of life for clients living with life-limiting illness.
    面向罹患不可逆致死性疾病的案主及其家庭，通过积极镇痛与控制痛苦不适症状、最大化提升患者余生生活质量的崇高医学专科。
    rehabilitation services /ˌriːhəˌbɪlɪˈteɪʃən ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/ 康复医疗服务 p. 36
    Therapies, exercise programs, and adaptive methods used to restore, improve, or maintain functional independence following injury or stroke.
    借助物理疗法、作业功能训练及假肢矫形辅具，帮助中风、骨折创伤病患最大化恢复生理机能与生活自立能力的医疗康复过程。
    respite care /ˈrɛspɪt ker/ 暂托喘息照护服务 p. 36
    Short-term temporary care providing relief to exhausted family caregivers who care for dependent family members.
    为常年在家照料重病或失智亲属而身心极度耗竭的家庭照料者提供短期解脱与休整的替代性照料支持服务。
    restorative care /rɪˈstɔːrətɪv ker/ 恢复性照护 p. 36
    Care aimed at regaining, maintaining, and improving the client's strength, mobility, and self-care abilities to their greatest potential.
    旨在重新唤醒并维持案主潜在自理功能、强化肢体肌力、防止失用性退化，促使其发挥最高自主独立性的持续性护理过程。
    retirement home /rɪˈtaɪərmənt hoʊm/ 退休活力公寓 / 自理养老社区 p. 38
    A privately paid residential facility where independent, mobile older adults rent private suites and receive hospitality services like meals and housekeeping.
    主要由长者个人自费租住的活力养老社区：入住长者神志清晰、具有独立行动能力，由机构提供餐饮配餐、室内保洁与文娱活动。
    acute care p. 36
    /əˈkjuːt ker/
    急性医疗照护

    Health care that is provided for a relatively short time (usually days to weeks) to diagnose and treat an immediate health issue.

    在相对较短的时间内（通常数天至数周）提供的医疗救护，旨在紧急诊断并救治突发危急健康问题或进行手术救治。

    acute illness p. 36
    /əˈkjuːt ˈɪlnəs/
    急性疾病

    An illness or disability that appears suddenly and lasts for a short period, usually less than 3 months.

    起病急骤、症状剧烈且病程相对短暂（通常持续不足 3 个月）的急性突发疾病或创伤（如急性阑尾炎、肺炎）。

    assisted-living facility p. 39
    /əˈsɪstɪd ˈlɪvɪŋ fəˈsɪləti/
    辅助生活照护公寓 / 支持型住房

    A live-in facility where residents live in their own private apartments and are provided hospitality and personal care support services.

    一种集中居住型照护设施：案主在独立的私人居室公寓中生活，由机构提供餐饮配餐、安全巡查及部分日常起居生活照料。

    chronic illness p. 36
    /ˈkrɒnɪk ˈɪlnəs/
    慢性疾病 / 迁延性疾病

    An ongoing illness or disability, slow or gradual in onset, that may or may not grow worse over time, typically lasting more than 3 months.

    起病缓慢隐匿、病程迁延日久（通常持续超过 3 个月以上）且可能进行性恶化的慢性不可逆疾病（如糖尿病、高血压、慢阻肺）。

    community-based services p. 37
    /kəˈmjuːnəti beɪst ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/
    社区型卫生服务

    Health care and support services provided in a community setting, outside of institutional facility walls.

    在传统集中式医疗机构围墙之外的广大社区环境中直接提供的卫生医疗与生活支持服务（如上门居家照护、日托中心）。

    community day program p. 41
    /kəˈmjuːnəti deɪ ˈproʊɡræm/
    社区日间康乐计划 / 成人日托中心

    A daytime program providing recreation, socialization, meals, and basic health monitoring for adults needing assistance while living at home.

    面向在家庭中居住但日间需要照料协助的失能长者或心理健康挑战者设立的日间康乐、社交、营养配餐及基础健康监测计划。

    complex continuing care p. 36
    /ˈkɒmplɛks kənˈtɪnjuːɪŋ ker/
    复杂延续性特护 / 亚急性照护

    Comprehensive inpatient care for clients recovering from severe illness, surgery, or exacerbation who no longer need acute care but require specialized therapy.

    为脱离急性抢救期、但仍伴有复杂医疗技术需求（复杂造口、机械通气辅助）或需强化康复训练的病患设立的过渡性病房住院特护。

    end-of-life care p. 37
    /ɛnd əv laɪf ker/
    生命终末期照护

    Physical, emotional, social, and spiritual support provided to clients approaching death and to their grieving families, encompassing palliative care.

    为停止治愈性抗肿瘤治疗、面临生命终点的绝症案主及其沉痛家属提供的生理止痛、心理抚慰、社交支持与精神灵性陪伴。

    facility-based settings p. 36
    /fəˈsɪləti beɪst ˈsɛtɪŋz/
    机构型照护环境

    Workplaces that provide accommodations and around-the-clock professional healthcare within a centralized physical facility.

    在集中设立的实体建筑大楼内为受助群体提供食宿居住以及 24 小时密集临床医疗照护的工作场所（如综合医院、养老院）。

    group home p. 39
    /ɡruːp hoʊm/
    集体家庭公寓 / 小型共同之家

    A residential home in a regular neighbourhood housing a small group of individuals with physical, intellectual, or mental health challenges.

    坐落于普通社区居民住宅区内的家庭式独立房屋，为几名伴有发育障碍、肢体残障或心理康复挑战的年轻成人提供集体生活支持。

    hospice p. 37
    /ˈhɒspɪs/
    安宁关怀院 / 临终舒缓驿站

    A specialized facility or dedicated program providing compassionate palliative care to terminally ill clients in their final weeks or months.

    专门面向生命仅剩数周至数月的晚期绝症案主设立的如家般温馨的舒缓疗护机构，核心聚焦于消除剧痛与维持心灵安详尊严。

    inpatient p. 36
    /ˈɪnˌpeɪʃənt/
    住院病患

    A client who is admitted to a healthcare facility to stay overnight or longer for diagnostic evaluation, surgery, or treatment.

    正式办理住院手续、在医院病房或照护机构内过夜留宿至少一晚以上接受医疗处置与手术照料的病患。

    long-term care facility p. 38
    /lɒŋ tɜːrm ker fəˈsɪləti/
    长期照护院舍 / 养老院 (LTC)

    A facility providing 24-hour nursing care, ADL assistance, meals, and accommodations to frail seniors unable to live safely at home.

    为无法在私人家庭中自理安全生存的高龄失能或失智长者，提供 24 小时全天候无间断护士临床特护与贴身起居生活照料的专业院舍。

    mental health care services p. 37
    /ˈmɛntl hɛlθ ker ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/
    心理精神卫生服务

    Services provided to individuals and families confronting psychiatric illnesses, substance use disorders, or severe emotional trauma.

    专门面向遭受精神分裂症、双相情感障碍、重度抑郁、物质成瘾或严重应激创伤的个体及其家庭开展的专业医疗与心理干预服务。

    outpatient p. 42
    /ˈaʊtˌpeɪʃənt/
    门诊就诊者 / 日间病患

    A client who receives healthcare services, tests, or treatments at a clinic or hospital without staying overnight.

    前往医院门诊、日间微创手术室或专科诊所接受检查与治疗，但在当天即返回家中、不在医疗机构内过夜的受助者。

    palliative care p. 37
    /ˈpæliətɪv ker/
    舒缓疗护 / 姑息医疗

    Compassionate care aimed at relieving pain and distressing symptoms to optimize quality of life for clients living with life-limiting illness.

    面向罹患不可逆致死性疾病的案主及其家庭，通过积极镇痛与控制痛苦不适症状、最大化提升患者余生生活质量的崇高医学专科。

    rehabilitation services p. 36
    /ˌriːhəˌbɪlɪˈteɪʃən ˈsɜːrvɪsɪz/
    康复医疗服务

    Therapies, exercise programs, and adaptive methods used to restore, improve, or maintain functional independence following injury or stroke.

    借助物理疗法、作业功能训练及假肢矫形辅具，帮助中风、骨折创伤病患最大化恢复生理机能与生活自立能力的医疗康复过程。

    respite care p. 36
    /ˈrɛspɪt ker/
    暂托喘息照护服务

    Short-term temporary care providing relief to exhausted family caregivers who care for dependent family members.

    为常年在家照料重病或失智亲属而身心极度耗竭的家庭照料者提供短期解脱与休整的替代性照料支持服务。

    restorative care p. 36
    /rɪˈstɔːrətɪv ker/
    恢复性照护

    Care aimed at regaining, maintaining, and improving the client's strength, mobility, and self-care abilities to their greatest potential.

    旨在重新唤醒并维持案主潜在自理功能、强化肢体肌力、防止失用性退化，促使其发挥最高自主独立性的持续性护理过程。

    retirement home p. 38
    /rɪˈtaɪərmənt hoʊm/
    退休活力公寓 / 自理养老社区

    A privately paid residential facility where independent, mobile older adults rent private suites and receive hospitality services like meals and housekeeping.

    主要由长者个人自费租住的活力养老社区：入住长者神志清晰、具有独立行动能力，由机构提供餐饮配餐、室内保洁与文娱活动。

    Support workers are employed in an extraordinary variety of healthcare settings across Canada. Some support workers provide services to clients living in their own homes, while others work in group homes, retirement communities, long-term care homes, or acute care hospitals. Each work setting presents distinct clinical environments, philosophies of care, teamwork models, and professional rewards and challenges.

    支持工作者在加拿大全境极其广泛多元的医疗卫生服务环境中执业。有的从业者深入千家万户为私人住宅中的长者提供居家上门照料，有的则在小型集体公寓、退休活力社区、长期照护养老院（LTC）或大型综合急症医院病区开展工作。每一种执业环境都呈现出截然不同的临床工作模式、照护哲学、团队协作结构以及专属的职业发展机遇与挑战。

    p. 36

    COMMUNITY-BASED VERSUS FACILITY-BASED CARE

    两大执业阵地的本质分野：社区型照护 vs 机构型照护

    All workplaces in which support workers practice can be grouped into two broad categories: community-based settings and facility-based settings. Understanding the distinction between these two realms is essential for career planning and clinical practice.

    支持工作者所涉足的全部工作场所，在宏观上均可以系统归纳划分为两大核心阵地：“社区型照护环境”（Community-Based Settings）与“机构型照护环境”（Facility-Based Settings）。深刻理解这两大领域的本质分野与运作机制，对于职业生涯规划及临床规范操作至关重要。

    Community-Based Settings

    社区型照护环境（在医疗机构围墙之外）

    Community-based settings encompass health care and support services delivered outside institutional walls. Services are provided in clients' private homes, supportive housing suites, community day centers, and schools. Care in community settings is focused on enabling clients to remain in their homes, promoting autonomy, preventing acute hospitalizations, and supporting family caregivers.

    社区型照护环境涵盖了在传统实体医疗机构围墙之外开展的全部卫生医疗与生活支持服务。服务阵地直接扎根于案主私人住宅、支持型保障住房居室、社区日间活动中心以及中小学校园。社区照护的核心使命在于：赋能长者留在熟悉的家庭环境中自立生活、最大化维系自主自决主权、防范因突发失能而过早被动入院，并为家庭长期照料者提供休整喘息。

    Facility-Based Settings

    机构型照护环境（集中式实体设施）

    Facility-based settings are workplaces where accommodations and continuous round-the-clock professional health care are provided within a centralized building. Facilities range from acute care hospitals and rehabilitation centres to long-term care facilities and residential hospices. In facilities, multidisciplinary teams are stationed on-site 24 hours a day to manage complex, unpredictable, or severe chronic health needs.

    机构型照护环境是指在集中设立的实体建筑大楼内，为受助群体提供食宿居住以及 24 小时全天候无间断专业医疗护理与起居生活照料的工作场所。机构谱系涵盖了从急症综合医院、大型康复中心，到长期照护养老院（LTC）以及专科临终关怀院（Hospice）。在机构环境中，由医生、护士及治疗师组成的跨学科团队全天候常驻现场，随时应对复杂、不可预测或严重的急慢性病情变化。

    p. 37

    COMMUNITY-BASED WORKPLACE SETTINGS

    多样化的社区型工作场所谱系

    Working in Indigenous Communities

    在原住民社区执业的崇高使命与文化挑战

    Support workers playing vital roles in First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities must develop profound cultural humility and safety. Practitioners collaborate with local community health representatives, Elders, and traditional healers. In remote fly-in northern communities, support workers face unique challenges, including extreme weather, limited medical infrastructure, and supply shortages, but experience profound professional gratitude and community connection.

    在第一民族保留地、因纽特人北极聚居区以及梅蒂斯人社区提供支持服务的从业者，必须具备深厚的人文关怀情操与“文化谦逊与安全”（Cultural Humility & Safety）素养。支持工作者需与当地社区卫生代表、部族德高望重的长老及传统草药治疗师密切配合。在交通闭塞、需搭乘小型水上飞机方能抵达的北部偏远村落中，从业者面临着极寒严冬、医疗基础设施匮乏及物资补给受限等艰苦挑战，但亦能收获来自原住民社群无比深沉的敬意与职业自豪。

    Community Health Centres and Home Care Agencies

    社区卫生健康中心与家庭医生门诊

    Community health centres (CHCs) offer interprofessional primary care, health promotion, disease prevention, and community advocacy. Support workers may assist with clinical clinics, patient transport, and translation. In home care agencies (both for-profit and not-for-profit), support workers are dispatched to provide personal care and home management in clients' residences.

    社区卫生健康中心（CHCs）提供涵盖跨专业团队的初级医疗接诊、健康教育宣讲、慢性病早筛以及社区权益发声服务。支持工作者可在其中协助门诊分诊、行动不便长者转运及双语翻译沟通。而在各省遍布的公立、私立居家照护中介机构中，支持工作者则接受统一排班调度，奔波穿梭于社区之间开展入户上门贴身生活照料与家居保洁服务。

    p. 38

    WORKING IN HOME CARE

    深入千家万户：居家照护执业全貌

    Home care is the most rapidly expanding sector of support work. Support workers in home care enter clients' private sanctuaries, working autonomously while following assigned care plans. A home care support worker's duties range from morning hygiene and wound dressing assistance to cooking culturally preferred meals and providing warm companionship.

    居家照护是当前整个加拿大支持工作领域发展最迅猛、需求最旺盛的黄金板块。从事居家照护的从业人员直接踏入案主私密的家庭生活领地，在严格遵循指定照护计划的前提下高度自主地开展工作。其日常工作内容涵盖从晨间洗漱擦浴、协助伤口换药，到为长者烹饪其喜爱的传统风味热餐以及提供促膝长谈的情感抚慰。

    BOX 3.1 Benefits and Challenges of Working in Home Care

    专栏 3.1：居家照护执业的优势与挑战对比表
    BENEFITS OF WORKING IN HOME CARE:
    • High level of professional autonomy and independence during daily visits.
    • Close, meaningful, one-on-one relationships with clients and their families.
    • Diverse workday and varied home environments; no monotonous facility routine.
    • Flexible shift scheduling and opportunities for part-time or full-time flexibility.
    • Satisfaction of enabling vulnerable individuals to remain safely in their homes.

    CHALLENGES OF WORKING IN HOME CARE:
    • Working alone with no on-site supervisor or colleagues immediately present for emergencies.
    • Extensive travel between appointments in harsh winter weather and traffic.
    • Unpredictable home environments: Clutter, poor lighting, pest infestations, secondhand smoke, aggressive pets.
    • Uncontrolled ergonomic conditions: Non-adjustable beds and cramped bathrooms strain body mechanics.
    • Risk of personal isolation and navigating tense family dynamics.
    居家照护执业的显著优势：
    • 极高的日常工作独立性与专业自主权，摆脱了医院车间般的严密盯梢。
    • 能够与案主及其家庭建立起深刻、真挚且一对一的高度信任纽带。
    • 每天穿梭于不同家庭与多元文化背景之中，工作环境丰富多变，毫无机构流水线工作的枯燥感。
    • 班次安排极富弹性，可根据个人生活节奏灵活选择全职或兼职排班。
    • 能够亲眼见证并切身感受到由于自己的协助，案主得以安全尊严留在家中的巨大成就感。

    居家照护执业面临的客观挑战：
    • 独自一人单兵作战，遇突发病情恶化时现场没有主管护士或同事能瞬间赶到协助。
    • 需每日在暴风雪、冻雨等恶劣天气及交通拥堵中长途驱车奔波于各预约家庭之间。
    • 私人住宅环境不可控：部分家庭堆满杂物通道狭窄、光线昏暗、二手烟弥漫、甚至伴有凶猛未栓绳宠物。
    • 人体工效学条件恶劣：普通低矮家庭床铺无法升降、逼仄的卫生间极大增加腰背肌肉拉伤风险。
    • 易产生职业孤独感，且需小心翼翼应对复杂微妙的家庭矛盾与亲属情绪摩擦。
    p. 39

    Community Day Programs (Adult Day Centres)

    成人日间康乐计划（日托中心）

    Community day programs provide daytime recreation, therapeutic exercise, socialization, and hot meals for older adults or individuals with physical or cognitive challenges. Clients attend for several hours during the day and return home in the evening. Support workers lead crafts, exercise classes, assist with meals, and provide essential personal care while family caregivers receive much-needed respite.

    “社区成人日间康乐计划”（Adult Day Programs / 日托中心）为白天留守在家的长者或伴有身心认知障碍的成年人提供日间文娱社交、康复体操、智力益智游戏以及营养热餐供应。案主通常在早晨由无障碍专车接往中心活动数小时，傍晚再返回自己家中居住。支持工作者在中心协助组织工艺美术、带领健美体操、协助分发午餐，并提供及时的如厕与擦浴协助，同时使常年照料的家属获得白天宝贵的喘息休整。

    Assisted-Living and Supportive Housing Facilities

    辅助生活照护公寓与支持型保障公寓

    Assisted-living facilities (also called supportive housing) offer a residential environment bridging the gap between independent home living and 24-hour nursing homes. Residents rent private bachelor or one-bedroom suites equipped with private bathrooms and kitchenettes.

    “辅助生活照护公寓”（Assisted-Living Facilities / 支持型保障住房）是一种介于完全自理居家生活与 24 小时密集特护养老院之间的绝佳过渡居住模式。入住长者租住包含独立卫生间与迷你小厨房的单身或一居室套房。

    Hospitality services such as central dining meals, weekly housekeeping, and 24-hour emergency response staff are provided. Support workers assist residents with scheduled personal care (bathing, dressing, medication reminders).

    机构统一提供中央餐厅一日三餐、每周室内深度保洁换洗床单、以及 24 小时紧急拉绳拉铃响应系统。常驻的支持工作者按预约计划每天上门协助洗澡更衣、提醒服药，既捍卫了长者的私密领地，又筑牢了安全后盾。

    p. 40

    FACILITY-BASED WORKPLACE SETTINGS: LONG-TERM CARE

    机构型照护环境：长期照护院舍（LTC / 养老院）

    Long-term care facilities (also referred to as homes for the aged, continuing care facilities, or nursing homes) provide accommodations, 24-hour registered nursing care, and comprehensive personal support services to individuals who can no longer live safely in their own homes due to severe physical limitations, multimorbidity, or advanced dementia.

    长期照护院舍（Long-Term Care Facilities，在各省亦称老年之家、持续关照中心或养老院）为由于严重的身体生理机能丧失、多重慢病共存或晚期阿尔茨海默病而无法在私人家庭中自理生存的重度失能失智长者，提供全天候居住食宿、24 小时无间断注册护士临床特护以及全方位的贴身生活起居支持。

    Creating a Homelike Atmosphere

    营造温馨家庭般的生活氛围（Homelike Atmosphere）

    A long-term care home is not an acute hospital where people stay for a few days to recover from surgery; it is the resident's true and permanent home for the remainder of their life. For this reason, maintaining a warm, comfortable, homelike atmosphere is of supreme ethical importance.

    长期照护养老院绝非人们为了开刀做手术短暂停留数日的冰冷急症医院，它是长者生命晚期余生常住的“真正的家”！正因如此，竭尽所能消除冷酷压抑的医疗感、精心营造并维系如家般温馨温暖的生活氛围（Homelike atmosphere），具有至高无上的伦理道德意义。

    Facilities encourage residents to personalize their private bedrooms with personal furniture, bedspreads, family photographs, and cherished mementos. Support workers must treat each resident's room as their private living room, knocking respectfully before entering and honouring the resident's personal habits and lifestyle preferences.

    机构大力鼓励长者携带私人家居用品、专属床单、全家福相框及钟爱的纪念品布置居室。支持工作者必须像对待长者的私人客厅一样敬重其个人空间，进门前必先轻叩房门，充分尊重长者的个人起居习惯与生活方式。

    p. 41

    BOX 3.2 Benefits and Challenges of Working in a Long-Term Care Facility

    专栏 3.2：长期照护院舍（养老院）执业的优势与挑战对比表
    BENEFITS OF WORKING IN LONG-TERM CARE:
    • On-site clinical support: Registered nurses and multidisciplinary team members are always available for emergencies and guidance.
    • Predictable shift hours and consistent, structured work routines.
    • Opportunities to build long-term, affectionate bonds with residents and their families over months or years.
    • Direct access to specialized ergonomic transfer equipment (ceiling lifts, sit-to-stand devices, shower trolleys).
    • Strong peer camaraderie and teamwork with fellow support workers and healthcare colleagues.

    CHALLENGES OF WORKING IN LONG-TERM CARE:
    • Heavy physical workload: Assisting multiple dependent residents with transfers, hygiene, and positioning.
    • Emotionally challenging encounters with cognitive decline, repetitive agitation, and dementia behaviours.
    • Experiencing the grief of losing beloved residents as they decline and pass away.
    • Navigating busy, fast-paced shift routines with strict timeframes for meals, baths, and toileting rounds.
    • Coping with facility staffing shortages and balancing care for 8 to 12 high-need residents per shift.
    长期照护养老院执业的显著优势：
    • 强大的临床后盾支撑：注册护士（RN/RPN）及跨学科团队时刻常驻现场，遇紧急状况可瞬间获得指导。
    • 上下班工作作息规律稳定，轮班工时与轮休计划高度可预期。
    • 能够与同一批长者朝夕相处数月乃至数年，建立起如家人般深厚、温暖且充满依恋的情感纽带。
    • 机构全面配备现代化的人体工效学设备（天花板轨道吊装移位机、坐站辅助机、液压洗浴平床）。
    • 拥有强大的同事团队同袍情谊，在遇到繁重操作时可随时呼叫双人协同搬运协作。

    长期照护养老院执业面临的客观挑战：
    • 极高的体力负荷：每班需连续协助多位重度失能长者完成复杂的床上翻身、轮椅转移与如厕排泄。
    • 心理情绪压力大：需耐心应对重度阿尔茨海默病患者出现的激越攻击、反复游荡、昼夜颠倒等异常行为。
    • 频繁直面死别之痛：见证朝夕相伴的长者身体机能逐步衰退直至离世，需承受巨大的情感哀伤。
    • 工作节奏快且受制于严格的时间表：餐饮出餐、洗浴排班与定时如厕巡查必须分秒必争完成。
    • 面临全行业人手紧缺压力：每人每班需承担 8 至 12 名重度失能老人的密集特护，对体魄与耐力要求极高。

    FIGURE 3.6 Socialization in Long-Term Care

    图 3.6：长期照护院舍中促进长者社交互动与文娱康乐
    FIGURE 3.6: Residents in residential care enjoy socializing in shared communal lounges. (iStockphoto/monkeybusinessimages.)
    Support workers play a crucial role in encouraging residents to leave their private rooms to participate in group dining, musical events, and social games, which combats depression and cognitive stagnation.
    图 3.6：长者在照护院舍公共文娱活动大厅中愉快开展社交联谊（iStockphoto/monkeybusinessimages）。
    支持工作者发挥着关键纽带作用：鼓励长者走出私人寝室，融入集体就餐、音乐欣赏及棋牌益智活动，有效驱散抑郁情绪并延缓认知衰退。
    p. 42

    OTHER LIVE-IN WORKPLACE SETTINGS

    其他集中常住式居住照护机构

    Retirement Homes (Retirement Residences)

    退休自理活力公寓（自费养老社区）

    Retirement homes are residential facilities catering to older adults who are cognitively intact and independently mobile, but choose to live in a congregate setting offering hospitality services (meals, housekeeping, recreation) and optional personal support. Retirement homes in Canada are almost entirely privately funded by residents and are regulated under provincial retirement homes legislation (such as the Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority in Ontario). Support workers in retirement homes provide medication reminders, assist with light ADLs, and ensure resident safety.

    “退休自理活力公寓”（Retirement Homes）专为神志清晰、具有独立行动能力但希望摆脱做饭保洁家务繁琐的长者而设计。机构提供包含高品质餐饮、居室深度保洁、康乐旅游在内的一站式酒店式生活服务以及自选的贴身起居照护。在加拿大，退休公寓绝大部分属于长者全额自费的私营活力社区，受省级专门法案（如安省《退休之家管理署》RHRA）依法监管。在其中执业的支持工作者主要负责定时提醒服药、协助轻度洗浴更衣以及执行夜间安全巡视。

    Group Homes

    小型集体家庭公寓（集体之家）

    A group home is a residential home located in an ordinary residential neighbourhood that houses a small number of individuals (typically 3 to 8 residents) living with developmental disabilities, physical impairments, or psychiatric illnesses. The philosophy of group home living is full community integration and normalizing daily routines. Support workers in group homes assist residents with cooking, shopping, taking public transit, vocational employment, and managing life skills.

    “小型集体家庭公寓”（Group Home / 集体之家）是坐落在普通民居街道中的独栋住宅，通常常住 3 至 8 名伴有发育障碍、肢体残障或精神康复挑战的年轻成人。集体之家的最高核心哲学是“去机构化”与“全社会深度融入”——让受助者像正常人一样在普通居民区中生活。支持工作者在其中扮演生活辅导员与照护者双重角色：协助其买菜做饭、学习乘坐公共汽车出行、参与庇护性工场就业，并掌握独立生活管理技能。

    p. 43

    WORKING DIRECTLY FOR CLIENTS

    受雇形式深度拆解：直接受雇于案主本人（私家专属支持）

    Some support workers choose to be employed directly by the client or the client's family, rather than through a healthcare agency or facility. Under this direct employment arrangement, the client or family acts as the formal employer: interviewing, hiring, supervising, paying wages, and determining daily tasks. Provincial direct-funding programs often provide government grants directly to individuals with severe physical disabilities so they can hire and direct their own attendant services.

    部分支持工作者选择不通过派遣中介机构或医疗院舍，而是直接与受助案主或其家属签订劳动雇佣合同。在这一“直接雇佣”（Direct-Hire）模式下，案主本人或其法定监护人成为法定雇主：负责自主面试、录用、日常督导排班、发放工资并界定每日工作职责。在加拿大各省的“直接资助计划”（Direct-Funding Programs）下，政府常常将专项照护津贴直接拨付给肢体残障人士个人，赋能其自主招募并督导专属的私人护理员。

    BOX 3.3 Benefits and Challenges of Working Directly for Clients

    专栏 3.3：直接受雇于案主本人的优势与执业挑战对比表
    BENEFITS OF WORKING DIRECTLY FOR CLIENTS:
    • Potential for higher hourly wages: Bypassing agency administrative overhead allows more funds to go directly to the worker.
    • Working with only one consistent client; deep rapport and personalized care.
    • Highly flexible working hours mutually negotiated directly with the client.
    • Fostering genuine empowerment: The client directs their own care according to personal lifestyle.

    CHALLENGES OF WORKING DIRECTLY FOR CLIENTS:
    • Complete absence of clinical supervision: No registered nurse available to assess problems or delegate tasks.
    • Lack of institutional employment benefits: No paid sick leave, vacation pay, pension, or health insurance coverage.
    • Administrative burden: Worker must manage own Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Employment Insurance (EI), and income tax deductions.
    • Precarious job security: If the client is hospitalized, moves to a facility, or passes away, employment terminates immediately.
    • Risk of role blur and unrealistic demands: Clients may demand tasks far outside support work or legal scope.
    直接受雇于案主本人的显著优势：
    • 潜在更高的每小时净收入：省去了商业中介机构层层抽成的管理费，资金直接落入从业者腰包。
    • 长期专职服务于唯一一位案主，彼此高度默契，照护流程极富个性化与温情。
    • 上下班工作时间由劳资双方直接面对面协商，排班极具人情味与灵活性。
    • 真正体现赋权原则：案主本人作为雇主主导自身的全部生活细节，尊严感得到最大化释放。

    直接受雇于案主本人面临的严峻挑战：
    • 彻底丧失专业护士的临床督导：现场没有任何注册护士负责风险评估或合法委派，遇事需自担法律风险。
    • 缺乏机构法定的员工福利：通常没有带薪病假、法定年假补偿、职业养老金或商业医疗补充保险。
    • 沉重的个人财务申报负担：从业者必须自行申报加拿大退休金计划（CPP）、就业保险（EI）并缴纳自雇所得税。
    • 职业稳定性极度脆弱：一旦案主突发急病长期住院、搬入养老院或不幸离世，劳动雇佣关系瞬间立刻终止。
    • 职责界限模糊易被过度索取：个别雇主可能提出超出支持工作甚至超出法律执业红线的非分高危要求。
    p. 44

    WORKING IN HOSPITALS AND ACUTE CARE SETTINGS

    综合医院、急症外科与专科亚急性病区执业全貌

    Hospitals are high-intensity, technology-driven workplaces where clients are admitted for short-term diagnostic evaluation, emergency resuscitation, surgical intervention, or severe acute medical treatment. Within hospitals, support workers (often termed patient care assistants or health care aides) collaborate closely with registered nurses and physicians across specialized clinical units:

    急症综合医院是高节奏、高技术密集的现代医疗核心堡垒。患者在此接受短期的急诊抢救、复杂外科大手术或急重症内科药物救治。在综合医院内，支持工作者（通常称为病患照护助理 PCA 或医疗助手 HCA）在注册护士与主管医生的紧密督导下，活跃在各大专科病房之中：

    • • Medical-Surgical Units: Assisting postoperative clients with mobilization, hygiene, vital signs, and surgical bed management.
      普通内外科病区：协助手术后早期的病患进行下床平稳活动、全身擦浴清洁、测量生命体征及术后病床规范整理。
    • • Special Care Units: Assisting in intensive care (ICU), coronary care (CCU), or burn units under direct one-on-one RN supervision.
      特护重症病房：在重症监护室（ICU）、冠心病监护病房（CCU）或烧伤中心，在专科特护注册护士的一对一床旁严密指导下协助基础生活支持。
    • • Maternal-Child Units: Assisting postpartum mothers with personal hygiene, newborn bathing demonstrations, and room restocking.
      母婴与产科病房：协助刚生产的产妇完成会阴冲洗清洗、展示新生儿温水洗澡操作，并补充无菌婴儿织物耗材。
    • • Subacute (Complex Continuing Care) Units: Providing restorative care, functional rehabilitation, and mobilization for patients recovering from major strokes or complex orthopedic surgery before discharge.
      亚急性（复杂延续性特护）病房：为经历大面积脑中风或复杂粉碎性骨折术后、病情趋于稳定但无法立刻出院的患者提供系统的恢复性功能锻炼与日常生活自理再训练。
    p. 45

    BOX 3.4 Benefits and Challenges of Working in a Hospital Setting

    专栏 3.4：急症综合医院执业的优势与挑战对比表
    BENEFITS OF WORKING IN A HOSPITAL:
    • Exposure to complex clinical conditions, advanced medical technology, and cutting-edge treatments.
    • Direct, constant supervision and learning opportunities alongside highly skilled RNs, NPs, and MDs.
    • Broad experience working across diverse medical specialties (surgery, pediatrics, emergency, orthopedics).
    • Strong collective union agreements providing competitive hourly wages, benefits, and shift premiums.
    • Standardized hospital policies, rigid infection control protocols, and abundant personal protective equipment (PPE).

    CHALLENGES OF WORKING IN A HOSPITAL:
    • High-stress, fast-paced acute environment requiring rapid adaptation to emergency crises.
    • Rapid patient turnover: Patients are discharged quickly, limiting opportunities to form deep therapeutic bonds.
    • Strictly defined, highly scrutinized roles where support workers perform narrow, repetitive supportive tasks.
    • Mandatory rotating shift work, including nights, weekends, and holidays, disrupting work-life balance.
    • Exposure to severe trauma, catastrophic blood loss, acute clinical deterioration, and infectious pathogens.
    急症综合医院执业的显著优势：
    • 能够直面复杂疑难危重症谱系，亲身体验前沿医疗高新科技与尖端救治手段，极大开阔临床视野。
    • 时刻置身于技术精湛的注册护士（RN）、执业护士（NP）及专科医生身边，享有无与伦比的现场观摩进修机会。
    • 拥有在不同医疗专科（外科、儿科、急诊科、骨科病房）轮转锻炼的宝贵职业经历。
    • 受强大的公立医疗工会集体劳资协议保护，享有极具竞争力的时薪待遇、优厚补充医疗福利及倒班夜班津贴。
    • 医院拥有极其标准严谨的规章流程、滴水不漏的感控隔离消杀机制以及极其充足充裕的个人防护装备（PPE）。

    急症综合医院执业面临的客观挑战：
    • 高度紧绷、步步惊心的高压急救环境，要求从业者具备极强的临场应变与抗压心理素质。
    • 病患周转极快：患者术后数天即迅速办理出院，从业人员几乎没有机会与患者建立起深厚持久的情感信任。
    • 职责界限受极其严苛的审核与规限，工作内容常常局限于流水线式的生命体征测量与铺床搬运。
    • 必须严格参与白班、中班、通宵大夜班的全年无休三班倒轮转，对个人生理节律与家庭生活带来巨大挑战。
    • 频繁直面严重创伤、大量呕血便血等残酷抢救场面以及高浓度的耐药耐甲氧西林超级细菌传染源。

    Choosing where to work depends on your personality, career goals, and values. Whether you thrive in the intimate autonomy of home care, the affectionate community of long-term care, or the fast-paced teamwork of a hospital, support work offers an unmatched variety of meaningful employment opportunities in high demand across Canada!

    究竟选择哪一种执业环境，完全取决于你个人的性格特质、职业生涯追求以及内心的核心价值取向。无论你是钟情于社区居家照护的温馨独立与专业自主，还是渴望在长期照护院舍中与长者建立如亲人般的朝夕依恋，抑或是热衷于在急症综合医院的现代化前线体验争分夺秒的跨学科团队协作——支持工作都能在加拿大这片土地上为你提供绝无仅有、选择无限且炙手可热的崇高就业舞台！

    p. 46

    CHAPTER REVIEW

    本章复习与临床思维修炼

    KEY POINTS

    全章核心知识要点精要清单
    • • Support workers must understand the scope of practice established by provincial education standards and employer policies, always staying strictly within their role. Performing delegated tasks requires following safe clinical steps to protect clients.
      无论在何种工作场所执业，支持工作者都必须全面熟知省级教育考评大纲与雇主管理规章所设定的法定执业范围，誓死严守职业权限边界；执行受委派任务时必须严格执行防范差错的安全操作步骤。
    • • The Canadian healthcare system is intentionally shifting resources to decrease acute hospital costs and expand community-based services.
      当前加拿大医疗体制的最鲜明发展大趋势是：大幅压缩昂贵的医院住院床位开支，坚决将财政与人力资源战略重心转移至社区型服务网络。
    • • The expansion of home- and community-based programs has created an unprecedented, growing demand for skilled support workers.
      随着社区居家照护与日间康乐项目的蓬勃扩展，全社会对高素质基层支持工作者的需求呈现出爆发式增长。
    • • Community-based settings encompass home care agencies, community health centres, school boards, doctors' offices, adult day programs, and supportive housing.
      社区型执业阵地涵盖：居家照护派遣中介、社区卫生服务中心、教育局特教随班就读、医生门诊、成人日间托老中心以及支持型保障公寓。
    • • When working directly for a client, the client/family selects, hires, supervises, and pays the worker, providing higher autonomy but lacking clinical nursing supervision.
      直接受雇于案主本人时，由家庭直接面试录用、考勤发薪并主导照护，虽享有较高时薪与自主性，但彻底缺乏专业护士的临床督导与工伤失业保障。
    • • Facility-based services provide centralized 24-hour accommodations and professional care within hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and long-term care homes.
      机构型执业阵地在实体大楼内提供集中食宿居住与 24 小时密集专业照料，涵盖急症综合医院、专科康复中心及长期照护养老院。
    • • Every work setting presents distinct advantages and specific professional challenges; support workers must carefully assess their personal strengths and preferences.
      每一种工作环境都伴随着极其独特的职业优势与不可忽视的执业挑战；从业者需结合自身性格与体魄优势做出最明智的职业抉择。

    CRITICAL THINKING IN PRACTICE

    临床实践中的批判性思维修炼

    CRITICAL THINKING: Determining Your Ideal Workplace Setting

    职业抉择实战推演：如何科学评估并选定最契合自身的执业阵地
    As a recently graduated support worker, you must weigh multiple factors when selecting a workplace:
    • Does the agency's philosophy of care (holistic, palliative, rehabilitative) align with your personal values?
    • Can you reliably travel to the location, especially during severe Canadian winter conditions?
    • Does the employer provide a clear job description, formal orientation, and access to a supervising nurse?
    • What other clinical and personal elements are crucial when deciding between home care, long-term care, and hospital employment?
    作为一名即将步入职场的专业支持工作者毕业生，在挑选意向执业机构时必须系统审视以下核心要素：
    • 该机构的照护核心哲学（如全人关怀、安宁疗护、强化自立康复）是否与你内心的崇高价值观高度同频？
    • 在加拿大漫长风雪交加的极端极寒严冬中，你是否具备风雨无阻安全准时抵达执业现场的可靠交通出行能力？
    • 该用人单位是否能提供严谨详尽的岗位职责说明书、完备系统的岗前入职带教培训，以及随时能够联络求助的带教督导护士？
    • 在权衡社区居家、长期照护养老院与急症医院时，还有哪些至关重要的个人体魄与生活规划考量？

    Answers to these questions are at the bottom of page 47. Circle the BEST answer. Questions 1 through 6 evaluate understanding of community trends, home care classification, acute settings, subacute facilities, respite goals, and live-in housing.

    本章复习自测题的官方标准答案刊印于原教材第 47 页底部。第 1 至第 6 题系统考核社区医疗发展潮流、居家照护归属属性、急症与亚急性照护场所界定、暂托喘息服务核心功能以及集中式居住照护设施的准确判别。

    p. 47

    Review questions 7 through 9 assess the learner's comprehension of retirement home resident profiles, 24-hour nursing care requirements in long-term care facilities, and the vital ethical significance of maintaining a homelike atmosphere.

    教材原版第 47 页涵盖核心自测题第 7 题至第 9 题，深入考核学习者对退休自理公寓入住群体健康特征、长期照护养老院（LTC）24 小时护士特护刚性需求、以及为余生常住长者精心营造如家般温馨生活氛围（Homelike Atmosphere）崇高意义的深刻领会。

    原版 9 道标准自测题（Pages 46–47，涵盖加拿大医疗向社区居家照护倾斜战略大趋势、居家照护归属属性、综合医院急症照护定位、长期照护院舍亚急性/复杂延续特护、暂托喘息服务核心宗旨、集中式常住居住设施 Live-in Facilities 界定、退休自理公寓入住群体健康特征、长期照护养老院 24 小时护士特护刚性需求及温馨如家环境氛围 Homelike Atmosphere 崇高意义）。选项设置双向兼容类名 quiz-opt eq-opt，点击选项即时验证正误，并附教材第 47 页官方权威标准答案及临床深度精解。

    QUESTION 01 待作答
    A current trend in the Canadian health care system is to:
    当前加拿大医疗卫生保健体系最鲜明的发展趋势是：
    A
    Increase public spending on hospitals
    大幅增加在公立综合急症医院大楼建设上的财政开支
    B
    Decrease spending on community-based services
    持续缩减在社区型卫生照护服务上的公共预算投入
    C
    Focus on providing more community-based services
    将战略发展重心全面聚焦于大力发展并提供更多样化的社区型卫生照护服务
    D
    Promote facility-based services over home care
    大力倡导并优先推广机构型集中照护，以彻底取代居家照护
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: To control escalating hospital costs and meet the preferences of an aging population, Canadian health policy is shifting focus toward providing more community-based and home-based services (p. 36, 46).
    临床解析： 教材全篇与第 46 页核心要点反复强调：为了有效遏制急症医院高昂的床位运营开支并迎合长者居家养老的心愿，加拿大各级政府正坚定不移地将公共政策与财政资源战略倾斜于**社区型医疗服务与居家照护（Community-based services & Home care）**。选项 A、B、D 均与当前国家医疗改革的大方向背道而驰。因此选项 C 正确。
    QUESTION 02 待作答
    Home care is an example of:
    居家照护（Home Care）属于下列哪一种医疗卫生服务形态的典型范例？
    A
    A community-based service
    社区型卫生服务（A community-based service）
    B
    A facility-based service
    机构型集中式照护服务（A facility-based service）
    C
    A community day program
    社区日间文娱日托计划（A community day program）
    D
    End-of-life care
    专科临终关怀唯一形式（End-of-life care）
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    Clinical Rationale: Home care is provided directly in clients' personal residences within the community, making it the archetypal community-based service (p. 37, 46).
    临床解析： 居家照护直接在案主私人家庭住宅中提供上门支持，是**“社区型照护服务”（Community-based service）**中最核心、最具代表性的中流砥柱（第 37 页、第 46 页）。虽然居家照护亦涵盖临终舒缓支持，但其本身所属的大类是社区服务体系。因此选项 A 正确。
    QUESTION 03 待作答
    Which work setting provides acute care?
    下列哪一类工作场所专门提供高精尖的“急性医疗照护”（Acute Care）？
    A
    Home care
    社区居家照护（Home care）
    B
    Long-term care facilities
    长期照护机构 / 养老院（Long-term care facilities）
    C
    Assisted-living facilities
    辅助生活照护公寓（Assisted-living facilities）
    D
    Hospitals
    急症综合医院（Hospitals）
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Acute care is short-term treatment for severe, sudden, or urgent medical conditions and is provided primarily in hospitals equipped with emergency departments and surgical suites (p. 36, 46).
    临床解析： 急性照护（Acute Care）是指针对突发急危重症、严重创伤或大手术后的短期紧急高阶救治，其标准执业阵地唯有配备完备急诊、ICU、手术室与检验病理科的**急症综合医院（Hospitals）**（第 36 页、第 46 页）。养老院与辅助生活居所仅提供慢病调理与生活照护。因此选项 D 正确。
    QUESTION 04 待作答
    Which work setting may provide subacute care?
    下列哪一类机构场所通常设有专门单元，能够提供“亚急性医疗照护”（Subacute Care / 复杂延续性特护）？
    A
    Retirement homes
    退休自理活力公寓（Retirement homes）
    B
    Long-term care facilities
    具备医疗资质的大型长期照护院舍（Long-term care facilities）
    C
    Group homes
    小型集体家庭公寓（Group homes）
    D
    Hospices
    临终安宁关怀院（Hospices）
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: Subacute care (also known as complex continuing care) is comprehensive inpatient care for clients recovering from severe illness or surgery. In Canada, it is provided in specialized hospital rehabilitation units or complex care units within long-term care facilities (p. 36, 46).
    临床解析： 亚急性照护（Subacute Care / 复杂延续性特护）专为度过急性期但仍需专业复杂伤口造口护理、营养支持或强化物理康复的病患所设立；在加拿大，许多具备较强临床医疗资质的大型**长期照护院舍（Long-term care facilities）**以及大型综合医院的延续照护病区，专门开设有此类亚急性与过渡性病房。因此选项 B 正确。
    QUESTION 05 待作答
    What type of service aims to provide a temporary break to family caregivers?
    哪一种服务形态设立的终极宗旨，在于为常年在家庭中照顾重病家属的“家庭照料者”提供临时的身心解脱与喘息休整？
    A
    Acute care services
    急性医疗救治服务（Acute care services）
    B
    Palliative care
    舒缓疗护（Palliative care）
    C
    Respite services
    暂托喘息服务（Respite services）
    D
    Outpatient services
    门诊日间服务（Outpatient services）
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: Respite care is designed specifically to provide temporary relief and a break for primary family caregivers caring for loved ones with chronic illness, physical disabilities, or dementia (p. 36, 46).
    临床解析： 暂托喘息服务（Respite services）的科学内涵正是“给照料者放个假”：由专业支持工作者接替看护数小时、数天，使长期处于身心极限的家属得以补觉、就医或处理私人事务，有效防范照料者身心崩溃危机（第 36 页、第 46 页）。因此选项 C 正确。
    QUESTION 06 待作答
    Which of the following is an example of a live-in facility?
    下列选项中，哪一项属于为案主提供全天候长期常住食宿与生活照料的“集中式居住型照护设施”（Live-in Facility）？
    A
    Hospital
    急症综合医院（Hospital）
    B
    Methadone clinic
    美沙酮戒毒替代门诊（Methadone clinic）
    C
    Private residence
    私人独栋居所（Private residence）
    D
    Assisted-living facility
    辅助生活照护公寓设施（Assisted-living facility）
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Live-in facilities provide residential accommodation alongside ongoing support services. Assisted-living facilities and long-term care homes are primary examples of live-in facilities (p. 39, 46). Hospitals are acute, short-stay treatment facilities, not permanent residential accommodations.
    临床解析： 集中式居住照护设施（Live-in Facility）是指案主将该机构作为其长期日常生活居所、在其中吃住起居并接受持续照护的场所。**辅助生活公寓（Assisted-living facility）**与长期照护养老院（LTC）皆是标准的 Live-in 设施（第 39 页、第 46 页）。医院病房属于短期急诊救治场所，绝非案主长期生活的常住居所；门诊诊所更属于非居住场所。因此选项 D 正确。
    QUESTION 07 待作答
    Residents in retirement facilities generally include:
    选择入住退休自理活力公寓（Retirement Facilities / Homes）的长者，其身体健康状况通常呈现出何种典型特征？
    A
    People with mental impairment
    患有严重认知精神障碍的人群
    B
    Young adults with physical or other disabilities
    伴有中重度肢体残疾的年轻人
    C
    Frail older persons with multiple health problems
    患有多重严重基础慢病的极度衰弱长者
    D
    Older persons with limited care needs
    仅伴有极少或有限生活照料需求的健康自理型年长者
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Retirement homes cater to older adults who are independently mobile and cognitively intact, needing only limited assistance such as hospitality meals, housekeeping, and social recreational activities (p. 38, 47).
    临床解析： 退休公寓（Retirement Homes）属于自费活力养老社区，入住的长者大多身心自理能力优良，神志清晰，仅需机构提供营养餐饮配餐、文娱休闲和基本的安全巡查，其**生活照料需求极为有限（Older persons with limited care needs）**（第 38 页、第 47 页）。选项 A、B、C 所描述的重度失能或失智病患，必须入住配备 24 小时密集临床特护的长期照护院舍（LTC）。因此选项 D 正确。
    QUESTION 08 待作答
    Residents in long-term care facilities generally require:
    入住在长期照护院舍（Long-Term Care Facilities / 养老院）内的长者，其身体与生活通常必然需要：
    A
    24-hour nursing care and support services
    24 小时全天候无间断的专业护士临床监护与贴身生活照护支持服务
    B
    Supervision and limited support services
    仅需轻微日间看护与极有限的生活支持
    C
    Acute care
    综合医院急危重症手术急性救治（Acute care）
    D
    Housekeeping services, but not meal services
    仅需要室内保洁打扫，而不需要中央送餐就餐服务
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    Clinical Rationale: Long-term care homes are designed for frail individuals with complex, chronic physical or cognitive impairments who require 24-hour skilled nursing supervision and comprehensive ADL support (p. 38, 47).
    临床解析： 原书第 38 页与第 47 页明确界定：能够达到政府公立长期照护机构严苛入住准入门槛的案主，皆是重度失能或失智衰弱群体，**必须由现场常驻的注册专业护士与支持工作者提供 24 小时全天候无死角的临床医疗护理与贴身起居生活支持（24-hour nursing care and support services）**。因此选项 A 正确。
    QUESTION 09 待作答
    In which setting is maintaining a homelike atmosphere especially important?
    在下列哪一类医疗护理执业环境中，尽一切可能消除冰冷医疗感、精心营造并维系“如家般温馨温暖的生活氛围”（Homelike Atmosphere）具有最为神圣和极其特殊的意义？
    A
    Hospital
    急症综合医院病房（Hospital）
    B
    Doctor's office
    专科医生门诊诊所（Doctor's office）
    C
    Community day program
    社区日间活动中心（Community day program）
    D
    Long-term care facility
    长期照护院舍 / 养老机构（Long-term care facility）
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Long-term care homes are permanent residences where frail seniors spend the remainder of their lives. Creating a comfortable, homelike atmosphere that minimizes clinical starkness while respecting privacy and familiarity is paramount (p. 40, 47).
    临床解析： 长期照护院舍（LTC）绝非病患短暂停留数天的冰冷医院，而是长者生命晚期余生常住的“真正的家”！在原书第 40 页与第 47 页中特意强调：护理院在居室布置、餐厅格调上必须全力消除冷酷压抑的医疗感，支持工作者必须以家人般的慈爱温情，**为长者营造温馨、充满烟火气与生活尊严的家园氛围（Homelike atmosphere）**。因此选项 D 正确。

    CHAPTER 4 Ethics

    第 4 章：职业伦理、行为守则与临床困境决断
    LEARNING OBJECTIVES · 执业胜任力标准

    OBJECTIVES

    本章学习与执业考核目标 (7 大核心能力指标)
    After reading this chapter, the learner should be able to do the following:
    完成本章研读后，学习者应当能够达成以下核心专业能力考核目标：
    • • Explain the purpose of a code of ethics.
      阐述医疗照护行业《职业伦理守则》（Code of Ethics）的设立宗旨与规范功能。
    • • Define belief and values.
      准确界定“信念（Belief）”与“价值观（Values）”的科学内涵及其对人类行为的指引作用。
    • • Differentiate between ethics and morals.
      深刻辨析“伦理（Ethics）”与“个人道德（Morals）”的本质分野与相互联系。
    • • Identify the basic principles of health care ethics.
      系统掌握医疗卫生伦理四大根本基石原则（自主权、公平正义、行善慈惠、不伤害）。
    • • Describe how each of the principles applies to support work.
      详尽阐述医疗伦理四大原则在支持工作者日常照料操作中的具体落地场景。
    • • Define the term ethical dilemma.
      科学定义“伦理困境（Ethical Dilemma）”的本质特征（对立道德选择的不可调和冲突）。
    • • Apply the principles to solve ethical dilemmas.
      熟练运用临床伦理决策分析框架，化解日常工作中案主自决权与生命安全之间的两难冲突。
    🌐 Elsevier Evolve 官方教参研习配套资源库： http://evolve.elsevier.com/Canada/Sorrentino/SupportWorker
    p. 49
    GLOSSARY

    KEY TERMS · 本章核心专业术语表

    14 核心词汇
    英文术语 / 国际音标 中文对照 / 出处 教材标准学术释义与职业界定
    autonomy /ɔːˈtɒnəmi/ 自主自决原则 / 自主权 p. 51
    Having the freedom and choice to make decisions that affect one's own life and body, also known as self-determination.
    个体拥有做出影响自身生活、身体与医疗决策的自由意志与自主选择权，亦称“自决权（Self-Determination）”。
    belief /bɪˈliːf/ 信念 p. 49
    A strong conviction that something is true, real, or correct without absolute empirical proof.
    个体内心深处坚信某事为真实、正确或存在的坚定心理信念与信仰认知。
    beneficence /bɪˈnɛfɪsəns/ 慈惠行善原则 / 利他原则 p. 52
    The ethical duty of doing or promoting good, actively enhancing the well-being and best interests of the client.
    主动为他人谋求福祉、行善利他并促进案主身心健康的道德义务，全力维护服务对象的最高利益。
    code of ethics /koʊd əv ˈɛθɪks/ 职业伦理守则 / 行为准则 p. 49
    A formal statement of the values, ethical principles, and professional ideals that guide employee conduct and relationships.
    由行业公会或雇主机构正式发布的、指导员工执业行为、人际关系及职业理想的核心价值观与道德规范总纲。
    conduct /ˈkɒndʌkt/ 个人行为操守 p. 49
    Personal behaviour and actions in professional and everyday life.
    个体在职业执业过程及日常生活中的言行举止、作风表现与道德操守。
    ethical dilemma /ˈɛθɪkəl dɪˈlɛmə/ 伦理两难困境 p. 50
    An apparent conflict between opposing moral choices where choosing one path inevitably results in violating another ethical duty.
    在两个相互对立的道德选择之间出现的尖锐冲突情境：选择其中一条路径必然会导致背离另一项崇高的道德义务。
    ethics /ˈɛθɪks/ 伦理学 / 伦理准则 p. 49
    The rules, standards, and values that guide human conduct when differentiating between right and wrong, good and bad.
    指引人类社会行为举止、并在是非曲直（Right vs Wrong）与善恶美丑之间做出审慎鉴别的原则、规范与价值体系。
    health care ethics /hɛlθ ker ˈɛθɪks/ 医疗卫生伦理学 p. 50
    The philosophical and clinical study of what is morally right and wrong when planning, delivering, and evaluating healthcare services.
    在规划、提供和评估医疗照护服务全过程中，系统研究医疗决策与执业行为是非善恶的哲学与应用科学。
    justice /ˈdʒʌstɪs/ 公平正义原则 p. 51
    The ethical principle that all people should be treated in an equal, fair, and impartial manner regardless of personal traits.
    确保所有人均享有平等、公正、不偏不倚待遇的伦理原则，坚决杜绝因种族、年龄、疾病晚期或脾气性格而歧视任何案主。
    morals /ˈmɒrəlz/ 个人道德观 / 道德信念 p. 49
    Fundamental principles of behaviour that an individual believes to be right or wrong for themselves, guided by personal conscience.
    个体基于个人良知、家庭教养与生活经历，在内心深处坚信对自己而言何为正确或错误的根本行为操守准则。
    nonmaleficence /ˌnɒn-məˈlɛfɪsəns/ 不伤害原则 / 无害原则 p. 55
    The foundational ethical duty to do no harm, seeking to avoid intentional, negligent, or accidental injury to the client.
    医疗与护理体系中最神圣的基础红线原则：誓死追求“绝不造成伤害”，全力防范蓄意伤害、过失疏忽或意外跌倒创伤。
    self-determination /ˌsɛlf dɪˌtɜːrmɪˈneɪʃən/ 自决主权 p. 51
    The right and freedom of an individual to direct their own life, make personal choices, and govern their own destiny.
    个体掌控自身命运、主导自身日常生活细节、并享有不被外人强制干涉个人决定的神圣自主权利。
    unethical /ʌnˈɛθɪkəl/ 不道德的 / 违背伦理准则的 p. 49
    Not conforming to approved standards of social morality or established professional codes of conduct.
    偏离公认社会道德标准、背离行业职业道德准则或做出侵犯案主合法权益的违纪失德行为。
    values /ˈvæljuːz/ 价值观 p. 49
    Qualities, ideals, and standards that an individual considers worthwhile, desirable, and meaningful in life.
    个体在内心深处视作至关重要、值得毕生追求且极具崇高价值的品质、理想与人生追求标准。

    The ethical principle that all people should be treated in an equal, fair, and impartial manner regardless of personal traits.

    确保所有人均享有平等、公正、不偏不倚待遇的伦理原则，坚决杜绝因种族、年龄、疾病晚期或脾气性格而歧视任何案主。

    morals p. 49
    /ˈmɒrəlz/
    个人道德观 / 道德信念

    Fundamental principles of behaviour that an individual believes to be right or wrong for themselves, guided by personal conscience.

    个体基于个人良知、家庭教养与生活经历，在内心深处坚信对自己而言何为正确或错误的根本行为操守准则。

    nonmaleficence p. 55
    /ˌnɒn-məˈlɛfɪsəns/
    不伤害原则 / 无害原则

    The foundational ethical duty to do no harm, seeking to avoid intentional, negligent, or accidental injury to the client.

    医疗与护理体系中最神圣的基础红线原则：誓死追求“绝不造成伤害”，全力防范蓄意伤害、过失疏忽或意外跌倒创伤。

    self-determination p. 51
    /ˌsɛlf dɪˌtɜːrmɪˈneɪʃən/
    自决主权

    The right and freedom of an individual to direct their own life, make personal choices, and govern their own destiny.

    个体掌控自身命运、主导自身日常生活细节、并享有不被外人强制干涉个人决定的神圣自主权利。

    unethical p. 49
    /ʌnˈɛθɪkəl/
    不道德的 / 违背伦理准则的

    Not conforming to approved standards of social morality or established professional codes of conduct.

    偏离公认社会道德标准、背离行业职业道德准则或做出侵犯案主合法权益的违纪失德行为。

    values p. 49
    /ˈvæljuːz/
    价值观

    Qualities, ideals, and standards that an individual considers worthwhile, desirable, and meaningful in life.

    个体在内心深处视作至关重要、值得毕生追求且极具崇高价值的品质、理想与人生追求标准。

    ETHICS, MORALS, VALUES, AND BELIEFS

    伦理、道德、价值观与信念的科学辨析

    The term ethics refers to the rules of conduct that guide us when deciding what is right and what is wrong, and what is good and what is bad. These rules come from society's expectations of how people should conduct themselves. In contrast, morals are the fundamental principles of behaviour each person believes to be right or wrong for themselves, guided by personal conscience without strict regard to legalities or customs.

    “伦理”（Ethics）是指指引我们在面对具体情境时甄别是非曲直（Right vs Wrong）以及善恶美丑的行为规范与价值准绳。这些规范源自整个人类社会对个体应当如何行事操守的共同期待。相比之下，“个人道德”（Morals）是指个体基于个人良知、在内心深处坚信对自己而言何为对、何为错的根本行为信念，它独立于具体的成文法律或民俗约定。

    Values are what an individual considers to be worthwhile, desirable, and meaningful qualities in a person (such as honesty, compassion, loyalty, and fairness). A belief is a conviction that something is true, often rooted in faith, cultural upbringing, or lived experience. Ethics, morals, values, and beliefs continuously interact to guide professional and personal decision-making.

    “价值观”（Values）是个体在内心深处视作至关重要、极具价值且值得毕生追求的人格品质与生活理想（如诚实守信、仁爱同理、忠诚尽责与公平公正）。“信念”（Belief）则是指个体对某种理念或事态为真实、存在的坚定认同，它往往深植于宗教信仰、文化熏陶或生活磨砺之中。伦理、道德、价值观与信念四者紧密交织，共同构筑了指引我们职业行为与临床决断的心灵罗盘。

    p. 50

    THE INFLUENCE OF CULTURE ON BELIEFS, VALUES, MORALS, AND ETHICS

    多元文化、历史创伤对伦理道德观念的深远塑造

    Support workers must recognize that culture, religion, historical trauma, and personal lived experiences profoundly shape what a client considers acceptable, ethical, or honourable. Actions that seem obvious to a healthcare worker may conflict with a client's core cultural morals.

    支持工作者必须清醒地认识到：文化传统、宗教教义、历史创伤以及案主过往的人生磨难，深刻塑造了当事人对何为得体、何为道德、何为尊严的认知。在医护从业者看来理所当然的常规医疗操作，在某些案主独特的文化道德世界中可能会引发强烈的心理冲突。

    CASE STUDY: Supporting Mr. Medvjed: How Past Experiences Affect Beliefs

    专栏案例研讨：支持梅德维杰德先生 —— 过往创伤如何深刻改变案主信念
    SCENARIO:
    Mr. Medvjed, age 86, is a resident in a long-term care facility. He fled war-torn Eastern Europe as a young man after enduring traumatic military interrogation and persecution. He hoards food beneath his mattress, becomes agitated when staff wear uniforms, and adamantly refuses to shower when bathroom doors are locked.

    CLINICAL REFLECTION:
    Mr. Medvjed's behaviour is not 'stubbornness' or 'deliberate non-compliance'; it is an adaptive survival response rooted in severe trauma. Forcing him into locked showers or confiscating his hoarded bread revictimizes him. A compassionate support worker accommodates his trauma: leaving bathroom doors unlocked, wearing non-clinical scrub patterns, and validating his need for food security.
    实战情境：
    梅德维杰德先生（Mr. Medvjed），86 岁，居住在长期照护院舍中。年轻时为了逃离战乱的东欧，他曾遭受过残酷的军事严刑拷打与政治迫害。在院舍生活中，他经常把未吃完的面包偷偷藏在床垫底下，一见到身穿白大褂或制服的员工就会神色恐慌，且一旦洗澡时关闭上锁浴室房门，他便会极度惊恐躁动、坚决抗拒洗澡。

    临床深度反思：
    梅德维杰德先生的行为绝非“固执任性”或“故意抗拒”，而是战后严重创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）深植于骨髓的生存防御机制！如果强行将其锁入浴室冲澡或粗暴没收其私藏的面包，将是对长者心灵的二次残酷伤害。富有同理心的支持工作者应当尊重其创伤背景：洗澡时虚掩房门消除其幽闭恐慌、改穿柔和的彩色便服工作服，并温和理解长者对食物安全的极度渴望。

    CODES OF ETHICS

    医疗卫生行业的职业伦理守则

    Regulated healthcare professionals (such as physicians and nurses) are legally bound by formal codes of ethics published by their respective governing colleges. Support workers do not currently have a single provincial statutory college code; instead, each employer, health authority, or home care agency publishes an agency code of ethics outlining the fundamental values and standards of conduct expected of support workers.

    受法律监管的医护人员（如注册护士与执业医师）受到各自法定专业监管学院发布的行业职业伦理守则的严格法律约束。支持工作者目前尚未通过省立法设立统属的专业监管学院；但各用人机构、卫生局或居家派遣中介均会制定并公布本单位的《员工职业伦理行为守则》，明确界定支持工作者必须誓死恪守的人本照护价值观与职业操守底线。

    p. 51

    THE FOUR PRINCIPLES OF HEALTH CARE ETHICS

    医疗卫生伦理四大根本基石原则

    1. The Principle of Autonomy (Self-Determination)

    第一基石：自主自决原则（Autonomy / Self-Determination）

    Autonomy—also referred to as self-determination—is the fundamental right of a mentally competent individual to make their own choices and decisions about their own body, life, and healthcare. Autonomy affirms that a person does not lose their civil rights simply because they become ill, frail, or enter a healthcare facility.

    “自主自决原则”（Autonomy，亦称自决权 Self-Determination）是指具有完全民事与知情同意心智能力的个体，拥有自主做出影响自身身体、生活方式以及医疗干预决策的神圣法定权利。自主权明确宣示：一个人绝不会仅仅因为生病衰老、失能或住进了医疗机构，就丧失了作为独立公民的基本人权！

    In support work, autonomy requires honouring the client's preferences: asking what clothes they wish to wear, respecting their meal choices, and honouring their chosen daily routines. Crucially, autonomy includes the legal right to refuse medical care, assistance, or medications. If a competent client refuses a bath or assistance, the support worker must respect the refusal, never use coercion or force, explain the risks gently, and report the refusal immediately to the supervising nurse.

    在日常支持工作中，践行自主权要求我们必须无条件尊重案主的个性化选择：主动征询其喜欢穿哪套衣服、尊重其饮食偏好、顺应其作息节奏。更关键的是，自主权赋予了案主合法拒绝医疗处置、拒绝翻身或拒绝服药的神圣法定权利！倘若一位神志清晰的案主坚决拒绝洗澡或拒绝护工搀扶，支持工作者必须坚决尊重其拒绝意愿，严禁使用任何形式的语言恐吓或肉体强迫，在耐心地用通俗语言告知潜在风险后，第一时间如实向主管护士汇报记录。

    p. 52

    2. The Principle of Justice

    第二基石：公平正义原则（Justice）

    The principle of justice means that all people should be treated in an equal, fair, and impartial manner. Healthcare resources, attention, and compassion must be distributed equitably according to need, without discrimination based on age, race, gender, religion, socioeconomic status, diagnosis, or temperament.

    “公平正义原则”（Justice）是指所有受助个体均应当获得完全平等、公允且不偏不倚的对待与关照。医疗资源分配、护工的时间精力与同理心关怀，必须严格依据案主的实际照护需求进行公允分配，坚决杜绝因年龄老幼、种族肤色、性别取向、宗教信仰、贫富差距、病情轻重或脾气性格好坏而产生任何偏袒、冷落或歧视。

    Support workers demonstrate justice by ensuring they do not spend excessive time with a pleasant, communicative resident while neglecting a withdrawn, agitated, or demanding resident. Every individual under your care deserves identical respect, thoroughness, and meticulous attention.

    支持工作者在临床中体现正义原则的生动实践是：绝不能因为某位长者性格风趣和善、逢人便夸就整天泡在其房间聊天，而对隔壁性格孤僻沉闷、情绪暴躁或频繁拉铃的老人避之不及甚至消极怠工。在你负责轮班的每一个病榻前，每一位长者都享有获得同等细致、耐心与精湛照护的神圣正义权利。

    3. The Principle of Beneficence

    第三基石：慈惠行善原则（Beneficence）

    The principle of beneficence means doing or promoting good. It requires healthcare providers to actively contribute to the client's health, safety, comfort, and well-being, striving to maximize clinical benefits in all interventions. Beneficence is not passive; it demands proactive kindness, empathy, and advocacy.

    “慈惠行善原则”（Beneficence）是指积极主动地为案主行善利他并谋求福祉。它要求医护从业者必须主动采取建设性的积极行动，全力促进服务对象的身心健康、人身安全、机体舒适与心灵愉悦，在每一次临床照料中力求使案主的获益最大化。行善绝非消极等待，它要求从业者倾注主动的关爱、真挚的同理心与敢于为弱者发声的执业担当。

    p. 53

    4. The Principle of Nonmaleficence

    第四基石：不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence / Primum Non Nocere）

    The principle of nonmaleficence is the foundational duty to do no harm (derived from the ancient medical maxim primum non nocere). It requires healthcare workers to intentionally refrain from inflicting harm, to prevent harm whenever possible, and to eliminate existing risks of harm to clients.

    “不伤害原则”（Nonmaleficence，源自古希腊希波克拉底医学名言“首先做到不伤害 Primum Non Nocere”）是整个医疗与护理伦理中最神圣、不可动摇的底线红线。它以法律铁律要求医护从业者：坚决蓄意不施加任何肉体或心理创伤、在任何可能的情境下竭力防范伤害的发生，并不遗余力地清除任何威胁案主安危的环境隐患。

    In support work, nonmaleficence means rigorously following infection control protocols to prevent outbreaks, using transfer equipment correctly to avoid fractures or drops, testing bathwater temperatures before immersion to prevent third-degree scalds, locking wheelchair brakes, and reporting suspected physical, emotional, sexual, or financial abuse or neglect immediately.

    在日常支持工作中，践行不伤害原则绝非空洞口号，它具体落地在极其严苛的操作规范中：洗手消毒防范院内超级细菌交叉感染、规范操作机械移位机杜绝长者坠床骨折、下水前必用手腕内侧测水温严防三度严重烫伤、轮椅停稳必锁死脚刹防溜车，以及一旦在案主身上发现可疑淤青擦伤或察觉虐待遗弃前兆，必须依法立即向上级护士进行紧急书面与口头双重汇报！

    p. 54

    ETHICAL DILEMMAS AND CONFLICTS OF INTEREST

    临床伦理两难困境与利益冲突的坚决防范

    An ethical dilemma is an apparent conflict between opposing moral choices where choosing one moral obligation inevitably leads to violating another. In healthcare, ethical dilemmas rarely present a clear choice between 'good' and 'bad'; rather, they involve excruciating tensions between two competing 'goods' or choosing the lesser of two unavoidable evils.

    “伦理两难困境”（Ethical Dilemma）是指在两个相互对立的崇高道德选择之间出现的尖锐冲突情境：选择履行其中一项道德职责，必然会在客观上导致背离另一项同样重要的道德义务。在复杂的医疗实践中，伦理两难极少呈现为非黑即白的“善与恶”对决，而往往是两个同样崇高的“善”之间的殊死博弈，或在两个无法避免的痛苦选择中艰难权衡并抉择“两害相权取其轻”。

    Avoiding Conflict of Interest

    坚决杜绝个人利益冲突（Conflict of Interest）

    Support workers must maintain absolute impartiality and professional boundaries. A conflict of interest occurs when a worker's personal, financial, or familial interests clash with the professional duty owed to the client.

    支持工作者必须时刻保持高度的职业纯洁性与严密的职业边界。当从业者个人的私利、财务状况或亲友利益与其对服务对象承担的崇高照护职责发生对立冲突时，即构成了极其严重的“利益冲突”（Conflict of Interest）。

    Support workers must never accept personal loans, gifts of substantial value, tips, bequests in a client's will, or sell products to clients. Any decision regarding a client's care must be made strictly for the client's benefit, never for the worker's personal advantage.

    支持工作者誓死严禁向案主借款、索取收受小费、接受贵重礼物、诱导长者在遗嘱中添加遗产赠予，或在工作场所推销个人微商副业。针对案主照护所做出的每一个临床决定，必须百分之百纯粹为了案主的最高福祉，绝不容许掺杂任何从业人员的私人私利算计！

    p. 55

    CASE STUDY: AUTONOMY VERSUS NONMALEFICENCE

    实战案例深研：当“案主自主自决权”激烈碰撞“防跌倒人身安全”

    CASE STUDY: Mr. Ferguson's Refusal of a Walker

    专栏实战案例：弗格森先生坚决拒绝使用四脚助行器
    THE CLINICAL SITUATION:
    Mr. Ferguson, age 79, lives in an assisted-living facility. He has Parkinson's disease with severe gait freezing and postural instability. Following two recent falls that caused scalp lacerations, the physiotherapist and nursing team assessed that he urgently requires a four-wheeled walker with handbrakes to ambulate safely.

    However, Mr. Ferguson fiercely refuses to use the walker, stating: 'I am not an invalid! Walkers are for old, decrepit people. I will walk with my wooden cane or not at all.' He attempts to walk unassisted to meals, stumbling repeatedly.

    THE ETHICAL DILEMMA:
    • On one hand, the principle of AUTONOMY dictates that Mr. Ferguson is mentally competent and has the sovereign legal right to make his own mobility choices and refuse assistive devices.
    • On the other hand, the principle of NONMALEFICENCE obligates the care team to protect him from foreseeable catastrophic harm (a fatal hip fracture, intracranial hemorrhage).

    THE RESOLUTION:
    Staff do not 'force' or physically restrain Mr. Ferguson (which would be illegal assault). Instead, the care team arranges an interprofessional family conference. The team validates his feelings about aging, explores stylish walking poles or low-profile rollators, pairs him with a support worker for standby assistance during peak dining hours, and establishes a dignity-preserving compromise.
    临床真实情境：
    弗格森先生（Mr. Ferguson），79 岁，居住在辅助生活照护公寓中。他患有进行性帕金森病，伴有严重的步态冻结与姿势平衡反射丧失。在最近连续发生两次导致头皮裂伤缝针的跌倒摔伤后，物理治疗师与责任护士经严格评估下达医嘱：他必须全程使用配备手刹的四轮助行车（Walker）方可下地活动。

    然而，神志清晰的弗格森先生坚决抗拒使用助行车，愤怒抗议道：“我绝不是残废！那玩意儿是给快断气的废人用的。我要么拄我的木拐杖走，要么就不出门！”他固执地拒绝推助行车，摇摇晃晃踉跄走去餐厅就餐，途中险象环生。

    尖锐的伦理两难冲突：
    • 一方面，自主自决原则（AUTONOMY）要求必须尊重弗格森先生作为完全民事能力人的意愿与主权，他有权拒绝使用其痛恨的辅助器具；
    • 另一方面，不伤害原则（NONMALEFICENCE）以生命至上原则要求医护团队必须履行防范其再次遭受灾难性髋关节骨折或颅内出血致命伤害的崇高职责。

    科学卓越的临床化解路径：
    团队绝不采取粗暴抢夺拐杖或身体约束硬推的违法侵权暴行；而是召开由案主、家属、主管护士与治疗师共同参加的三方伦理座谈会。团队充分倾听长者对衰老抗拒的心声，为其量身推荐更为轻巧美观的登山式平衡杖，并在用餐高峰期专门安排支持工作者贴身伴随步行保护，最终达成了既充分捍卫长者自尊、又确保绝对防摔安全的双赢折中方案。
    p. 56

    A FOUR-STEP FRAMEWORK FOR RESOLVING ETHICAL DILEMMAS

    解决临床伦理两难困境的四步科学决断框架

    When confronted with complex ethical tensions, support workers should never act impulsively or make solitary decisions. They must follow a structured, collaborative four-step decision-making model:

    当在病榻旁面临复杂的伦理道德冲突时，支持工作者绝不能凭一时冲动草率行事，更绝不能单枪匹马擅自做出武断决断。从业者必须严格遵照以下结构化、团队协作的四步决策科学模型：

    • • Step 1: Identify the Ethical Issue and Competing Principles. Clearly articulate what the ethical conflict is. Which fundamental principles (Autonomy vs Nonmaleficence, Justice vs Beneficence) are in direct tension?
      第一步：精准辨识核心伦理问题与对立原则。清晰透彻地界定伦理冲突的症结所在：究竟是哪两项根本原则（如“案主自主权”与“不伤害人身安全”、“公平正义”与“利他行善”）发生了激烈碰撞？
    • • Step 2: Gather Comprehensive Information and Perspectives. Collect all relevant medical facts, cognitive assessments, cultural beliefs, family viewpoints, and agency policies. Listen deeply to the client's own stated fears and desires.
      第二步：全面收集各方临床事实与多重视角。详尽梳理案主的病史诊断、认知能力评估报告、宗教文化禁忌、家属核心诉求以及机构法定管理规章，以极大的同理心深度倾听案主本人的内心真实渴望与恐惧。
    • • Step 3: Consider All Possible Options and Weigh Ethical Consequences. Brainstorm creative alternative compromises. Evaluate each option through the lens of the DIPPS model. What are the short-term and long-term harms and benefits of each choice?
      第三步：全面头脑风暴构思所有备选方案并权衡伦理后果。基于 DIPPS 人本照护模型系统审视每个折中方案：哪种选择能够将对案主尊严与自主权的损害降到最低？哪种选择能够最大限度保障其人身生命安全？
    • • Step 4: Decide on the Best Action, Implement Collaboratively, and Evaluate Outcome. Select the most ethical, compassionate course in concert with the supervising nurse and team. Document objectively, monitor results, and reassess as needs change.
      第四步：审慎确定最佳行动路径、团队协同执行并严密追踪评估成效。在责任主管护士与跨学科团队指导下选定最具人文同理心的处置方案。在病历中做出客观详尽记录，持续观察长者反馈并动态调整。

    Seeking Professional Support

    构建强大的职业伦理支持后盾

    Remember: Support workers are never expected to resolve complex ethical or legal dilemmas in isolation. Always consult your supervising nurse, social worker, or your facility's clinical ethics committee. Open interprofessional dialogue protects both the client and the worker.

    请时刻牢记：支持工作者绝非独行侠，没有任何人要求你孤军奋战独自承担复杂的法律与伦理重担！在遇到两难抉择时，必须第一时间向你的主管护士、责任组长、社会工作者或医院的临床医学伦理委员会（Ethics Committee）请示咨询。开放透明的跨学科专业探讨，是筑牢案主生命尊严与从业者执业安全的双重铠甲！

    p. 57

    CHAPTER REVIEW

    本章复习与临床思维修炼

    KEY POINTS

    全章核心知识要点精要清单
    • • Ethics refers to rules or values guiding right from wrong and good from bad, based on societal expectations.
      伦理是指基于人类社会共同期许、指引我们在日常行为中甄别是非曲直与善恶美丑的行为规范与价值体系。
    • • Morals are fundamental principles of behaviour an individual believes to be right or wrong for themselves, guided by personal conscience.
      个人道德是指个体基于自身良知在内心深处坚信对自己而言何为对错的根本准则，不受制于外部成文法律或世俗习俗。
    • • Values are qualities considered worthwhile in a person; beliefs are convictions that something is true.
      价值观是个体视作具有崇高价值的人格品质；信念则是个体内心深处坚信某事为真实存在的心理信仰。
    • • Culture, religion, and lived trauma influence ethical beliefs, morals, and values, which in turn drive personal actions.
      文化传统、宗教信仰及过往人生创伤深刻塑造了伦理信念与道德观，并最终主导着个体的实际行为取向。
    • • The principle of justice means all people should be treated in a fair, equal, and impartial manner.
      公平正义原则要求必须以完全公允、平等且不偏不倚的崇高态度对待每一个受助生命，杜绝偏袒与歧视。
    • • The principle of autonomy means having the freedom and sovereign right to make choices and direct one's own care.
      自主自决原则是指神志清晰的案主享有做出自主选择、主导自身日常生活并合法拒绝医疗处置的神圣自决主权。
    • • The principle of beneficence means actively doing or promoting good, maximizing well-being and positive outcomes.
      慈惠行善原则是指积极主动地为案主谋求福祉、行善利他并全面促进其身心健康的道德作为。
    • • The principle of nonmaleficence is the foundational duty to do no harm, preventing injury and removing hazards.
      不伤害原则是誓死追求“绝不造成伤害”的不可动摇底线，全力防范蓄意伤害、过失疏忽或意外跌倒创伤。
    • • An ethical dilemma is an apparent conflict between opposing moral choices; solving it requires considering the four principles, gathering facts, and consulting the team.
      伦理两难困境是对立道德职责之间的尖锐冲突；化解它必须熟练运用四大伦理基石、全面倾听各方心声并依靠团队协作。
    • • Support workers must strictly avoid conflicts of interest, refusing gifts, loans, or personal ventures that exploit the therapeutic relationship.
      从业者必须坚决防范个人利益冲突，誓死拒收昂贵礼物、借款小费，绝不利用照护关系谋求任何私人私利。

    CRITICAL THINKING IN PRACTICE

    临床实践中的批判性思维修炼

    CRITICAL THINKING: The Family Demanding Force-Feeding

    实战情境思维修炼：家属极度恐慌要求“强行将饭菜硬灌进嘴里”的伦理应对
    THE CLINICAL SCENARIO:
    You are assisting Mr. Zhang, age 82, in a long-term care facility with his evening meal. Mr. Zhang is cognitively intact but frail and terminal; he calmly shakes his head and refuses to eat after three spoonfuls. His wife, who is deeply distressed about his progressive weight loss and terrified of losing him, grabs your arm and demands: 'Force the food into him! Shove it in his mouth! He will starve to death if you don't!'

    CRITICAL THINKING QUESTIONS:
    1. Does Mr. Zhang have the legal and ethical right to refuse to eat? (Autonomy)
    2. Does Mrs. Zhang have the legal right to demand that her husband be force-fed? (Substituted judgment limits)
    3. What are the severe physical and legal dangers of attempting to force food into a resistant elder? (Nonmaleficence, aspiration pneumonia, choking, battery)
    4. What is your immediate response to Mrs. Zhang with empathy and compassion? Who do you report to immediately?
    实战临床情境：
    你正在长期照护养老院内协助 82 岁的张老先生进食晚餐。张老先生神志完全清晰但处于肿瘤晚期极度衰竭；在勉强咽下三口粥后，他平静地摇了摇头，闭口坚决拒绝再进食。其守候在病榻旁的妻子见状情绪失控、极度恐慌于丈夫体重骤降与死亡逼近，一把抓住你的手臂厉声哭求道：“给我硬把饭灌进去！强行撬开他的嘴往里塞！你们不灌他就会活活饿死的！”

    批判性思维修炼核心命题：
    1. 神志清醒的张老先生是否拥有拒绝继续进食的神圣法律与伦理权利？（自主权 Autonomy 的神圣性）
    2. 张太太作为家属，是否有权强令医护人员对其配偶实施强迫性硬塞喂食？（家属意志绝不能凌驾于具有心智能力当事人的明示拒绝之上）
    3. 倘若照护者屈从家属压力试图强行撬嘴灌食，将面临何种可怕的身体与法律灾难？（不仅构成违法的身体侵害 Battery，更极易导致致命的食物误吸入气道、窒息或严重吸入性肺炎瞬间毙命！）
    4. 你应当如何以充满慈爱同理的心情安抚极度悲恸的张太太，并将这一情况以何种规范流程向责任主管护士汇报？

    Answers to these questions are at the bottom of page 58. Questions 1 through 5 are True/False questions testing the scope, function, and principles of ethics. Questions 6 through 10 test application of autonomy, justice, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and identifying conflicts of interest.

    本章复习自测题的标准官方答案刊印于原教材第 58 页底部。第 1 至第 5 题为正误判断题，检验伦理守则的适用场景与功能边界；第 6 至第 10 题深入考核四大伦理基石原则的场景对应与利益冲突辨识。

    p. 58

    Review question 11 evaluates the support worker's clinical and ethical competence when facing a real-world dilemma: balancing a resident's right to refuse painful mechanical chair transfers against the prevention of severe pressure ulcers, highlighting the necessity of multidisciplinary communication and compromise.

    教材原版第 58 页核心考核自测题第 11 题，全面检验学习者在面对极端现实伦理两难时的综合决断力：如何在长者抗拒搬运剧痛拒绝离床的自主权、与主管护士防范褥疮压疮恶化的不伤害原则之间寻觅最佳平衡，深刻彰显了搭建跨学科沟通桥梁与探寻人性化双赢折中方案的卓越职业智慧。

    Chapter 4 Self-Test & Review Questions · Pages 57–58 11 Authentic Clinical Questions
    KNOWLEDGE CHECK · INTERACTIVE PRACTICE

    第 4 章全真自测复习题与详尽职业精解

    原版 11 道标准自测题（Pages 57–58，涵盖日常照护伦理普遍适用性、职业伦理守则指导功能与边界、伦理科学定义、隐私保密神圣伦理属性、不伤害与合乎伦理之辩析、安全环境与不伤害原则 Nonmaleficence、尊严维护与利他行善 Beneficence、一视同仁与公平正义 Justice、尊重个性偏好与自主自决 Autonomy、决策中最忌讳的自私利益冲突以及压疮长者抗拒移位伦理两难的跨学科三方沟通折中解决路径）。选项设置双向兼容类名 quiz-opt eq-opt，点击选项即时验证正误，并附教材第 58 页官方权威标准答案及临床深度精解。

    QUESTION 01 待作答
    T / F: Ethics apply only to life-and-death situations.
    判断正误（T / F）：职业道德与伦理准则，仅仅适用于涉及生死攸关的极端抢救生命紧急情境中。
    T
    True
    正确
    F
    False
    错误
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: Ethics apply to everyday situations—from knocking before entering a room and preserving modesty to respecting food preferences—not just extreme life-and-death dilemmas (p. 49, 57).
    临床解析： 伦理准则绝非仅仅在 ICU 拔管或临终绝症抢救时才派上用场。在支持工作者的日常执业中，从每一次进门前敲门礼貌问候（维护尊严）、协助洗澡保护被单隐私（维护隐私）、遵照长者意愿选择衣服搭配（尊重自主）、到严格换水防烫伤（不伤害），职业伦理如影随形渗透在日常照料每一个看似平凡的微小细节之中（第 49 页、第 57 页）。因此答案为 F。
    QUESTION 02 待作答
    T / F: Codes of ethics provide rules and answers to ethical dilemmas.
    判断正误（T / F）：行业职业伦理守则（Code of Ethics）为医护人员在工作中遭遇的所有伦理道德两难困境，直接提供了现成且绝对唯一的标准答案。
    T
    True
    正确
    F
    False
    错误
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: Codes of ethics provide principles, ideals, and professional guidance, but they cannot provide rigid 'recipes' or definitive automatic answers to every complex, unique ethical dilemma (p. 49, 57).
    临床解析： 职业伦理守则提供的是宏观的“根本指导原则、职业准绳与道德方向标”（Guiding principles and values），但现实世界中的伦理困境极其复杂多变，守则绝不可能变成一本包治百病、自动吐出标准答案的操作手册（第 49 页、第 57 页）。从业者必须运用临床批判性思维，结合特定情境进行深入的个案推演与团队权衡。因此答案为 F。
    QUESTION 03 待作答
    T / F: Ethics are a guide when deciding between right and wrong, and good and bad.
    判断正误（T / F）：伦理准则的核心职能，在于指引我们在纷繁的人类社会行为中甄别是非曲直（Right from Wrong）与善恶美丑（Good from Bad）。
    T
    True
    正确
    F
    False
    错误
    标准权威答案： 选项 T
    Clinical Rationale: Ethics are defined as the fundamental rules of conduct and principles that guide human actions when differentiating between right and wrong, good and bad (p. 49, 57).
    临床解析： 原书第 49 页及第 57 页核心要点第一条开宗明义界定：伦理学（Ethics）的根本科学定义，正是引导我们在面对两难选择时鉴别是非与良善的崇高道德指南针。因此表述完全正确，答案为 T。
    QUESTION 04 待作答
    T / F: Keeping a resident's information confidential is ethical behaviour.
    判断正误（T / F）：时刻将住院院舍长者的身体隐私、既往病史与个人健康资讯严格保密，属于标准的崇高职业伦理行为。
    T
    True
    正确
    F
    False
    错误
    标准权威答案： 选项 T
    Clinical Rationale: Guarding and respecting a client's private personal and health information (confidentiality) is a foundational tenet of professional ethics and legal statutes (p. 49, 57).
    临床解析： 严守信息保密性（Confidentiality）不仅是《个人健康信息保护法》（PHIPA）的法定要求，更是支持工作者职业道德守则（Box 4.1）中誓死履行的崇高伦理义务（第 49 页、第 57 页）。因此答案为 T。
    QUESTION 05 待作答
    T / F: Any decision regarding a client's care is ethical if it does not harm the person.
    判断正误（T / F）：针对服务对象照护所做出的任何决定，只要其在客观上没有对当事人造成身体上的直接肉体伤害，就必然属于合乎伦理道德的正当决定。
    T
    True
    正确
    F
    False
    错误
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: An action that causes no physical harm may still be deeply unethical if it violates autonomy, breaches confidentiality, infantilizes dignity, or acts unjustly (p. 50, 57).
    临床解析： 这一认知极其危险！合乎伦理绝不仅仅局限于“没有直接打伤或摔伤病患”（不伤害原则只是四大基石之一）。倘若照护者为了省事而剥夺长者自主选择衣服的权利（严重侵犯自主权）、或像训斥婴儿般侮辱长者（严重侵犯人格尊严）、或在病患背后四处散播其私密八卦（严重侵犯隐私保密），虽然没有造成任何物理肉体创伤，但属于极其严重的不道德失德行径（第 50 页、第 57 页）。因此答案为 F。
    QUESTION 06 待作答
    Providing a safe environment is an example of:
    在日常照护中时刻保持地面干燥防滑、清除过道杂物电线、按规使用床挡防护以提供绝对安全无险的居住环境，是践行下列哪一项伦理原则的典范？
    A
    Autonomy
    自主自决原则（Autonomy）
    B
    Justice
    公平正义原则（Justice）
    C
    Beneficence
    慈惠行善原则（Beneficence）
    D
    Nonmaleficence
    不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence）
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Nonmaleficence means seeking to do no harm and actively removing environmental hazards that could cause accidental injury, falls, or complications (p. 55, 57).
    临床解析： 不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence）的核心要义是积极消除任何可能对案主造成身体创伤或痛苦的潜在危害。通过保持环境整洁、消除防滑防烫隐患、牢固锁定床刹，正是为了杜绝案主受到意外身体创伤，属于不伤害原则的典型体现（第 55 页、第 57 页）。因此选项 D 正确。
    QUESTION 07 待作答
    Showing respect and protecting a client's dignity is an example of:
    发自内心地展现对长者的崇高敬重、无论其身体残缺衰老与否均全力捍卫其人格尊严，是践行下列哪一项伦理原则的体现？
    A
    Autonomy
    自主自决原则（Autonomy）
    B
    Justice
    公平正义原则（Justice）
    C
    Beneficence
    慈惠行善原则（Beneficence）
    D
    Nonmaleficence
    不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence）
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: Beneficence means doing and promoting good. Actively demonstrating respect, uplifting a resident's emotional spirit, and nurturing their dignity promotes their holistic well-being (p. 52, 57).
    临床解析： 慈惠行善（Beneficence）要求医护人员不仅仅是消极地“不造成伤害”，而是主动采取积极作为去增进案主的身心福祉。通过礼貌问候、体温般的抚慰与誓死捍卫其尊严，是主动向长者倾注善意与关爱，属于行善利他原则的崇高体现（第 52 页、第 57 页）。因此选项 C 正确。
    QUESTION 08 待作答
    Treating all clients with equal care and attention, regardless of their condition or temperament, is an example of:
    无论案主是神志清醒还是重度失智、无论其温和配合还是暴躁易怒、无论其贫富社会地位，均一视同仁给予同等的倾情关怀与照料，是践行下列哪一项伦理原则的典范？
    A
    Autonomy
    自主自决原则（Autonomy）
    B
    Justice
    公平正义原则（Justice）
    C
    Beneficence
    慈惠行善原则（Beneficence）
    D
    Nonmaleficence
    不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence）
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: Justice dictates fairness and equity—treating every single client with impartial care and dedicated attention without bias, favoritism, or prejudice (p. 51, 57).
    临床解析： 公平正义原则（Justice）的崇高灵魂正是“一视同仁、不偏不倚”（Fair and equal treatment）。绝不能因为某位长者性格挑剔爱按铃就冷落怠慢，更不能因为某位长者安静不吭声就将其遗忘在角落，公正对待每一个人正是正义原则的最高准绳（第 51 页、第 57 页）。因此选项 B 正确。
    QUESTION 09 待作答
    Respecting personal preferences is an example of:
    在日常生活中充分尊重长者几点起床、喜欢穿哪件衣服、早餐喜欢喝茶还是咖啡等个人偏好（Preferences），是践行下列哪一项伦理原则的典范？
    A
    Autonomy
    自主自决原则（Autonomy）
    B
    Justice
    公平正义原则（Justice）
    C
    Beneficence
    慈惠行善原则（Beneficence）
    D
    Nonmaleficence
    不伤害原则（Nonmaleficence）
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    Clinical Rationale: Autonomy (self-determination) means recognizing clients as independent persons endowed with the right to make choices and direct their own daily routines (p. 51, 57).
    临床解析： 自主自决权（Autonomy）的核心内涵在于承认案主是独立的主权个体，拥有决定自己起居细节与个人生活方式的自由。尊重案主的个性化偏好，正是向长者让渡自决主权、摒弃包办替代的关键体现（第 51 页、第 57 页）。因此选项 A 正确。
    QUESTION 10 待作答
    Which question is least helpful when deciding on an ethical solution to a problem?
    在面临复杂的临床伦理困境权衡决策时，下列哪一个考量问题是最无帮助、最不具参考价值、甚至从根本上违背职业道德的？
    A
    Does the solution respect the client's wishes and stated preferences?
    这一解决方案是否充分尊重了受助案主本人的核心意愿与明确偏好？
    B
    Does the solution treat the client justly and fairly?
    这一解决方案是否公正、公允且一视同仁地对待了当事案主？
    C
    Does the solution provide a short-term benefit or a long-term benefit to the client?
    这一解决方案究竟能够为受助案主带来短期眼前获益，还是长久长远福祉？
    D
    Does the solution benefit you?
    这一解决方案能否给你个人带来私利或好处？
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: Client-centred healthcare ethics mandate that decisions are made strictly in the best interests of the client, never for the personal convenience, financial gain, or selfish benefit of the healthcare worker (p. 54, 57).
    临床解析： 选项 D 属于赤裸裸的个人私利诱惑与利己主义！医疗伦理决策的至高灵魂是“以案主为中心”（Client-centred），所有的审视均必须围绕案主的尊严、权利与安危展开；把“自己能否捞到好处”作为决策考量，是严重的利益冲突失德行径，最不应当出现在专业决策考量之中（第 54 页、第 57 页）。因此选项 D 正确。
    QUESTION 11 待作答
    Mr. Will, a client in a long-term care facility, refuses to be lifted into his chair for meals because he says being moved makes him too uncomfortable. As a result, he is developing pressure sores on his buttocks. You know that it is important to change positions frequently (see Chapter 15). Your supervisor has advised that he be 'forced' out of bed, but you wish to respect his wishes. Which of the following should be done first to deal with this ethical dilemma?
    长期照护院舍内的威尔先生（Mr. Will）坚决抗拒在用餐时被机械移位机吊入轮椅，抱怨搬运过程令其全身骨骼剧痛难忍。由于长年拒绝离床坐轮椅，其臀部骶尾部皮肤已出现发红并濒临破溃形成压疮。你知道定期更换体位与减压对长者极其关键。你的当班主管护士生硬地下令“必须强行将其弄下床”，但你内心极度渴望尊重长者拒绝折磨的意愿。面对这一尖锐的伦理两难，你首先应当采取的最佳处置措施是：
    A
    Leave Mr. Will in his bed for meals.
    彻底放弃沟通，直接听任威尔先生整天躺在床上用餐，不闻不问
    B
    Tell Mr. Will that he has to be moved but do it quickly so his pain is minimized.
    生硬告知威尔先生必须搬动，但在操作中动作粗暴快速以求速战速决
    C
    Discuss your concerns with the other team members, Mr. Will, and his family to see if a compromise can be reached.
    积极主动地与跨学科团队其他成员、主管护士、威尔先生本人及其家属展开三方诚恳座谈沟通，深入探查疼痛根源，共同探讨能否达成多方满意的折中双赢方案
    D
    Ask for a different client to take care of.
    逃避矛盾，直接向上级申请调换另一位听话的长者负责照料
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: Ethical dilemma resolution begins with collaborative communication. Open dialogue among the care team, client, and family allows exploration of root causes (e.g., inadequate pain management before transfers, improper sling sizing) and crafting dignified clinical compromises (p. 56, 58).
    临床解析： 选项 C 展现了顶阶专业从业者的问题解决成熟智慧与伦理担当。强行使用暴力硬拽（选项 B）是违法的身体侵害虐待；彻底撒手不管任由压疮恶化致死（选项 A）违背不伤害与行善原则；逃避推诿（选项 D）更是缺乏专业责任感。最佳路径正是搭建沟通桥梁（Discuss concerns with team, client, and family）：探查是否可以通过在搬运前遵医嘱提前口服镇痛药、更换更为舒适柔软的定制移位吊兜、或在床上采取高半卧位就餐等综合折中措施，既消除长者的搬运剧痛，又切实保障了骶尾部减压防压疮的临床目标（第 56 页、第 58 页）。因此选项 C 为唯一正确答案。
