    OBJECTIVES

    本章学习与执业考核目标
    After reading this chapter, the learner should be able to do the following:
    完成本章研读后，学习者应当能够达成以下核心专业能力考核目标：
    Explain the basic rights protected by the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms and the provincial and territorial human rights codes.
    阐述《加拿大权利与自由宪章》以及各省与地区人权法典所保护的基本权利。
    Describe client rights.
    详尽描述服务对象（Clients）所享有的各项合法权利。
    Identify ways support workers can respect their client's rights.
    指出支持工作者在日常工作中尊重服务对象各项权利的具体途径与方法。
    Describe the difference between criminal law and civil law.
    阐明刑法（Criminal Law）与民法（Civil Law）的根本法律属性界限与责任差异。
    Describe how negligence, defamation, assault, battery, false imprisonment, and invasion of privacy apply to the support worker's job.
    阐述过失疏忽、诽谤、恐吓/侵犯人身意图、人身侵害、非法拘禁以及侵犯隐私等侵权责任在支持工作者执业中的具体适用与认定。
    Define electronic privacy and describe how confidentiality can be maintained electronically.
    定义电子隐私权，并阐述在电子通信与数字化工作中维护信息保密性的实操要则。
    List the types of legislation that address support workers' rights and duties.
    列举规制与保障支持工作者法定权益与执业职责的各大类法律法规。
    Apply the information in this chapter to clinical practice properly.
    将本章所确立的法律与伦理规约精准、审慎地运用于实际临床护理照护实践中。
    🌐 Elsevier Evolve 官方教参研习配套资源库： http://evolve.elsevier.com/Canada/Sorrentino/SupportWorker
    p. 60

    KEY TERMS

    核心专业术语表 (原版 28 词全文收录)

    Key Terms · 核心专业术语表（全 38 词速查）

    英文术语 / 国际音标 中文对照 / 出处 教材标准学术释义与临床界定
    act /ækt/ 成文法 / 法案 p. 62
    A specific law that has passed through the required legislative steps.
    经过法定的立法程序审议通过并正式生效颁布的具体法律。
    administrator /ədˈmɪnɪstreɪtər/ 遗产管理人 p. 69
    The person appointed by the provincial courts to administer the estate of a client who has died without leaving a will.
    当案主去世前未立遗嘱时，由省法院依法指定负责清算、管理与分配其遗产的人员。
    advance care directive /ədˈvɑːns keə dɪˈrɛktɪv/ 预先照护指示 p. 67
    See advance directive.
    参见事先医疗指示（advance directive）。
    advance directive /ədˈvɑːns dɪˈrɛktɪv/ 事先医疗指示 / 预先医疗决定 p. 67
    A legal document in which a person states wishes about future health care, treatment, and personal care. Also known as an advance care directive, or sometimes a living will.
    一种具有法律效力的文书，个人借此陈述关于未来医疗救治、治疗方案及个人生活照护的意愿。亦称为预先照护指示，有时被称为生前预嘱。
    assault /əˈsɔːlt/ 恐吓罪 / 侵犯人身意图罪 p. 71
    Intentionally attempting to or threatening to touch a person's body without consent, causing the person to fear bodily harm.
    在未经知情同意的情况下，故意企图或口头/动作威胁触碰他人身体，致使对方产生人身安全遭受迫切伤害之恐惧的行为。
    battery /ˈbætəri/ 人身侵害罪 / 殴打罪 p. 71
    The touching of a person's body without the person's consent.
    在未经他人明确知情同意的情况下，实际发生未经许可的身体触碰或施加外力的行为。
    Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms /kəˈneɪdiən ˈtʃɑːtər.../ 《加拿大权利与自由宪章》 p. 61
    Part of the Canadian Constitution that lists the basic rights and freedoms to which all Canadians are entitled.
    加拿大最高宪法的核心宪法性组成部分，明确列举了全体加拿大居民依法享有的根本权利与基本自由。
    civil laws /ˈsɪvəl lɔːz/ 民法 p. 70
    Laws that deal with relationships between people.
    专门处理与调整平等主体（个人之间、或个人与私人法人之间）民事权利义务关系的法律体系。
    consent /kənˈsɛnt/ 知情同意 p. 66
    Agreement or approval—for example, to medical treatment, health care, or personal care services.
    对特定医疗干预、健康照料或个人照护服务所表达的自主许可、批准与法律同意。
    crime /kraɪm/ 犯罪 p. 70
    A violation of criminal law.
    对国家刑法规范的违法侵害行为。
    criminal laws /ˈkrɪmɪnəl lɔːz/ 刑法 p. 70
    Laws concerned with offences against the public and against society in general.
    涉及危害公众利益以及整体社会秩序之违法罪行的法律部门体系。
    defamation /ˌdɛfəˈmeɪʃən/ 诽谤侵权 p. 71
    The injuring of the name and reputation of a person by making false statements to a third person.
    通过向第三方陈述或散布虚假言论，贬损破坏特定人员名誉与社会声望的侵权行为。
    electronic privacy /ɪˌlɛkˈtrɒnɪk ˈprɪvəsi/ 电子隐私权 p. 65
    A person's right not to have their image, words, or character description or comments about their reputation made public by electronic means.
    个人依法享有的、不容许其肖像、原话、人格特征描写或对其名誉之评论被通过电子媒介向公众公开发布与传播的法定权利。
    estate trustee /ɪˈsteɪt trʌsˈtiː/ 遗产受托人 p. 69
    The person chosen by the now-deceased person to deal with their possessions, as stated in the will. Also known as guardian of property or executor or executrix.
    根据逝者生前遗嘱所指定负责清点处理其财产物资的法律代表。亦称财产监护人（guardian of property）或遗嘱执行人（executor/executrix）。
    executor, executrix /ɪɡˈzɛkjətər, ɪɡˈzɛkjətrɪks/ 遗嘱执行人（男/女） p. 69
    See estate trustee.
    参见遗产受托人（estate trustee）。
    false imprisonment /fɔːls ɪmˈprɪznmənt/ 非法拘禁 p. 71
    Unlawful restraint or restrictions of a person's freedom of movement.
    对他人身体行动自由实施非法的物理束缚、行动限制或空间隔离禁锢。
    guardian of property /ˈɡɑːdiən əv ˈprɒpəti/ 财产监护人 p. 69
    See estate trustee.
    参见遗产受托人（estate trustee）。
    harassment /ˈhærəsmənt, həˈræsmənt/ 骚扰 / 职场欺凌 p. 73
    Troubling, tormenting, offending, or worrying a person through one's behaviour or comments.
    通过令人不适的言行举止持续困扰、折磨、冒犯或引发他人心理焦虑的侵害行为。
    human rights codes /ˈhjuːmən raɪts kəʊdz/ 各省人权法典 p. 61
    Provincial and territorial legislation that prevents discrimination and promotes human rights in each jurisdiction.
    各省与地区用以预防歧视、保障该行政管辖区内所有个体基本人权的专门法律体系。
    informed consent /ɪnˈfɔːmd kənˈsɛnt/ 知情同意 p. 66
    Consent obtained under the legal condition whereby a person is first given complete, accurate, and relevant information so as to fully understand the action or procedure and its potential implications.
    在当事人预先充分获悉完整、准确且相关的信息，从而全面理解该医疗干预或照护操作及其潜在后果的前提下依法签署或表达的同意。
    invasion of privacy /ɪnˈveɪʒən əv ˈprɪvəsi/ 侵犯隐私权 p. 71
    Violation of a person's right not to have their name, photograph, private affairs, health information, or any personal information made public without consent.
    未经本人知情同意，擅自公开发布其姓名、照片、私生活事务、健康状况或任何个人隐私信息的侵权违法行为。
    legislation /ˌlɛdʒɪsˈleɪʃən/ 法律法规 / 法规体系 p. 61
    A body of laws that govern the behaviour of a country's residents.
    规制与约束一个国家或地区全体居民社会行为的成套成文法律体系。
    liable /ˈlaɪəbl/ 负有法律责任的 p. 70
    Legally responsible.
    在法律意义上须为其行为后果承担法律与民事赔偿责任。
    libel /ˈlaɪbəl/ 书面诽谤罪 p. 71
    The making of false written statements that hurt the reputation of another person.
    通过书面文字、印刷品、网络帖子或画作发布损害他人声誉的虚假言论。
    living will /ˈlɪvɪŋ wɪl/ 生前预嘱 p. 67
    A document that lets the reader know one's preferences about care intended to sustain life and reflects one's wishes at the time that it was created and signed. (This document has no legal status in Canada.)
    用于表达签署者关于维持生命救治措施意愿的书面文书，反映其签署当下的意愿（该文书在加拿大没有独立的独立法定效力，通常作为事先医疗指示的参考）。
    negligence /ˈnɛɡlɪdʒəns/ 过失疏忽 / 执业疏失 p. 70
    Failure to act in a careful or competent manner, resulting in harm to a person or damage to property.
    未以谨慎、审慎或合格胜任的方式履行照护职责，导致服务对象遭受人身伤害或财产损害的非故意侵权行为。
    oath of confidentiality /əʊθ əv ˌkɒnfɪˌdɛnʃiˈæləti/ 保密誓词 / 保密承诺协议 p. 65
    A pledge that promises that the signer will respect and guard personal and private information about a client, family, or agency.
    签署者郑重承诺尊重并严格恪守有关案主、其家庭成员或雇主机构之一切个人隐私与机密信息的法定誓约文书。
    patient advocate /ˈpeɪʃənt ˈædvəkət/ 病患权益倡导人 p. 63
    An individual who represents the interests and rights of clients within the health care system.
    在医疗健康系统中代表服务对象利益、维护其各项合法权益的独立专业倡导者。
    power of attorney /ˈpaʊər əv əˈtɜːni/ 委托代理权 / 委托书 p. 67
    See substitute decision maker for health care.
    参见医疗照护替代决策人（substitute decision maker for health care）。
    proxy /ˈprɒksi/ 医疗代理人 p. 67
    See substitute decision maker for health care.
    参见医疗照护替代决策人。
    regulations /ˌrɛɡjʊˈleɪʃənz/ 行政法规 / 细则规程 p. 62
    Detailed rules that implement the requirements of a legislative act.
    用于贯彻并落实成文法律所确立原则与要求的具体实操性法规细则。
    right /raɪt/ 权利 p. 61
    Something to which a person is justly entitled.
    一个人理所应当、基于正义与法律所享有之合法资格与权能。
    slander /ˈslɑːndər/ 口头诽谤罪 p. 71
    The making of false verbal statements that hurt the reputation of a person.
    通过口头言语陈述散布损害他人名誉声望的虚假陈述。
    substitute decision maker for health care /ˈsʌbstɪtjuːt dɪˈsɪʒən.../ 医疗照护替代决策人 p. 67
    A person authorized to make health care decisions on behalf of a living person who is unable to do so. Also called power of attorney for health care or proxy, depending on the province.
    经法律授权，代表失去自决能力的在世案主做出医疗救治决策的代理人。根据各省法律亦称为医疗持久委托人或医疗代理人。
    substitute decision maker for property /ˈsʌbstɪtjuːt dɪˈsɪʒən.../ 财产事务替代决策人 p. 69
    The person who would represent an incapable person's interests regarding their belongings.
    在当事人失去行为能力时，依法代表其管理其个人财产与财物利益的法定代理人。
    tort /tɔːt/ 侵权民事过错 p. 70
    A wrongful act committed by an individual against another person or the person's property.
    个人针对他人人身或其财产所实施的民事违法过错侵害行为。
    unintentional tort /ˌʌnɪnˈtɛnʃənl tɔːt/ 非故意侵权行为 p. 70
    An act committed that results in harm to another person or property, but without the intent to cause harm (e.g., negligence).
    虽非故意造成侵害后果，但因未尽审慎照料义务而导致他人遭受损害的民事侵权行为（如过失疏忽）。
    will /wɪl/ 遗嘱 p. 69
    A legal document stating a person's wishes concerning the distribution or disposal of their property.

    guardian of property /ˈɡɑːdiən əv ˈprɒpəti/
    财产监护人
    See estate trustee. (p. 69)
    参见遗产受托人（estate trustee）。
    harassment /ˈhærəsmənt, həˈræsmənt/
    骚扰 / 职场欺凌
    Troubling, tormenting, offending, or worrying a person through one's behaviour or comments. (p. 73)
    通过令人不适的言行举止持续困扰、折磨、冒犯或引发他人心理焦虑的侵害行为。
    human rights codes /ˈhjuːmən raɪts kəʊdz/
    各省人权法典
    Provincial and territorial legislation that prevents discrimination and promotes human rights in each jurisdiction. (p. 61)
    各省与地区用以预防歧视、保障该行政管辖区内所有个体基本人权的专门法律体系。
    informed consent /ɪnˈfɔːmd kənˈsɛnt/
    知情同意
    Consent obtained under the legal condition whereby a person is first given complete, accurate, and relevant information so as to fully understand the action or procedure and its potential implications. (p. 66)
    在当事人预先充分获悉完整、准确且相关的信息，从而全面理解该医疗干预或照护操作及其潜在后果的前提下依法签署或表达的同意。
    invasion of privacy /ɪnˈveɪʒən əv ˈprɪvəsi/
    侵犯隐私权
    Violation of a person's right not to have their name, photograph, private affairs, health information, or any personal information made public without consent. (p. 71)
    未经本人知情同意，擅自公开发布其姓名、照片、私生活事务、健康状况或任何个人隐私信息的侵权违法行为。
    legislation /ˌlɛdʒɪsˈleɪʃən/
    法律法规 / 法规体系
    A body of laws that govern the behaviour of a country's residents. (p. 61)
    规制与约束一个国家或地区全体居民社会行为的成套成文法律体系。
    liable /ˈlaɪəbl/
    负有法律责任的
    Legally responsible. (p. 70)
    在法律意义上须为其行为后果承担法律与民事赔偿责任。
    libel /ˈlaɪbəl/
    书面诽谤罪
    The making of false written statements that hurt the reputation of another person. (p. 71)
    通过书面文字、印刷品、网络帖子或画作发布损害他人声誉的虚假言论。
    living will /ˈlɪvɪŋ wɪl/
    生前预嘱
    A document that lets the reader know one's preferences about care intended to sustain life and reflects one's wishes at the time that it was created and signed. (This document has no legal status in Canada.) (p. 67)
    用于表达签署者关于维持生命救治措施意愿的书面文书，反映其签署当下的意愿（该文书在加拿大没有独立的独立法定效力，通常作为事先医疗指示的参考）。
    negligence /ˈnɛɡlɪdʒəns/
    过失疏忽 / 执业疏失
    Failure to act in a careful or competent manner, resulting in harm to a person or damage to property. (p. 70)
    未以谨慎、审慎或合格胜任的方式履行照护职责，导致服务对象遭受人身伤害或财产损害的非故意侵权行为。
    oath of confidentiality /əʊθ əv ˌkɒnfɪˌdɛnʃiˈæləti/
    保密誓词 / 保密承诺协议
    A pledge that promises that the signer will respect and guard personal and private information about a client, family, or agency. (p. 65)
    签署者郑重承诺尊重并严格恪守有关案主、其家庭成员或雇主机构之一切个人隐私与机密信息的法定誓约文书。
    patient advocate /ˈpeɪʃənt ˈædvəkət/
    病患权益倡导人
    An individual who represents the interests and rights of clients within the health care system. (p. 63)
    在医疗健康系统中代表服务对象利益、维护其各项合法权益的独立专业倡导者。
    power of attorney /ˈpaʊər əv əˈtɜːni/
    委托代理权 / 委托书
    See substitute decision maker for health care. (p. 67)
    参见医疗照护替代决策人（substitute decision maker for health care）。
    proxy /ˈprɒksi/
    医疗代理人
    See substitute decision maker for health care. (p. 67)
    参见医疗照护替代决策人。
    regulations /ˌrɛɡjʊˈleɪʃənz/
    行政法规 / 细则规程
    Detailed rules that implement the requirements of a legislative act. (p. 62)
    用于贯彻并落实成文法律所确立原则与要求的具体实操性法规细则。
    right /raɪt/
    权利
    Something to which a person is justly entitled. (p. 61)
    一个人理所应当、基于正义与法律所享有之合法资格与权能。
    slander /ˈslɑːndər/
    口头诽谤罪
    The making of false verbal statements that hurt the reputation of a person. (p. 71)
    通过口头言语陈述散布损害他人名誉声望的虚假陈述。
    substitute decision maker for health care /ˈsʌbstɪtjuːt dɪˈsɪʒən.../
    医疗照护替代决策人
    A person authorized to make health care decisions on behalf of a living person who is unable to do so. Also called power of attorney for health care or proxy, depending on the province. (p. 67)
    经法律授权，代表失去自决能力的在世案主做出医疗救治决策的代理人。根据各省法律亦称为医疗持久委托人或医疗代理人。
    substitute decision maker for property /ˈsʌbstɪtjuːt dɪˈsɪʒən.../
    财产事务替代决策人
    The person who would represent an incapable person's interests regarding their belongings. (p. 69)
    在当事人失去行为能力时，依法代表其管理其个人财产与财物利益的法定代理人。
    tort /tɔːt/
    侵权民事过错
    A wrongful act committed by an individual against another person or the person's property. (p. 70)
    个人针对他人人身或其财产所实施的民事违法过错侵害行为。
    unintentional tort /ˌʌnɪnˈtɛnʃənl tɔːt/
    非故意侵权行为
    An act committed that results in harm to another person or property, but without the intent to cause harm (e.g., negligence). (p. 70)
    虽非故意造成侵害后果，但因未尽审慎照料义务而导致他人遭受损害的民事侵权行为（如过失疏忽）。
    will /wɪl/
    遗嘱
    A legal document stating a person's wishes concerning the distribution or disposal of their property. (p. 69)
    明确陈述当事人去世后关于其个人财产如何分配与处置意愿的法定文书。
    p. 61

    You and your clients are entitled to a number of legal rights. The foundation of a good client-worker relationship is a basic understanding of the rights of the client, the worker's rights, and the legal responsibilities of the worker. As a support worker, how you conduct yourself at work and how you relate to your clients are determined by:

    您和您的服务对象依法享有诸多法定权利。良好的医患照护合作关系的基石，是对服务对象的法定权利、支持工作者的职业权利、以及工作者法定执业职责的深刻理解。作为一名支持工作者，您在工作中的行为准则以及您对待服务对象的方式，取决于以下三大准绳：

    • • Your professional code of ethics (see Chapter 4)
      您的职业伦理守则（参见第 4 章）
    • • Your employer's policies
      您的雇主机构政策规程
    • • Federal and provincial or territorial laws
      联邦以及所在省份或地区的法律法规

    Whereas ethics could be said to be rules of conduct that guide society when deciding what is right and what is wrong, and what is good and what is bad, legislation tells society what it can and cannot do. Legislation is a body of laws that govern the behaviour of a country's residents.

    如果说道德伦理是指导社会裁定什么是对什么是错、什么是善什么是恶的行为准则，那么法律法规（Legislation）则明确告诉社会成员什么可以做、什么绝不能做。法律法规是规制一个国家居民社会行为的成套成文法律体系。

    In Canada, legislation helps to make sure that all health care clients receive safe and skillful care and enjoy the privacy that all people deserve. Enforced by the courts, legislation also protects clients' rights and health care providers' rights.

    在加拿大，法律法规有助于确保所有医疗受助者均能获得安全、高技能的专业照料，并享有每个人应得的隐私尊严。由法院依法强制实施的法律法规，同时坚决保障着服务对象的权利与医护照护提供者的合法权益。

    UNDERSTANDING RIGHTS

    深刻理解法定理性与道德权利

    A right is something to which a person is justly entitled. Some rights, sometimes called moral rights, are based on a sense of fairness or ethics. For example, when you and a classmate arrange to study together, you have the right to expect that the classmate will show up and be prepared to work.

    权利（Right）是一个人理所应当、基于正义所享有的合法资格。部分权利有时被称为道德权利（Moral Rights），它们建立在公平观念或伦理道德的基础上。

    In another example, if you discussed a personal matter with a friend, you have the right to expect that your friend will not repeat this information to others. These rights are not based on written laws. They are based on moral principles: Commitments should be honoured, and secrets should be kept.

    例如，当您与一位同学约定共同复习研讨时，您有权期望对方按时赴约并做好研读准备；又如，如果您与一位挚友探讨私密个人事务，您有权期望对方不会向他人散播这一秘密。这些权利并非源自成文法律，而是建立在崇高道德准则之上：承诺应当恪守，秘密必须保守。

    Rights that are formally recognized in law are legal rights based on rules and principles outlined in the law and enforced by society. For example, various laws give you the rights to vote, to receive medical care, to own property, and to receive fair treatment if accused of a crime.

    在法律中获得正式认可的权利则是法定权利（Legal Rights），它们建立在成文法律所载明的规则与原则之上，并由社会国家强制力保证执行。例如，多项具体法律赋予您享有选举权、享有医疗照护的权利、拥有私人财产的权利、以及在遭受刑事指控时享有公平受审待遇的权利。

    Laws reflect the values of the society that created them. Canadians enjoy rights and freedoms that enable a life of equality and dignity.

    法律深刻反映了铸造这些法律的社会核心价值观。全体加拿大人享有广泛的权利与自由，从而能够过上平等且富有尊严的生活。

    BASIC HUMAN RIGHTS IN CANADA

    加拿大公民的基本人权体系

    The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms is federal legislation that applies to all Canadians regardless of where they live. As part of the Canadian Constitution, the Charter applies at the federal level, so all provincial and territorial laws must be consistent with its rules.

    《加拿大权利与自由宪章》（Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms）是一部适用于全体加拿大人（无论其居住在何处）的最高联邦立法。作为加拿大最高宪法的不可分割的一部分，《宪章》在国家最高层级生效，因此所有省份和地区的法律均必须与其规定保持绝对一致。

    The Charter lists the basic rights and freedoms to which all Canadians are entitled. They include the following:

    《宪章》明确列举了全体加拿大人依法享有的根本权利与基本自由，主要包括以下各项：

    • • Freedom of conscience and religion
      良知自由与宗教信仰自由
    • • Freedom of thought, belief, opinion, and expression
      思想、信念、观点与言论表达自由
    • • Freedom of peaceful assembly and association (usually these freedoms are associated with the right to form a union or engage in a strike)
      和平集会与结社自由（通常此类自由与组建工会或参与合法罢工的权利密切相关）
    • • The right to vote
      公民选举投票权
    • • The right to enter, stay in, or leave Canada
      自由出入境、居留或离开加拿大的迁徙权利
    • • The right to life, liberty, and security
      生命权、自由权与人身安全保障权
    • • The right to equality before and under the law, without discrimination based on race, ethnic origin, colour, religion, gender, age, or mental or physical disability
      在法律面前人人平等并受法律平等保护的权利，绝不容许因种族、民族渊源、肤色、宗教信条、性别、年龄或身心残疾而遭受任何歧视

    (The Charter is also discussed in Chapters 7 and 12 as this legislation pertains to the topics discussed there.)

    （由于该部宪法性法律与多元文化及职场议题息息相关，本教材亦将在第 7 章与第 12 章中对《宪章》展开延伸探讨。）

    Each Canadian province and territory also has a human rights code. These codes reaffirm the principle that all people are entitled to equal rights and opportunities—such as the same type and quality of support services—without discrimination because of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, or disability.

    加拿大的每一个省份与地区亦均颁布有各自的人权法典（Human Rights Code）。这些人权法典庄严重新确认了一项核心原则：所有人均平等享有同等的权利与机会——例如获取相同类型与同等品质的支持照料服务——绝不容许因种族、族裔背景、宗教信仰、性别、年龄或身心残疾而遭受任何歧视待遇。

    BASIC RIGHTS OF PEOPLE RECEIVING HEALTH SERVICES

    接受医疗与照护服务群体的基本法定权利

    The Human Rights Act is provincial and territorial legislation based on the Canadian Human Rights Act and applies to its specific province or territory. Each Human Rights Act is intended to (1) prevent discrimination and (2) promote and advance human rights in that jurisdiction. Some of the issues addressed by the Human Rights Act of each province or territory include the following:

    各省与地区的人权法案（Human Rights Act）是依据联邦《加拿大国家人权法》制定并适用于各自行政管辖区的专门地方立法。每部人权法案旨在达成两大核心宗旨：(1) 坚决预防歧视；(2) 在该管辖区内全面促进与推进人权事业。各省或地区人权法案重点规制的核心议题包括以下各项：

    • • Indigenous rights
      原住民权益保障
    • • Age discrimination
      严禁年龄歧视
    • • Disability
      身心残疾保护与无障碍环境
    • • Employment
      平等就业机会与公平对待
    • • Gender identity
      性别认同与性别表达保护
    • • Hiring practices
      招聘与用人实操中的反歧视原则
    p. 62

    BOX 5.1 Some Complex-Care Facility Issues Controlled by Legislation (British Columbia,1 Manitoba,2 Nova Scotia,3 Saskatchewan,4 Ontario5)

    专栏 5.1：受法定法律规制的复杂护理与长期照护机构核心运营事项（涵盖卑诗省、曼省、新斯科舍省、萨省、安省等）
    Social activities and recreation programs
    社交文娱活动与康乐疗愈项目规划
    Bedroom requirements - space, furnishings, privacy, windows, and lighting
    卧室建筑与生活标准——空间面积、家具配置、私密隔帘、采光窗户与照明
    Room temperature and water temperature
    室内居住温度与生活热水恒温标准（防烫伤）
    Bathrooms and bathing facilities
    卫生间设施与安全沐浴助浴设备
    Safety requirements, including fire safety and call systems
    法定安全技术规范，包括消防火警系统与床头紧急呼叫系统
    Mobility and access
    无障碍通行、轮椅活动与通道安全
    Dining area, lounges, recreation, and outside activity area
    餐饮就餐区、多功能休息厅、康乐室及室外活动绿地
    Care and supervision; care plans
    护理照料与临床监管；个性化照护计划（Care Plans）
    Confidentiality and privacy
    信息机密性与人身生活隐私保障
    Neglect and abuse
    严厉杜绝与强制报告虐待（Abuse）与疏于照料（Neglect）
    Use of restraints
    严禁随意使用身体或化学约束（Restraints），执行严苛医学审批
    Preparation and service of food
    食品安全储存、营养烹制与餐饮配餐服务
    Medication safety; administration of medication; medication records
    药品安全监管、药物辅助服药/给药规范及药物管理档案（MAR）
    Access to health services; oral health
    获取全面医疗健康服务与专业口腔口腔护理的权利
    Housing
    安全宜居的住宿居住环境
    Pregnancy and breastfeeding
    孕产妇及哺乳期支持保障
    Racism
    坚决杜绝种族主义与仇恨歧视
    Religious rights
    宗教信仰与精神寄托权利
    Sexual harassment
    零容忍任何形式的性骚扰
    Sexual orientation
    保护性取向与多元性别平权

    As well, all provinces and territories have legislation that addresses the rights and freedoms of people using health care services. Your clients, however, may be unable to exercise their rights because of illness or injury; physical, cognitive, or mental challenges; or old age, if the client is frail, confused, or isolated.

    此外，加拿大所有省份与地区均颁布有专门规制使用医疗卫生保健服务人群合法权利与自由的法律法规。然而，您的服务对象往往可能因患病或负伤、身体残疾、认知或心理精神障碍、或者因高龄衰弱、思维意识混乱或社会孤立，而无法独立行使或捍卫其法定权利。

    The laws governing health care have different titles across the country and may differ in details. You should be aware of the acts that govern your province or territory, which can easily be found on the Internet. Provincial and territorial governments constantly revise health care legislation and introduce new laws to protect the rights of people receiving care in facilities and in the community.

    规制医疗护理的法律在全国各地的正式名称不尽相同，具体条文细节亦有所差异。您必须清楚知晓规制您所在省份或地区的具体法案（这些法律均可在官方互联网上便捷检索）。各省与地区政府持续对医疗保健法规进行修订，并不断推出新法律，以强力捍卫在照护机构内及社区家庭中接受照料人群的各项合法权利。

    Health care legislation consists of acts and regulations. An act is another term for a law.

    医疗卫生法规体系主要由成文法案（Acts）与行政法规细则（Regulations）共同构成。法案是成文法律的正式代名词。

    Regulations are detailed rules that implement the requirements of the act. Most health care acts consist of general requirements for maintaining health, safety, and well-being.

    规程细则是落实并执行法案法定要求的具体详尽规则。大多数医疗法案确立了维护健康、安全与生活安康的总体性要求。

    For example, British Columbia's Community Care and Assisted Living Act sets out general requirements for the licensing, administration, operation, and inspection of long-term care facilities and also sets out broad standards of care. The Residential Care Regulation, which accompanies the Act, sets out detailed rules for meeting those broad standards of care. BOX 5.1 outlines some of the rules covered in British Columbia's Residential Care Regulation, as well as regulations in other provinces such as Manitoba, Nova Scotia, Saskatchewan, and Ontario.

    例如，卑诗省《社区照料与协助生活法》（Community Care and Assisted Living Act）确立了长期照护机构牌照审批、行政管理、日常运营及法定监察的总体原则，并制定了广泛的照护基准。伴随该法案实施的《住院照料规程》（Residential Care Regulation）则规定了满足上述广泛照料标准的详尽实操准则。专栏 5.1 概括了卑诗省《住院照料规程》以及曼尼托巴、新斯科舍、萨斯喀彻温和安大略等省份法规所涵盖的核心规定。

    Some provincial and territorial governments do not have regulations that lay out detailed rules. Instead, they issue standards that expand on their legislation.

    部分省份和地区政府并未专门颁布名为规程的细则，而是通过颁布专门标准（Standards）来对其立法进行具体化拓展。例如，阿尔伯塔省的长期照护立法伴随有称为《持续照护卫生服务标准》（Continuing Care Health Service Standards）的法定规范。

    For example, Alberta's long-term care legislation is accompanied by standards called Continuing Care Health Service Standards. Regardless of whether detailed rules are contained in regulations or standards, all live-in facilities in a province or territory must abide by these rules. Not to do so could result in removal of their licences.

    无论这些详尽规则是载于规程还是标准之中，所在省份或地区的所有全寄宿制照护机构均必须无条件恪守这些规范。未遵守规定将直接导致被依法吊销执业运营牌照的严重法律后果。

    Bill of Rights

    住院住户权利法案（Bill of Rights）

    There is no single list of rights afforded to all Canadians receiving care in facilities and in the community. However, some provinces, such as British Columbia, Manitoba and Ontario, have created a bill of rights for clients, which is essentially a summary of the lengthy rules contained in regulations and standards. For example, consider British Columbia's Residents' Bill of Rights for long-term care clients (BOX 5.2).

    目前加拿大尚未出台一部适用于全国所有在机构与社区接受照料人群的统一人权清单。然而，部分省份（例如卑诗省、曼尼托巴省和安大略省）已专门为受助案主制定了权利法案（Bill of Rights），其本质上是对繁复冗长的规程细则与照护标准的精炼浓缩总结。例如，请研读卑诗省专门针对长期照护住院案主制定的《住户权利法案》（专栏 5.2）。

    Some facilities and agencies write their own bills of rights based on provincial or territorial laws. Clients must receive a written list of their rights. As a support worker, you must know the provincial or territorial laws and your employer policy regarding client rights.

    许多医疗养老机构和社区服务社亦会依据省级或地区法律编撰符合自身院舍特色的权利法案。服务对象在入住或接受服务时，必须获得一份书面的权利清单。作为一名支持工作者，您必须对规制案主权利的省际法律以及您雇主机构的具体政策做到烂熟于胸。

    p. 63

    BOX 5.2 British Columbia's Residents' Bill of Rights

    专栏 5.2：加拿大卑诗省《长期护理院住户权利法案》（法定全文精解）
    Commitment to Care
    1. An adult person in care has the right to a care plan developed:
    (a) specifically for him or her, and
    (b) on the basis of his or her unique abilities, physical, social and emotional needs, and cultural, and spiritual preferences.
    照护承诺（Commitment to Care）
    1. 接受照料的成年受助案主有权拥有为其量身定制的专属照护计划：
    (a) 专为其个人特异性需求量身定制编制；并且
    (b) 紧密基于其独特的身心机能、生理机能、社交与情感需求、以及文化信仰与精神寄托偏好。
    Rights to Health, Safety and Dignity
    2. An adult person in care has the right to the protection and promotion of his or her health, safety and dignity, including a right to all of the following:
    (a) to be treated in a manner, and to live in an environment, that promotes his or her health, safety and dignity;
    (b) to be protected from abuse and neglect;
    (c) to have his or her lifestyle and choices respected and supported, and to pursue social, cultural, religious, spiritual and other interests;
    (d) to have his or her personal privacy respected, including in relation to his or her records, bedroom, belongings and storage spaces;
    (e) to receive visitors and to communicate with visitors in private;
    (f) to keep and display personal possessions, pictures and furnishings in his or her bedroom.
    健康、安全与尊严权利（Rights to Health, Safety and Dignity）
    2. 成年受助案主享有其健康、人身安全与人格尊严获得保护与促进的权利，具体包括以下全部法定权益：
    (a) 在能全面促进其健康、安全与尊严的方式下获得对待，并在促进尊严的环境中生活；
    (b) 受到绝对保护，免受任何身体、言语、心理、性或经济上的虐待（Abuse）与疏于照料（Neglect）；
    (c) 其生活方式与个人自主选择获得充分尊重与支持，并有权追求其社交、文化、宗教、精神及其他个人兴趣；
    (d) 个人生活与信息隐私权获得尊重，包括其健康档案、卧室、私人物品与储物空间的隐私；
    (e) 在不受打扰的私密空间接待访客并与访客展开私密交谈沟通；
    (f) 在其个人卧室内存放、摆放并陈列私人物品、家庭纪念照片与个人家具。
    Rights to Participation and Freedom of Expression
    3. An adult person in care has the right to participate in his or her own care and to freely express his or her views, including a right to all of the following:
    (a) to participate in the development and implementation of his or her care plan;
    (b) to establish and participate in a resident or family council to represent the interests of persons in care;
    (c) to have his or her family or representative participate on a resident or family council on their own behalf;
    (d) to have access to a fair and effective process to express concerns, make complaints or resolve disputes within the facility;
    (e) to be informed as to how to make a complaint to an authority outside the facility;
    (f) to have a person of his or her choice represent him or her during disputes, complaints or care conferences.
    参与权与表达自由权利（Rights to Participation and Freedom of Expression）
    3. 成年受助案主有权深度参与其自身的照护事务并自由表达个人观点，具体包括以下全部权益：
    (a) 亲自深度参与其照护计划的制定、评估与具体临床实施；
    (b) 发起组建并积极参与住户自治委员会或家属委员会，以代表全体受助者的共同利益；
    (c) 允许其家属或法定代表代理其参与住户或家属委员会；
    (d) 享有获得公正、高效且透明之机构内部申诉处理流程的权利，以自由表达关切、提出正式投诉或化解争议纠纷；
    (e) 充分知晓如何向机构外部法定监管机构提出正式投诉的法定渠道与程序；
    (f) 在发生争议纠纷、投诉调查或召开临床个案研讨会时，有权指定其信任的代理人全程代表其个人利益。
    Adapted from Government of British Columbia. (2009). Residents' bill of rights.
    本标准改编自加拿大卑诗省政府（2009年颁布）《住院住户权利法案》（Residents' Bill of Rights）。
    p. 64

    Generally, all clients have the following rights, which are a combination of moral and legal rights:

    总体而言，所有受助服务对象均享有以下各项根本权利（这些权利是有机融合的道德权利与法定权利的统一体）：

    • • The right to be treated with dignity and respect
      享有获得充满人格尊严与崇高尊重的对待的权利
    • • The right to safety from harassment, belittling, threats, verbal or physical harm of any kind from workers, family members, or other clients
      享有人身安全保障权，免受来自护理人员、家属或其他院舍病友任何形式的骚扰、贬损、威胁恐吓、言语侮辱或躯体暴力侵害
    • • The right to privacy and confidentiality, verbally, in writing, or electronically
      享有口头言谈、书面文件或电子网络数据维度的全方位隐私权与信息绝对机密性
    • • The right to give or withhold informed consent
      享有在充分知情前提下表达首肯同意或拒绝医疗照护方案的自决权
    • • The right to autonomy
      享有对自身生活方式与日常事务的完全自决与自主掌控权

    The Aphasia Institute of Ontario introduced the first-ever pictographic version of the Ontario Residents' Bill of Rights in 2005 (FIGURE 5.1). In live-in facilities, it must be posted near the text version of the Residents' Bill of Rights. This pictogram offers effective ways to communicate with clients who retain thinking and social skills but have difficulty expressing themselves when speaking, understanding the speech of others, and reading and writing.

    安大略省失语症研究所（Aphasia Institute）于 2005 年首创推出了全球首部图示版《安省住户权利法案》（图 5.1）。在所有寄宿制养老照护机构中，该图示版海报必须紧邻张贴于文字版权利法案旁。这种图示表达法为那些保留有思维认知和社交愿望、但在口语表达、听力理解或阅读书写方面存在严重失语障碍的案主，提供了极其高效的视觉化沟通桥梁。

    The Right to Be Treated With Dignity and Respect

    享有获得人格尊严与崇高尊重的神圣权利

    The right to dignity is both an ethical principle and a legal obligation throughout Canada. It is also a guiding principle of caregiving, as emphasized throughout this textbook under the acronym DIPPS (Dignity, Independence, Individualized care, Preferences, Privacy, and Safety).

    人格尊严权在全加拿大范围内既是一项崇高的执业伦理准则，更是一项不可逾越的法定强制义务。它构成了贯穿本书始终的核心照护哲学支柱——即 DIPPS 原则（尊严 Dignity、独立 Independence、个体化个性化照料 Individualized care、自主偏好 Preferences、隐私机密 Privacy、以及人身安全 Safety）。

    Most health care legislation aims to protect and promote the client's dignity. For example, British Columbia's Community Care and Assisted Living Act states that facilities must be operated 'in a manner that will maintain the spirit, dignity, and individuality of the client being cared for.' Ontario's Long-Term Care Homes Act similarly reinforces that residents have the right to be treated with courtesy and respect and in a way that fully recognizes their dignity.

    绝大多数医疗卫生立法均以坚决维护与促进案主的人格尊严为终极宗旨。例如，卑诗省《社区照料与协助生活法》明确载明：院舍设施的运营必须'以维护受助案主的精神风貌、人格尊严及独特个性为神圣准绳'。安大略省《长期照料院法》亦同样重申：住院住户有权在获得礼貌对待与崇高尊重、且完全认可其尊严的方式下接受一切护理服务。

    p. 65

    Respecting people's dignity means relating to them the way you would want to be related to if you were in their position. Speak respectfully to them, keeping in mind their hearing or sight limitations if they have any (FIGURE 5.3).

    尊重案主的人格尊严，意味着设身处地——以您若处在对方病患处境时所期盼被对待的方式去对待他们。以礼貌尊敬的态度与他们交谈，并时刻留意对方是否伴有听力衰退或视力减退等生理局限（图 5.3）。

    In support work, how you relate to a client is just as important as the care you provide. Treating clients with dignity provides them with emotional support and greatly contributes to their quality of life. BOX 5.3 lists ways of respecting the client's dignity.

    在支持工作中，您与案主的沟通互动方式，与您所提供的具体物理护理操作同等关键。以充满尊严的方式对待案主，能赋予其强大的情感支撑，并极大跃升其生命晚期的生活质量。专栏 5.3 列举了在日常执业中恪守案主尊严的具体黄金法则。

    The Right to Privacy and Confidentiality

    享有隐私与信息机密性的法定权利

    People using health care services have the right to personal privacy. They have the right to receive care in private and in a way that does not expose their bodies unnecessarily. Only staff members involved in the client's care should see, handle, or examine the client's body.

    所有使用医疗照护服务的人群依法享有神圣的人身隐私权。他们有权在完全私密的环境中接受照料，且身体绝不遭受任何不必要或未经遮挡的暴露。唯有直接参与该案主临床护理的医疗照护团队人员，方有资格查看、触碰或医学检查案主的身体。

    Information about the client's care, treatment, and condition is confidential (see Chapter 1). All provinces and territories have legislation that protects the privacy and confidentiality of clients' health information. This legislation is usually called a privacy act.

    有关案主的一切照料方案、治疗记录及健康身体状况均属绝密信息（参见第 1 章）。加拿大所有省份与地区均颁布有捍卫案主个人健康信息隐私与机密性的法律，此类法律通常被称为《隐私保护法》（Privacy Act）。

    Privacy acts provide guidelines to facilities and agencies on how to collect, use, and disclose personal health information. Most agencies require that all staff (and usually volunteers and students) sign an oath of confidentiality, a pledge that promises that the signer will respect and guard personal and private information about a client, family, or agency (see Chapter 9). When in doubt about whether or not to discuss something that you saw in regard to the client, you should always follow your employer's policies.

    隐私法对医疗照护机构和社区机构在如何采集、使用与披露个人健康信息方面做出了强制性法定规范。绝大多数机构均严正要求全体雇员（乃至学生与志愿者）在入职第一天必须签署《保密誓词》（Oath of Confidentiality）——这是一份庄严承诺，誓约签署者将恪守并严密守护案主、其家庭及机构的一切私密隐私信息（参见第 9 章）。如果您对工作中所见所闻是否可以对外谈及产生任何疑虑，必须严格服从雇主的保密政策，保持绝对缄默。

    In today's age of electronic communication, people tend to forget that everyone has the right to privacy. In health care, electronic privacy could be defined as a person's right not to have their image, words, or character description or comments about their reputation made public by electronic means. (See Chapter 9 for more discussion on electronic communication.) It is wrong, both ethically and now legally in most provinces, to post pictures, names, or discussions about your clients, no matter how 'nice' you think you are being to that client, on any social media site (see the Supporting Mrs. Jones: Social Media Versus a Client's Right to Confidentiality box for an example of how one client's privacy rights were violated).

    在当今高度数字化的电子通信时代，人们往往淡忘了每个人依法享有的隐私权。在医疗保健领域，电子隐私权（Electronic Privacy）被定义为：个人依法享有的、绝不容许其个人肖像、言谈原话、人格特征描写或涉及其声誉的言论被通过任何电子媒介向公众公开发布与传播的法定权利（关于电子通信的深度研读参见第 9 章）。无论您主观上自认为对案主有多么'友好友善'，在任何社交媒体平台（微信、Facebook、Instagram等）发布案主的照片、姓名或谈论其病情，在伦理上均属重大过错，且在绝大多数省份已被明确确立为违法行为（参见下文专栏'支援琼斯太太：社交媒体发布与案主保密权的惨痛冲突'案例）。

    p. 66

    BOX 5.3 Respecting the Client's Right to Dignity

    专栏 5.3：在临床日常照料中恪守与维护案主尊严的执业黄金法则
    Make eye contact with the client if culturally appropriate, and listen attentively (see FIGURE 5.3).
    在文化习俗容许的前提下与案主保持真诚的目光接触，并保持全神贯注的主动倾听（参见图 5.3）。
    Stand or sit close to the client, as appropriate. Use touch if you are sure the client would approve. Respect cultural differences regarding touching and personal space preferences (see Chapter 7).
    在适宜尺度下贴近案主站立或就座。在确信获得案主许可且对方感到舒适时运用疗愈性身体触碰。高度尊重涉及肢体接触与个人空间界限的跨文化多元差异（参见第 7 章）。
    Be patient. Provide kind and thoughtful care.
    保持高度耐心。提供体贴入微、充满人本温度的善良照料。
    Say 'please' and 'thank you,' and practise other common acts of courtesy.
    常说'请'和'谢谢'，在细微之处贯彻日常文明礼貌习惯。
    Never yell at, scold, embarrass, laugh at, or be sarcastic toward the client.
    绝不冲着案主大吼大叫、大声训斥、使其当众难堪、讥笑嘲弄或使用任何冷嘲热讽的尖酸言语。
    Respect the client's belongings and property. Do not touch personal possessions unless you have a reason to and have the client's permission. Be sure to put items back where you found them.
    充分尊重案主的个人所有物与生活财产。除非因护理需要且事先征得案主同意，否则绝不可擅自翻动其私人物品。用毕务必将其原样归还原处。
    Address an adult client by title and last name, unless the client tells you otherwise. Never call an adult client 'sweetie,' 'honey,' 'dear,' 'grandpa,' or any other such term.
    以正式尊称与姓氏（如'史密斯先生'、'布朗女士'）尊称成年案主，除非对方主动明确要求您直呼其名。在任何情况下，绝不可轻浮称呼成年长者为'甜心'、'宝贝'、'亲爱的'或'老爷爷/老奶奶'等贬损尊严的幼态化代称。
    Tell your supervisor about the client's complaints or concerns about the agency, facility, or services.
    一旦案主对机构设施、服务质量或人员态度表达任何不满、抱怨或关切，务必立即如实向上级主管主管护士汇报反馈。
    Reinforce clients' independence by allowing them to do things for themselves. Avoid creating dependency.
    通过允许并鼓励案主自行动手完成力所能及的日常事务，全力强化其自立自理能力；坚决避免因过度包办而制造不必要的身体与心理依赖。
    Assist the client with personal care and grooming to promote a neat, clean, and dignified appearance.
    悉心协助案主做好个人卫生盥洗与仪容修饰，维护整洁、体面且富有尊严的仪容风貌。

    The Right to Give or Withhold Informed Consent

    享有作出知情同意或拒绝治疗的首要自决权

    All people have the right to decide for themselves whether or not they agree to medical treatment, health care, or personal care services. This agreement or approval is called consent.

    所有人均享有对是否接受医疗救治、健康干预或个人照护服务进行独立自主裁决的神圣权利。这种自主表达的赞同或批准，在法律上统称为同意（Consent）。

    The right to consent extends further in that people have a right to complete, accurate, and relevant information about their treatment or procedure and the potential consequences of agreeing to or refusing it. Consent obtained under this condition is called informed consent.

    同意权的法理内涵更为深远：人们依法享有预先获悉关于该项治疗或手术操作的完整、精确且相关的医学信息，并充分了解选择接受或拒绝该方案所带来的潜在健康后果。在此种法定透明条件下所取得的同意，被称为知情同意（Informed Consent）。

    For consent to be informed and valid, three conditions must be met: (1) The client must be given all information about the nature of the treatment, the benefits, the potential risks, and alternative options; (2) The client must have the mental capacity to understand and appreciate the information; (3) The consent must be given voluntarily, without coercion, manipulation, or undue influence.

    知情同意欲具备法律效力，必须同时严苛满足三大法定前置条件：(1) 案主必须获悉关于该治疗性质、预期临床获益、潜在风险并发症及所有替代治疗方案的全部信息；(2) 案主必须具备能够充分理解并评估这些医学信息的法定民事精神行为能力；(3) 同意必须由其完全自愿作出，绝不容许存在任何强迫、欺骗诱导或不正当的外在施压影响。

    Who is responsible for obtaining informed consent? In Canadian health care, the physician or registered healthcare provider who is performing the procedure is legally responsible for discussing the details and securing informed consent.

    由谁负责获取知情同意？在加拿大医疗照护体系中，负责实施该手术或复杂医疗干预的主治医师或注册医护人员，负有向案主详尽解释并依法取得其知情同意的法定职责。

    The support worker is never responsible for obtaining written informed consent, nor are support workers permitted to explain surgical or complex medical procedures. You may, however, be asked to witness the client's signature on a consent form, depending strictly on your employer's written policy.

    支持工作者（PSW）绝对不可代为获取书面知情同意书，亦绝对严禁向案主解释手术或复杂侵入性医疗操作。根据您雇主机构的书面政策规约，您有时可能被允许作为见证人在同意书上见证案主本人的亲笔签名，但绝不可超越角色边界。

    p. 67

    BOX 5.4 Respecting the Client's Right to Privacy

    专栏 5.4：在日常临床照料中严守案主隐私权的执业行为细则
    Knock on the client's door and wait for permission to enter.
    进入案主房间前务必先轻声敲门，并耐心静候获得许可后方可进入。
    Ask others in the room to leave before giving care to the client. To stay, they must have the client's permission.
    在为案主实施身体照护前，礼貌请房间内的其他探视人员暂时回避；若要留步，必须事先获得案主本人的明确同意。
    Close the door, and use curtains or screens when providing care or whenever the client requests it. Also, close drapes and window shades.
    在实施护理照护时或在案主提出要求时，务必关闭房门并拉合床周隔帘或屏风；同时务必拉严窗帘与遮光百叶窗。
    Drape the client properly during personal care and procedures. Expose only the body part involved in the treatment or procedure.
    在进行身体护理和临床操作过程中，使用大浴巾进行极其严谨的身体遮盖（Proper Draping），仅暴露当前正在进行清洗或护理操作的特定身体解剖部位。
    Keep the client covered when moving them through a facility's corridors and elevators.
    使用轮椅或平车在机构走廊及电梯间推送转运案主时，务必使用毛毯将其身体妥善包裹遮盖，避免任何身体暴露。
    Close the bathroom door when the client is using the bathroom. If the client needs help, stay in the bathroom with the client, and keep the door closed.
    当案主使用卫生间如厕时，务必关闭卫生间房门。若案主需要助厕协助，您应留在卫生间内陪护，同时保持房门关闭。
    Do not open or read the client's mail or personal documents (FIGURE 5.4).
    绝不可擅自拆开或偷看案主的私人信件、账单或个人书面文件（参见图 5.4）。
    Do not touch or examine the client's belongings without permission.
    未经案主亲口许可，绝不随意触碰、翻看或翻动其私人物品。
    Allow the client to visit with others in the facility and to use the telephone in private.
    保障案主在机构内接待访客以及使用电话进行通话时的绝对私密空间。
    Do not pry into the client's private life or ask for personal information that is not necessary for your work.
    绝不打探案主的私人感情与生活隐私，严禁打听任何与当前照料工作无关的个人背景信息。
    Keep all personal and health care information about the client confidential.
    对案主的所有个人身世与医疗健康记录信息，严格恪守不可泄露的终身保密义务。

    Advance Directive

    事先医疗指示（Advance Directive）与生前决策

    An advance directive (also known as an advance care directive) is a legal document that allows clients to state their wishes about future health care, treatment, and personal care. It lets family members and health care providers know what treatments the client wants or does not want if the client becomes unable to make decisions in the future. Advance directives usually address end-of-life care issues such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), mechanical ventilation, tube feeding, dialysis, and organ or tissue donation.

    事先医疗指示（Advance Directive，亦称为预先照护指示）是一部具有法律效力的正式文书，允许受助案主在身心清醒健全时预先书面声明其对未来医疗干预、生命支持抢救方案及个人照料的真实意愿。当案主未来因严重疾病、创伤昏迷或严重认知障碍失去知情决策能力时，该指示可明确指引家属及医护团队知晓案主期望接受或拒绝哪些救治措施。事先医疗指示通常涉及生命终末期抢救议题，例如心肺复苏术（CPR）、机械人工通气呼吸机、鼻饲胃管喂养（Tube feeding）、血液透析以及器官或组织捐献等重大人道决断。

    p. 68

    Supporting Mrs. Jones: Social Media Versus a Client's Right to Confidentiality

    临床个案深度剖析：支援琼斯太太——社交媒体发布与案主保密权的严重冲突
    Jane (not her real name) was a student support worker who was very fond of one particular client, Mrs. Jones, to whom she provided support care in her home. On the client's birthday, Jane took a picture of her on her cellphone and posted the picture on a social networking site. The picture showed Mrs. Jones smiling and wearing a hat with a cellophane bow that had been taken from the wrapping of a birthday present.
    简（化名）是一名在读的支持工作者实习生，她对自己在社区居家照料的一位特定长者——琼斯太太非常喜爱。在琼斯太太生日当天，简用自己的智能手机为长者拍了一张照片，并将其公开发布到了社交网络平台上。照片中，琼斯太太面带微笑，头上戴着一顶用生日礼物包装纸上的玻璃纸蝴蝶结扎成的小帽子。
    Mrs. Jones's teenage grandchildren, who live in another city, happened to come across this site, where they saw the picture of their grandmother. The grandchildren showed it to their parents, who were shocked and horrified that their mother (usually a very proper woman) was displayed in such an undignified manner. When they questioned their mother, she recalled that it was the student who took her picture. The client's children called the student's school and filed a formal complaint.
    琼斯太太居住在另一座城市的几位十几岁的孙辈偶然浏览该社交网站时，惊愕地看到了自己祖母的照片。孩子们立即将照片给父母看，长者的子女们感到无比震惊与愤慨，因为他们素来端庄典雅的母亲竟然在互联网上以这样一种毫无尊严且滑稽的方式被公开展览。当子女们致电质问母亲时，长者回忆起确实是那位实习生用手机拍摄了照片。长者的子女立即致电简所在的高校，提出了极其正式严厉的法律投诉。
    The school's lawyer agreed that the student violated the client's right to privacy by posting her picture on the Internet without her permission. The lawyer also reminded the school of its obligation to inform students that they must destroy any client information (printed or electronic) in such a way that it cannot be retrieved or reassembled. The student was eventually asked to leave her support worker program because her actions went against the oath of confidentiality that she had signed in the first week of her program.
    高校的法务律师在审查后认定：该学生未经案主知情授权便擅自将照片发布到互联网上，已经无可辩驳地严重侵害了案主的法定隐私权。律师同时严肃重申了学校的法律义务，即必须坚决警示所有学生，必须以不可逆、无法恢复重建的物理或数据方式销毁任何涉及案主的信息记录。这名学生最终被学校勒令退学并开除学籍，因为她的行为彻底违背了她在入学第一周亲手郑重签署的《保密誓词》。

    Living Will

    生前预嘱（Living Will）与加拿大法律地位

    The term living will originated in the United States and has no legal status in Canada. In Canada, it is usually known as an advance directive.

    生前预嘱（Living Will）这一术语最初发源于美国，在加拿大司法体系中并不具备独立的法律效力。在加拿大，此类意愿通常通过合法的事先医疗指示（Advance Directive）予以体现。

    A living will is a document that lets the reader know a person's preferences about care intended to sustain life and reflects a person's wishes at the time that it is created and signed. Some people who are still living in their own homes create living wills with the hope that their wishes will be respected when they can no longer make decisions.

    生前预嘱是一份旨在向读者告知当事人关于维持生命救治措施之偏好的书面文书，反映了其在起草并签署该文书当下的主观意愿。许多仍居住在社区家中的长者会起草生前预嘱，期望未来一旦失去自决意识时，其个人意愿能够获得家属与医护的遵从。

    p. 69

    Supporting Mme. LeBrun: Is a Living Will Enforceable?

    临床批判性思维修炼：支援勒布伦夫人——非正式'生前预嘱'是否具备强制执行力？
    Mme. Violette LeBrun lives in a province that issues an organ donor section on her health card. Mme. LeBrun indicated that she would like her organs to be donated upon her death. She also instructed her friends and family that if anything happened, she did not want to be kept alive on life support. Mme. LeBrun even purchased over the Internet a 'living will kit,' filled it out, and gave it to her lawyer for safekeeping until the time came for her family to make this decision.
    维奥莱特·勒布伦夫人（Mme. Violette LeBrun）居住在一个省份，该省医疗健康卡上附有器官捐献登记栏。勒布伦夫人在健康卡上正式签名勾选，表明希望在身故后捐献全部器官。她还多次向亲友严肃嘱托：一旦发生意外不测，她坚决不愿依靠生命维持系统苟延残喘。勒布伦夫人甚至通过互联网自行购买了一套'生前预嘱模板工具包'，自行填写完毕后交由她的私人律师妥善保管，以便未来面临抉择时供家属查阅。
    Later, Mme. LeBrun was involved in a head-on motor vehicle accident and was declared brain-dead by the emergency department doctor. She was placed on life support until her family could be notified. Her family immediately rushed to the emergency department and then were shown Mme. LeBrun's organ donor request on her health card that indicated her wish to donate her organs. Her family were then asked if they would give permission for Mme. LeBrun's organs to be taken from her body.
    不幸的是，后来勒布伦夫人遭遇了一起严重的车辆迎头对撞车祸，急诊科医生经抢救后宣布其已处于脑死亡状态。医院为其实施了生命维持系统监护，直到通知到其家属。家属闻讯后火速赶赴急诊室，医生向其家属展示了勒布伦夫人健康卡上的器官捐献意愿签署栏，并询问家属是否同意签署法定许可，以便外科医生实施器官摘除移植手术。
    Mme. LeBrun's husband and daughter, both in a state of shock, refused to allow the doctors to retrieve any of Mme. LeBrun's organs. They decided that 'Mom had been through enough pain' and asked for her to be taken off the life-support system. Her body was then sent to the funeral home that her family specified.
    此时，勒布伦夫人的丈夫与女儿均处于极度的精神创伤与休克悲痛之中，他们坚决拒绝允许医生摘除勒布伦夫人的任何器官。家属哭泣着坚决主张：'妈妈已经承受了太多痛苦'，并强烈要求立即撤除生命维持系统。医院最终尊重了具有法定第一顺位代理权家属的决断，撤除呼吸机宣布死亡，遗体被运往家属指定的殡仪馆。
    CRITICAL THINKING ANALYSIS:
    1. Why was Mme. LeBrun's wishes overridden? Under current legislation in many Canadian provinces, even if a person signs an organ donor card, health care providers still require the consent of the legal substitute decision-maker (next of kin) at the bedside before organ retrieval.
    2. The 'living will kit' purchased online did not meet the strict statutory execution requirements of the provincial Health Care Consent Act, nor had she formally appointed a durable Power of Attorney for Personal Care. Therefore, the immediate family held full legal authority to direct care and refuse organ donation.
    临床法理与批判性思维核心解析：
    1. 为什么勒布伦夫人的个人意愿被推翻？在加拿大许多省份现行法律框架下，即便死者生前签署了器官捐赠卡，在实际实施器官摘除手术前，医护团队在法律实操中仍必须取得床旁法定近亲属（第一顺位替代决策人）的知情签字许可。
    2. 勒布伦夫人在互联网上购买的所谓'生前预嘱工具包'并未严密满足该省《医疗知情同意法案》所规定的严格法定签署见证要件，且她生前未正式依法签署任命具有法律效力的'人身照料持久委托人'（POA for Personal Care）。因此，其法定配偶和成年子女依法拥有最高决定权，其床旁的拒绝撤回具有压倒一切的最终法律效力。

    Substitute Decision Maker for Property

    财产事务替代决策人（SDM for Property）

    A person who acts on behalf of a client in regard to property is a substitute decision maker for property. This person may or may not have been chosen by the client when they were able to make such decisions. A substitute decision maker for property cannot make personal care decisions unless a separate document is signed identifying that person also as the substitute decision maker for personal care.

    代表案主全权处理其名下财产事务的人员，被称为财产事务替代决策人。该人选可能是案主在神志清醒有行为能力时依法委任的，也可能并非案主亲自挑选。必须严密注意：财产事务替代决策人绝无任何法定权力代表案主做出人身或医疗照料决策，除非当事人另行依法签署了一份单独的法定委托文书，明确指定同一人兼任人身照料替代决策人。

    If a client does not have a substitute decision maker for property, the provincial or territorial court may appoint someone to act as one. The appointed person would be legally bound to act in the client's best interests. Although terms may vary among jurisdictions, a person who handles property after a client dies is the executor or executrix (or estate trustee) named in the will.

    若案主生前未依法委任财产替代决策人且已失去行为能力，省或地区法院可依法裁定指定专人代为行使财产监护权。该被指定人负有神圣法定信托义务，必须完全基于案主的最大合法利益行事。虽然各司法管辖区的法律称谓有所不同，但在案主身故后全权负责清理与处置其遗产的人员，被称为生前遗嘱中所载明的遗嘱执行人（男 Executor / 女 Executrix）或遗产受托人（Estate Trustee）。

    Wills & Legal Boundaries for Support Workers

    遗嘱法律规范与支持工作者的绝对执业红线

    A will is a legal document stating a person's wishes concerning the distribution or disposal of their property upon death. As a support worker, you must observe strict legal and professional boundaries regarding clients' wills:

    遗嘱（Will）是一份法定正式法律文书，用于详细陈述立遗嘱人在去世后关于其名下所有财产如何分配与处分的真实意愿。作为一名支持工作者，您必须在涉及案主遗嘱的事务中坚决严守以下铁律红线：

    • • Never witness a client's will. In most jurisdictions, witnessing a client's will is a direct violation of professional boundaries and can invalidate the will or disqualify any beneficiaries.
      绝对不可作为见证人在案主的遗嘱上签字。在绝大多数司法管辖区，医护人员为案主见证遗嘱直接构成严重违背职业伦理边界，不仅可能导致该遗嘱被法院判定无效，更可能使任何受赠人失去继承资格。
    • • Never accept substantial gifts, property, or bequests from a client. Doing so can lead to criminal charges of undue influence or exploitation of a vulnerable person and immediate termination of employment.
      绝不容许接受案主馈赠的贵重个人礼物、财产份额或遗赠继承。此种行为极易招致'利用脆弱群体不正当施压牟利'的严重刑事指控，并将面临被立即开除并吊销执业资质的严惩。
    p. 70

    If you fail to act in a competent manner or violate someone's rights, you are legally responsible (liable) for your actions and could be fined, sued, or even imprisoned.

    如果您在工作中未能以审慎胜任的方式履行照护职责，或者侵犯了他人受法律保护的法定权利，您必须依法为其行为后果承担全部法律责任（Liable），并可能遭受行政罚款、民事起诉索赔、甚至被判处刑事监禁。

    UNDERSTANDING LEGAL ISSUES

    深入理解法律责任的核心体系

    You must obey both criminal laws and civil laws. Criminal laws are concerned with offences against the public and against society in general. A violation of criminal law is called a crime—for example, theft, murder, rape, or abuse—and a person found guilty of a crime is fined or sent to prison.

    在执业与日常生活中，您必须同时恪守刑法（Criminal Laws）与民法（Civil Laws）。刑法专门惩治危害公众安全与整体社会秩序的严重违法犯罪行为。违反刑法的行为被称为犯罪（Crime）——例如盗窃、故意伤害杀害、强奸或虐待脆弱长者等罪行——被法院判定犯有罪行的人将面临严厉罚金或被判入狱服刑。

    Civil laws deal with relationships between people. For example, laws relating to business disputes, divorce, or adoption are civil laws. A tort is a wrongful act committed by an individual against another person or the person's property.

    民法专门调整平等民事主体（人与人之间、或人与私法实体之间）的法律关系。例如关于商业合同纠纷、离婚抚养或领养孤儿的法规均属民法范畴。侵权行为（Tort）是指一个人针对另一个人的人身安全或其财产权益所实施的民事违法过错。

    A person who commits such an act can be sued by the injured person. Torts may be intentional or unintentional. An example of an unintentional tort is negligence. Examples of intentional torts are assault, battery, false imprisonment, invasion of privacy, and defamation of character.

    实施侵权过错的主体可被遭受侵害的当事人直接向民事法院提起诉讼索赔。侵权行为分为非故意侵权（Unintentional Tort）与故意侵权（Intentional Tort）。非故意侵权的典型代表是过失疏忽（Negligence）；而故意侵权的典型代表包括恐吓罪（Assault）、人身侵害殴打（Battery）、非法拘禁（False Imprisonment）、侵犯隐私（Invasion of Privacy）以及名誉诽谤（Defamation）。

    Negligence

    过失疏忽（Negligence）的核心法律构成要件

    Clients expect their health care providers to do their jobs competently and carefully. Negligence occurs when a person fails to act in a careful or competent manner and thereby harms the client or damages property. Negligence is an unintentional wrong because the person at fault did not intend to cause harm.

    受助案主完全有权合理期望医护提供者能够审慎、熟练且胜任地履行其工作职责。当一名护理人员未能以谨慎或合格的方式履行职责，从而直接导致案主遭受人身伤害或财产损害时，便构成了过失疏忽（Negligence）。

    They either failed to do what a reasonable and careful person would have done or did what a reasonable and careful person would not have done. The negligent individual may have to pay damages (a sum of money) to the injured person. The causes of negligence are given below:

    过失疏忽属于一种非故意侵权民事过错，因为过错方主观上并未蓄意谋害案主，而是其要么未能履行一个理智审慎之合格同行在此种情形下应当履行的职责，要么实施了一个理智审慎同行绝不会犯下的鲁莽举动。被认定构成过失疏忽的责任人必须向受害当事人支付巨额法定民事损害赔偿金。导致过失疏忽的三大核心诱因如下：

    • • Not performing a task or procedure correctly. As a support worker, always perform your tasks and procedures exactly as you have been taught. Not following procedures can result in harming the client. For example, you are taught to keep a urinary drainage bag below the client's bladder level. If you keep it above the bladder level, urine will not drain, and the client could develop a urinary tract infection. Such negligence could harm the client, and charges could result.
      未正确、合规地执行护理操作规程。作为一名支持工作者，务必完全严格按照培训标准所教导的医学技术规范执行操作。不遵守标准流程极易直接造成案主身体伤害。例如，在专业培训中要求导尿管集尿袋必须始终维持低于案主膀胱解剖水平面；若您粗心将其挂在高于膀胱水平处，尿液将逆流淤积无法顺畅引流，极易诱发严重的逆行性尿路感染甚至败血症。此种过失将重创案主健康，并招致严重的法律侵权指控。
    • • Performing a task or procedure that you are not trained or authorized to do.
      擅自实施超出您专业受训资质或未获合法授权的越权医疗操作。

    FOCUS ON LONG-TERM CARE: Resident Autonomy

    聚焦长期照护：捍卫住院住户的自主选择权（Resident Autonomy）
    Residents in long-term care facilities have the right to make their own choices, including when to get up, when to go to bed, what to wear, how to spend their time, and what to eat (FIGURE 5.5). As a support worker, you must allow your clients to make choices whenever it is safely possible. Doing so reinforces their sense of dignity and control over their lives.
    长期照护机构中的住户享有对个人生活做出自主抉择的神圣权利，包括决定何时晨起起床、何时就寝休息、当天穿着什么款式的衣裳、如何打发休闲时光、以及选择一日三餐的菜肴食谱（参见图 5.5）。作为一名支持工作者，只要在人身安全容许的前提下，您必须全方位支持并赋权案主自主作出决断。如此执业能够极大重塑他们对自己生命历程的尊严感与掌控感。
    p. 71

    Performing a task or procedure that you are not allowed to do. Do not do more than is allowed within your job description, your employer's policies, and legislation within your province or territory. You may be asked to do something beyond your scope of practice—for example, giving medications.

    严禁实施超出法律执业边界的任务或操作：切勿超出您法定岗位职责说明书（Job Description）、雇主规章制度以及所在省或地区立法的执业许可范围。在实际工作中，有人可能会要求您实施超出执业范围的操作——例如代为执行给药注射。

    Even if you are assured that you are not liable, you should remember that you are responsible for your own actions. In other words, you may, in fact, be liable. In such a situation, remember that refusing to follow through on a request that is beyond your scope of practice is your right and your duty.

    即便有人向您口头信誓旦旦保证'出了事不用您负责'，您必须时刻铭记：在加拿大法律面前，每个人永远对其本人的亲手行为负有不可推卸的终身责任！换言之，您事实上必将承担全部法律赔偿与刑事责任。在此种高危情境下，坚决拒绝执行超出执业范围的违规要求，不仅是您的神圣职业权利，更是您不可推卸的法定职业操守！

    Making a mistake because of carelessness that causes harm to a client. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes, but a mistake that results from carelessness and causes harm is a negligent act.

    因粗心大意导致案主遭受人身伤害的过错过失：每个人在工作中都有可能犯错，但因疏忽大意且造成实质人身伤害后果的过错，直接构成法定的过失侵权行为。例如，如果您在洗浴后没有立即将地面水渍拖干，极易导致案主脚底打滑重重跌倒骨折，您的这种粗心在法律上即被定性为严重的过失疏忽。

    For example, if you do not mop up a spill, you could cause a client to slip and fall, and your carelessness could be considered negligence. BOX 5.5 contains examples of negligent acts committed by support workers.

    专栏 5.5 详尽列举了支持工作者在临床照料中极其容易触犯的典型过失侵权恶性案例。

    BOX 5.5 Examples of Negligent Acts Committed by Support Workers

    专栏 5.5：支持工作者在临床实操中易触犯的典型过失疏忽（Negligence）案例
    A support worker leaves the bed in the raised position. The client falls out of bed and breaks his hip.
    支持工作者在护理结束后忘记将病床降至最低位置。案主随后从高处跌落坠床，导致股骨颈髋关节粉碎性骨折。
    A support worker raises the bed rails when the care plan states that they should be left down. The client falls while trying to climb over the bed rails.
    照护计划明确规定床栏必须保持放下状态，但支持工作者擅自升起双侧床栏。案主夜间试图翻越床栏如厕，失去重心倒栽坠床重伤。
    A support worker does not raise the bed rails when the care plan states they should be raised. The client falls out of bed.
    照护计划明确要求床栏必须升起固定，支持工作者疏忽未升起床栏。案主在睡眠中翻身滚落坠床。
    A support worker does not check the temperature of bathwater. The client is burned when placed in the tub.
    支持工作者未事先使用温度计或手腕内侧测试沐浴水温。将案主浸入过烫浴缸水中，导致其皮肤遭受严重烫伤。
    A support worker leaves a frail, disoriented client unattended in the shower. The client falls and suffers a serious head injury.
    支持工作者将一位身体极度虚弱、定向力障碍的长者独自留在淋浴间无人看护。案主在湿滑地面跌倒，头部遭受致命颅脑外伤。
    A support worker does not report a significant change in the client's condition, such as sudden confusion or severe pain. The client later suffers a major stroke or collapses from internal bleeding.
    支持工作者观察到案主出现突发性意识模糊或剧烈疼痛等重大病情恶化体征，却未立即向主管护士汇报。案主随后突发大面积脑中风或因内出血休克死亡。

    The Importance of Accurate Charting: A client could be harmed even when you do your job competently and carefully. It is important to record every procedure accurately, following your employer's policy.

    精准护理记录（Charting）的法律护身符价值：即便您完全胜任且审慎地履行了职责，案主仍可能发生意外或并发症。严格按照雇主规程及时、精确记录每一项护理操作至关重要！

    What you record may later on protect you from charges of negligence. For example, a client confined to bed develops serious pressure sores. The family thinks she was left lying in the same position too long.

    您亲笔所做的法定护理记录，日后极可能成为保护您免遭过失起诉的最有力法律铁证。例如，一名长期卧床的案主发生了严重压疮（褥疮），家属愤怒控告指责是护理人员将其长时间遗忘在同一卧位所致。

    Your charting shows that you repositioned her every hour, as stated in her care plan. This proves that you gave the required care and did not cause the pressure sores. If you had not recorded that you repositioned her, the court may conclude that you were negligent ('If it wasn't charted, it wasn't done').

    然而，您的护理翻身记录清晰详尽地载明您严格按照照护计划每隔 1 小时为其实施了体位变换与减压。这在法庭上强有力地证明了您履行了全套法定护理标准，压疮并非因您的过失引起。反之，若您做了翻身却未在记录单上签字记录，法庭将遵循法律铁律直接推定——'凡未经记录者，即视为从未发生'（If it wasn't charted, it wasn't done），从而直接裁定您构成过失侵权！

    p. 72

    Assault, Battery, and False Imprisonment

    恐吓、人身侵害与非法拘禁的法定法律界限

    Assault and battery are intentional torts as well as crimes. Assault is intentionally attempting or threatening to touch a person's body without consent, causing the person to fear bodily harm.

    恐吓威胁（Assault）与人身侵害（Battery）既是民事故意侵权行为，更是受到刑法严惩的刑事罪行。恐吓罪是指在未经对方知情同意的情况下，故意企图或言行威胁触碰他人身体，致使对方产生人身安全即将遭受伤害的迫切恐惧感。

    Threatening to restrain a client unless they behave is an assault. Battery is the actual touching of a person's body without consent. Giving a client a bath or performing a procedure after the client has clearly refused is considered battery.

    例如，威胁长者'如果你不乖乖听话就把你绑在轮椅上'直接构成恐吓罪。人身侵害罪则是指在未经同意的前提下实际发生未经许可的身体触碰。在案主明确拒绝之后，仍强行给案主脱衣擦澡或强行实施某项操作，在法律上即直接构成人身侵害殴打罪！

    False imprisonment is the unlawful restraint of or restrictions on a person's freedom of movement. For example, preventing a client from leaving a facility, locking a client in a room, or the unnecessary use of physical or chemical restraints without a physician's written order constitutes false imprisonment.

    非法拘禁（False Imprisonment）是指对他人身体行动自由实施非法的物理束缚、行动限制或空间隔离。例如，违背案主意愿阻止其离开院舍机构、将案主反锁在房间内、或者在未经执业医师书面开具法定约束医嘱的前提下滥用物理约束带或化学药物约束，均在法律上直接构成严重的非法拘禁犯罪！

    Defamation of Character: Slander vs. Libel

    人格名誉诽谤侵权：口头诽谤与书面诽谤

    Defamation is injuring the name and reputation of a person by making false statements to a third person. Slander is the making of false verbal statements that hurt the reputation of a person.

    诽谤（Defamation）是指通过向第三方散布虚假言论，贬损破坏他人名誉与社会声誉的侵权过错。口头诽谤（Slander）是指通过口头口语交谈散布损害他人名誉的虚假言论；而书面诽谤（Libel）则是指通过书面文字、正式出版物、社交网络公开言论等形式散布损害他人声誉的虚假言辞。

    Libel is the making of false written, published, or electronic statements that hurt the reputation of another person. Support workers must never engage in workplace gossip or make derogatory comments about clients, colleagues, or employers.

    支持工作者在职场中绝不可参与任何长舌闲话、八卦流言，严禁散布任何贬损案主、同事或雇主机构的名誉评论。

    LEGISLATION AFFECTING THE WORKER

    保护与规制支持工作者权益的法定法律体系

    Just as legislation protects clients' rights, various federal, provincial, and territorial laws protect the rights of support workers and outline their legal duties. All provinces and territories have legislation that addresses human rights, occupational health and safety, employment standards, labour relations, workers' compensation, long-term care services, and community services.

    正如法律法规严密捍卫受助服务对象的合法权益一样，加拿大各级联邦、省和地区法律亦强力捍卫着支持工作者自身的法定执业权益，并明确划定了工作者的法律职责边界。全国所有省份与地区均构建有涵盖人权法案、职业健康与安全法规、就业劳工标准法、劳资工会关系法、工伤抚恤补偿制度、长期照护院法及社区服务法的全方位法律安全网。

    p. 73

    Human Rights Legislation for Workers

    保障支持工作者职场平权的人权法律

    Human rights codes protect workers' basic human rights. This legislation states that employers must treat all workers equally and not discriminate on the basis of a worker's ethnic background, colour, gender, sexual orientation, religion, age, or disability.

    各省人权法典坚决捍卫劳动者的根本人权。该法律明确规定：雇主必须一视同仁地对待全体员工，绝不容许基于员工的族裔渊源、肤色、性别、性取向、宗教信仰、年龄或身心残疾而实施任何歧视对待。

    Employers and employment agencies also cannot discriminate at the request of a client. Human rights legislation declares that workers have the right to be free from harassment (also called workplace bullying) by the employer, the client, or a fellow worker. Harassment means troubling, tormenting, offending, or worrying a person through one's behaviour or comments.

    即便应服务对象客户的无理要求，雇主及用人派遣中介亦绝对严禁实施歧视。人权立法庄严宣告：每一位劳动者均享有在职场中免遭雇主、受助案主或同事任何形式骚扰（亦称职场霸凌 Workplace Bullying）的神圣权利。骚扰是指通过令人生厌的言谈举止蓄意困扰、折磨、冒犯或引发他人心理恐惧焦虑的侵害行为。

    Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) Legislation

    职业健康与安全法案（OH&S）：劳动者的三大根本安全权利

    All provinces and territories have occupational health and safety (OH&S) legislation. This legislation outlines the rights and responsibilities of workers, employers, and supervisors in creating and maintaining a safe work environment. Employers must 'take every precaution reasonable in the circumstances for the protection of a worker.' Under OH&S legislation, workers have three fundamental rights:

    加拿大所有省份与地区均颁布有强制性的《职业健康与安全法案》（OH&S）。该法案明确确立了雇员、雇主以及现场督导主管在构建并维护安全无害工作环境中的法定权利与强制义务。法律严令雇主必须'在具体情境下采取一切合乎情理的审慎防范措施以全力保护劳动者的人身安全'。在 OH&S 法律框架下，每一位支持工作者均享有三项至高无上的根本劳动安全权利：

    • • The right to know about potential hazards in the workplace and receive proper safety training (e.g., WHMIS training for hazardous chemicals, safe transfer techniques).
      知情权（Right to Know）：有权全面知悉职场中的潜在危险源，并依法强制接受雇主提供的充分安全技术培训（例如工作场所危险品信息系统 WHMIS 培训、机械升降机安全转移技术等）。
    • • The right to participate in workplace health and safety committees and voice safety concerns without fear of retaliation.
      参与权（Right to Participate）：有权参与院舍职场联合健康与安全委员会，公开就职场安全隐患建言献策，绝不承受任何解雇或排挤打击报复。
    • • The right to refuse unsafe work if the worker has reasonable cause to believe that a job or condition poses an imminent danger to their health or safety.
      拒绝危险工作权（Right to Refuse Unsafe Work）：当工作者有合理理由相信某项操作或作业环境对自己或他人生命健康安全构成迫切重大危险时，依法享有拒绝上岗作业的绝对法定权利。

    Employment Standards, Labour Relations, and Workers' Compensation (WCB)

    就业劳工标准法、工会集体谈判与工伤抚恤补偿机制

    Employment standards legislation outlines minimum employment conditions, including minimum wage, overtime pay, hours of work, vacation entitlements, and termination notice. Labour relations legislation gives workers the right to organize, form or join trade unions, and bargain collectively for better wages, benefits, and working conditions. Workers' compensation legislation provides financial compensation, medical treatment, and vocational rehabilitation to workers who are injured on the job or develop occupational illnesses.

    《就业标准法案》（Employment Standards Legislation）确立了全社会法定的最低劳动保障底线，包括法定最低时薪、加班工资倍率、最长法定工时限额、带薪休假年假以及辞退提前通知期。《劳资关系法案》（Labour Relations Legislation）庄严确立了广大医护支持工作者依法组织工会、加入行业工会并开展集体劳资谈判以争取更优厚薪酬福利与人本执业环境的神圣结社权利。而各省《工伤赔偿法》（Workers' Compensation Board, WCB）则确保任何在执业岗位上因工负伤或罹患职业病的护理人员，均能依法全额获得工伤薪酬补偿、免费医疗救治与专业职业康复保障。

    p. 74

    Community Services Legislation & Professional Record Keeping

    社区卫生服务立法体系与医疗护理记录规范

    Community services legislation sets out the rules and procedures for accessing and providing community services, including support work. It defines the different types of community services and details how the services are to be provided. This legislation also governs health care records, detailing how documentation must be created, maintained, and kept confidential to ensure high accountability and the continuity of compassionate client care.

    社区服务立法（Community Services Legislation）详尽制定了居民获取并由专业机构提供各项社区健康服务的法定规则与准入程序，其中包含广泛的个人支持护理服务。该立法严密界定了不同社区照护服务类型的边界，并就各项上门护理服务应如何合规实施做出了详尽要求。同时，该部立法对受助者的健康档案记录（Health Care Records）确立了极其严苛的规范，详尽规制了照护记录应如何如实书写、妥善归档及严密保密，以确保高度的执业透明度并保障人性化照护的连续性。

    Clinical Practice in the Community (社区临床实操典范)

    本页配图生动展现了加拿大专业支持工作者深入社区与长者家庭，以充满尊严、跨文化包容与卓越专业技能，为长者及其家庭筑起最坚实的健康安全屏障。

    p. 75

    CHAPTER REVIEW

    全章学术精要与考点总结回顾

    KEY POINTS (核心知识要点全真归纳)

    核心知识要点全真归纳（加拿大执业必背 5 大支柱）
    As a support worker, your conduct at work is determined by (1) your code of ethics, (2) your employer's policies, and (3) federal and provincial or territorial laws.
    作为一名支持工作者，您在工作中的行为操守受控于三大根本准绳：(1) 您的职业伦理守则；(2) 您雇主机构的政策规程；(3) 联邦与省/地区的法律法规。
    The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms lists the basic rights and freedoms to which all Canadians are entitled. All provincial and territorial laws must be consistent with its rules.
    《加拿大权利与自由宪章》明确列举了全体加拿大人依法享有的根本权利与基本自由。所有省份与地区的立法均必须与其宪法性原则保持绝对一致。
    All people have the right to be treated with respect and dignity, as reinforced throughout this book by the acronym DIPPS (Dignity, Independence, Individualized care, Preferences, Privacy, and Safety).
    所有人均享有受到尊重与尊严对待的神圣权利，这一原则贯穿本书核心的 DIPPS 照护金法则（尊严、独立自立、个体化照护、个人偏好、隐私机密、人身安全）。
    All people have a right to decide whether or not to agree to medical treatment or health care or personal care services—called consent. This right extends further in that people have a right to complete, accurate, and relevant information about the situation and the potential implications for consenting or refusing to consent—called informed consent.
    所有人均享有对其是否接受医疗救治、健康干预或个人照护自主表达同意与否的权利——这被称为知情同意。该权利进一步延伸为：当事人在做出决断前，依法享有获取完整、准确且相关的信息，并充分知晓表达同意或拒绝可能导致的潜在健康后果——这被称为知情同意（Informed Consent）。
    Wills are legal documents drawn up by people stating how they want their property distributed upon their death. A living will is a written statement that tells the person's wishes in regard to accepting or refusing medical care; living wills are not legally enforceable in Canada. Advance directives are legal documents that allow clients to communicate their decisions about their own end-of-life care. A substitute decision maker, or power of attorney, is a person appointed to make decisions for a client who is unable to make informed decisions.
    遗嘱是个人生前设立关于其去世后财产如何分配的法律文书。生前预嘱是一份表达在失去自决能力时接受或拒绝维持生命治疗意愿的书面声明，在加拿大不具备独立的法定强制执行力。事先医疗指示则是允许案主传达关于生命终末期救治决策的合法文书。替代决策人（或持久授权委托人）是在案主丧失知情决策能力时依法被委任代表其做出决策的法定代理人。

    CRITICAL THINKING IN PRACTICE (Page 75): Mrs. Lopez

    临床批判性思维修炼：洛佩兹太太——痴呆症长者的跌倒风险防范与尊严自主冲突
    Mrs. Lopez is a 79-year-old client with progressive vascular dementia who has generalized weakness in both legs. She is at high risk of falling. Her care plan states that she must be supervised when ambulating and that an audible chair alarm must be placed under her seat cushion to alert staff when she attempts to stand up unassisted. Mrs. Lopez repeatedly removes the alarm, shouting that the buzzing sound makes her feel like a 'prisoner' and an 'animal in a cage.' The family demands that you tie her into the chair with a restraint vest to prevent a broken hip.
    洛佩兹太太现年 79 岁，患有进行性血管性痴呆症伴双下肢全身性无力，属于极高跌倒风险长者。其照护计划明确规定：长者在室内走动时必须全程处于视线监护之下，且其座椅坐垫下必须放置蜂鸣椅垫报警器（Chair Alarm），以便在长者试图自行站起时向护士台发出高分贝警报。然而，洛佩兹太太反复愤怒地拽掉该报警器，痛苦地尖叫哭诉说这种刺耳的蜂鸣噪音让她觉得自己像个'囚犯'和'笼子里的动物'。其家属为此极为焦虑，强烈要求护理人员使用约束衣背心将老人牢牢捆绑在轮椅上，以防其再次跌倒发生髋骨骨折。
    Clinical Decision Analysis:
    1. Tying Mrs. Lopez into the chair with a restraint vest without a physician's written order constitutes False Imprisonment and Battery. Support workers cannot apply restraints at the request of family members.
    2. The chair alarm, while intended for safety, violates her sense of dignity and triggers severe agitation. The professional response is to document her distress, consult the supervising nurse, and re-evaluate the care plan to implement dignified, least-restraint alternatives (e.g., lower seating, purposeful scheduled activities, closer visual companionship).
    临床专业决策精解：
    1. 在缺乏执业医师依法开具的书面强制医疗医嘱的前提下，仅凭家属要求使用约束背心将长者捆绑在轮椅上，在法律上直接构成严重的'非法拘禁罪'（False Imprisonment）与'人身侵害殴打罪'（Battery）！支持工作者绝对不可顺从家属要求滥用身体约束。
    2. 椅子报警器虽然出于安全防跌倒初衷，但已严重践踏了长者的自尊心，并诱发了灾难性的心理烦躁。合格的支持工作者应立即将长者的心理痛苦与诉求如实记录并汇报给主管注册护士，启动多学科个案重评，寻求最具尊严的'最少约束替代干预方案'（如调整超低重心矮椅、设置定时如厕与散步日程、提供富有生活意义的桌旁陪伴活动等）。

    QUESTION 01 待作答
    1. Which of the following is true about basic human rights in Canada?
    1. 关于加拿大公民的基本人权体系，下列哪项表述是绝对正确的？
    A They are guaranteed only to Canadian citizens.
    B They apply to all people within Canadian borders regardless of origin.
    C They can be overridden by an employer's internal policy manual.
    D They do not include the right to equality under the law.

    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    《加拿大权利与自由宪章》作为最高宪法性立法，保障加拿大境内全体居民的根本人权与平等保护，任何雇主规章或地方行政条例均绝无权力凌驾于宪法之上。

    2. 加拿大各省与地区人权法典（Human Rights Codes）的核心宗旨是促进：
    A Freedom from poverty by reducing taxes
    B Unequal treatment with respect to services and facilities

    D Equal treatment with respect to age, gender, and ethnicity
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    人权法典的核心法律宗旨在于消除在公共设施、就业劳动与医疗卫生服务中基于年龄、性别认同、种族、宗教信仰或残疾的任何歧视，保障人人平等的对待。
    QUESTION 03 待作答
    3. Which of the following is an example of treating a client with respect and dignity?
    3. 下列哪项临床照护实操行为是充满人格尊严与尊重的崇高典范？
    A Assuming that the client needs your help before they ask
    B Forgetting to insert the hearing aids for the client
    C Ordering the client's food at mealtime without asking them
    D Being careful with the client's personal possessions and knocking before entering
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    进门前主动敲门并耐心等待应门、悉心珍视并保护案主的私人物品，直接体现了对案主私人空间主权与人格尊严的高度敬畏。
    QUESTION 04 待作答
    4. Which of the following is required to help a client give informed consent?
    4. 为协助案主作出具备法律效力的知情同意，下列哪项要素是必不可少的？
    A Asking the client politely to hurry up and make a decision
    B Ignoring details about the potential risks and side effects of the treatment
    C Reassurance that the proposed treatment is the only option
    D Information about the likely consequences of not having the treatment and potential risks
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    知情同意权的核心精义在于：案主在做出决定前，必须充分获悉该干预的潜在风险并发症、预期获益以及如果拒绝治疗可能引发的身体健康后果。
    QUESTION 05 待作答
    5. Who decides the kind of recreation activities a long-term care client will do?
    5. 在长期照护机构中，究竟应由谁最终决定住户参与何种休闲文娱与康乐活动？
    A The client's family
    B The client's physician or nurse
    C The facility administration
    D The client
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    根据《住户权利法案》与 DIPPS 原则中的'自主偏好'（Preferences）原则，案主对其个人业余时间如何度过拥有最高的自决主权。
    QUESTION 06 待作答
    6. If a client complains to you about the home care agency's policy, you should:
    6. 如果受助长者在居家上门护理中向您抱怨机构的规章政策，您的正确专业做法是：
    A Inform your supervisor about the complaint
    B Advise the client to speak to your supervisor directly and do nothing yourself
    C Ignore the client's complaint as long as your care is completed
    D Try to distract the client and change the subject
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    支持工作者是机构与服务对象之间的沟通纽带，遇案主提出服务关切与投诉时，负有向主管护士（Supervisor）及时、如实汇报反馈的法定职责。
    QUESTION 07 待作答
    7. Which of the following statements about negligence is true?
    7. 关于过失疏忽（Negligence）的法律属性，下列哪项判断是完全正确的？
    A It is an intentional tort.
    B The client acted in a reasonable manner.
    C Harm was caused to a client or a client's property through failure to act competently.
    D A prison term may automatically result in civil court.
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    过失疏忽是一种非故意民事侵权行为（Unintentional Tort），其核心构成要件在于工作者未尽到理智审慎同行应有的照料职责，从而对案主造成了实质性的人身或财产伤害。
    QUESTION 08 待作答
    8. The intentional attempt or threat to touch a person's body without consent is:
    8. 在未获知情同意的前提下，故意企图或言语威胁触碰他人身体，致其产生恐惧的行为被定义为：
    A Battery
    B Assault
    C Defamation
    D False imprisonment
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    恐吓（Assault）强调引发伤害恐惧的企图或威胁言行；而人身侵害殴打（Battery）则强调未经许可的实际身体接触发生。
    QUESTION 09 待作答
    9. Touching a client's body without the client's consent is:
    9. 在未经案主明确知情同意的前提下，实际触碰案主身体的物理行为属于：
    A Battery
    B Assault
    C Invasion of privacy
    D Negligence
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    未经许可实施身体触碰（即便出于给药擦澡的善良初衷，只要案主已明确拒绝）在法律上均构成人身侵害罪（Battery）。
    QUESTION 10 待作答
    10. If you restrain a client without a doctor's order, you could be charged with:
    10. 如果您在未经执业医师书面开具法定医嘱的情况下擅自约束限制案主自由，您将面临何种指控？
    A Defamation
    B Slander
    C False imprisonment
    D Negligence
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    非法剥夺或限制案主的身体行动自由（无论是上锁、绑缚还是私自使用约束带）均直接构成非法拘禁罪（False Imprisonment）。
    QUESTION 11 待作答
    11. Under OH&S legislation, you have the right to:
    11. 依据职业健康与安全法规（OH&S），您依法享有的核心劳动法权利是：
    A Refuse unsafe work if it poses a danger to your health or safety
    B Delegate medical duties to unregistered family members
    C Ignore employer safety policies during home visits
    D Refuse care to clients based on personal prejudice
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    OH&S 法律赋予劳动者三大权利：知情权、参与权以及在面临迫切严重危险时绝对拒绝危险工作的权利（Right to Refuse Unsafe Work）。
    QUESTION 12 待作答
    12. Legislation that covers financial compensation for workers injured on the job is called:
    12. 为因工负伤或罹患职业病的劳动者提供全额经济赔偿与医疗抚恤的专门法律是：
    A The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
    B Workers' compensation legislation (WCB)
    C Employment standards legislation
    D Regulated health professions legislation
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    各省与地区的《工伤补偿法》（Workers' Compensation Legislation / WCB）专职为因工负伤或因工致残的劳动者提供工伤工资替代津贴、终身医疗康复抚恤金及再就业职业培训。

    OBJECTIVES

    本章学习与执业能力考核目标
    After reading this chapter, the learner should be able to do the following:
    完成本章研读后，学习者应当能够达成以下核心专业能力考核目标：
    Differentiate between the current definition of health and the one used in the past.
    准确辨析当代健康定义与 19 世纪传统生物医学消极定义之间的本质飞跃。
    Describe the concept of holism and explain how it affects the role of a support worker.
    阐述“全人理念”（Holism）的核心内涵，并解释其如何指导支持工作者的执业角色。
    Explain the current concepts of health and wellness.
    深入阐释当代健康（Health）与安康（Wellness）的科学概念。
    Describe the 12 aspects of our health and environment that are beyond our immediate control (known as the determinants of health).
    系统阐述超出个人直接控制范畴的 12 项宏观健康与生活环境决定因素（即健康的决定因素）。
    Describe how health can be achieved in all dimensions of life.
    阐明如何在生命的各大维度中全面达成健康与平衡。
    Explain the effects of culture, stigma, and discrimination on clients who have illnesses and disabilities.
    阐释文化背景、社会污名化（Stigma）与歧视对身患疾病与残疾案主的深重影响。
    Describe personal factors that can influence health.
    阐述影响个人健康的内在生活方式、心理防御与行为抉择因素。
    Explain how people, families, or communities who follow good holistic health practices can still become very ill.
    科学解释为何践行良好全人健康生活方式的个人、家庭或社区仍可能遭受严重疾病侵袭。
    Explain common reactions to illness and disability.
    详尽剖析案主遭遇突发疾病与渐进性残疾时的常见身心防御与情绪行为反应。
    Describe change and loss associated with illness and disability.
    系统阐述疾病与残障给案主日常生活、心理自尊及独立自理能力带来的深远转变与丧失。
    🌐 Elsevier Evolve 官方教参研习配套资源库： http://evolve.elsevier.com/Canada/Sorrentino/SupportWorker
    p. 78

    KEY TERMS

    核心专业术语表 (全 27 词全文收录)

    Key Terms · 核心专业术语表（全 27 词速查）

    英文术语 / 国际音标 中文对照 / 出处 教材标准学术释义与临床界定
    attitude /ˈætɪtjuːd/ 健康态度 p. 85
    A person's beliefs, values, or opinions toward engaging in healthy behaviours.
    个人对于参与健康促进行为、采纳积极生活方式所秉持的核心信念、价值观或主观看法。
    cognitive health /ˈkɒɡnɪtɪv hɛlθ/ 认知健康 p. 81
    Well-being in the intellectual dimension, achieved through an active, creative mind.
    在智力维度的良好状态，通过保持大脑活跃、具备创造性思维与终身学习能力而达成。
    determinants of health /dɪˈtɜːmɪnənts ɒv hɛlθ/ 健康的决定因素 p. 82
    The most important factors—such as lifestyle, environment, human biology, and health services—that determine health status in an individual or a community.
    决定个人或社区整体健康状况的最核心综合因素，包括生活方式、生活环境、人类生物学遗传以及卫生服务可及性。
    dimensions of health /dɪˈmɛnʃənz ɒv hɛlθ/ 健康的维度 p. 79
    All aspects of a person's health—physical, emotional, social, spiritual, cognitive. Holistic health considers all of these aspects.
    构成一个人健康的全部维度——身体、情绪、社交、精神与认知。全人健康理念将所有这些维度视为不可分割的整体。
    disability /ˌdɪsəˈbɪlɪti/ 残疾 / 机能丧失 p. 87
    The loss of physical or mental function.
    身体或心理生理功能的受损或丧失。
    discrimination /dɪˌskrɪmɪˈneɪʃən/ 歧视 p. 92
    The unfair treatment of people on the basis of such aspects as their physical characteristics, health history, or group membership.
    基于身体特征、健康病史、社会阶层、族群或文化身份等属性对特定人群施加的不公正、不平等待遇。
    emotional health /ɪˈməʊʃənl hɛlθ/ 情绪健康 p. 80
    Well-being in the emotional dimension, achieved when people feel good about themselves.
    情绪维度的良好状态；当个体拥有积极的自我认同、良好的自控力与环境适应韧性时达成。
    environmental health /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmɛntl hɛlθ/ 环境健康 p. 84
    According to the World Health Organization, 'all the physical, chemical, and biological factors external to a person and all the related factors impacting behaviours.'
    世界卫生组织定义为：个体外部所有的物理、化学与生物因素，以及所有影响人类行为的相关环境因素的总和。
    equitable /ˈɛkwɪtəbl/ 公正合理的 / 公平的 p. 83
    Fair, reasonable, and just.
    符合社会正义、公平合理且无特权偏倚的状态。
    gender /ˈdʒɛndər/ 社会性别 p. 85
    The roles, personality traits, attitudes, behaviours, values, and relative power and influence assigned to the sexes by society.
    社会基于生理性别所赋予个人的角色期待、性格特质、态度行为、价值观以及相对的社会权力与影响力。
    genetic endowment /dʒɪˈnɛtɪk ɪnˈdaʊmənt/ 遗传禀赋 / 基因构成 p. 84
    The genetic makeup that predisposes an individual to adopt certain behaviours that affect health status.
    决定个体生理素质与疾病易感倾向的先天遗传基因生物学构成。
    health /hɛlθ/ 健康 p. 79
    A state of well-being in all dimensions of one's life.
    个体在生命全部维度中达到的一种安康与良好状态。
    holism /ˈhəʊlɪzəm/ 全人理念 p. 79
    A concept that considers the whole person; the whole person has physical, social, emotional, cognitive, and spiritual dimensions.
    一种将服务对象视为完整有机体的哲学与照护理念；全人由身体、社交、情绪、认知与精神五大维度交融构成。
    holistic health /həʊˈlɪstɪk hɛlθ/ 全人健康 p. 79
    A state of well-being in all dimensions of one's life.
    个体在生理、心理、社交、认知与精神所有维度全面协调平衡的理想良好状态。
    illness /ˈɪlnɪs/ 疾病 p. 87
    The loss of physical or mental health.
    身体或心理生理健康的丧失或受损状态。
    marginalize /ˈmɑːdʒɪnəlaɪz/ 边缘化 / 社会排斥 p. 85
    The act of excluding people who are not part of the majority culture.
    排斥、孤立非主流文化群体或脆弱社会群体的行为与社会现象。
    optimal health /ˈɒptɪməl hɛlθ/ 最优健康状态 p. 85
    State of achievable maximum well-being in each of the five dimensions: physical, emotional, social, cognitive, and spiritual.
    个体在自身条件约束下，在身体、情绪、社交、认知与精神五大维度中所能达到的最大可能安康状态。
    personal empowerment /ˈpɜːsənl ɪmˈpaʊəmənt/ 个人赋权 / 自主掌控感 p. 87
    Understanding and accepting that you can make your own healthy lifestyle choices, free from the influences of others.
    深刻认识并确信自己拥有独立做出健康生活方式抉择的自决权利与行动能力，免受外界消极影响。
    physical health /ˈfɪzɪkl hɛlθ/ 身体健康 / 生理健康 p. 79
    Well-being in the physical dimension, achieved when the body is strong, fit, and free from disease.
    身体维度的良好状态，当机体强健、适应力强且免受病痛困扰时达成。
    primary prevention strategies /ˈpraɪməri prɪˈvɛnʃən ˈstrætədʒiz/ 一级预防策略 p. 87
    Strategies that are aimed at preventing a disease or illness by reducing its risk factors.
    旨在通过降低已知危险因素来直接阻断疾病发生的根本性防范措施（如接种疫苗、改善营养）。
    prognosis /prɒɡˈnəʊsɪs/ 预后 p. 88
    The expected course of recovery, which may range from full recovery to death, based on the usual outcome of the illness.
    基于某种疾病的典型转归规律，对病情未来发展演变以及恢复前景（从完全康复到死亡）的医学预测。
    psychosocial health /ˌsaɪkəʊˈsəʊʃəl hɛlθ/ 心理社会健康 p. 79
    Well-being in the social, emotional, intellectual, and spiritual dimensions of one's life.
    个体在社交、情绪、智力与精神等非生理维度的良好适应与福祉状态。
    social health /ˈsəʊʃəl hɛlθ/ 社交健康 p. 80
    Well-being in the social dimension, achieved when people have stable and satisfying relationships.
    社交维度的良好状态，通过与家庭、朋友及社群建立稳定、互相支持且令人满意的亲密关系而达成。
    social support system /ˈsəʊʃəl səˈpɔːt ˈsɪstɪm/ 社会支持系统 p. 80
    An informal group of people who help each other or others outside the group.
    一个由家人、朋友、邻里或社团构成的非正式互助网络，在成员面临生活危机时提供物质与情感依靠。
    spiritual health /ˈspɪrɪtʃuəl hɛlθ/ 精神健康 p. 80
    Well-being in the spiritual dimension achieved through the belief in a purpose greater than the self.
    精神维度的良好状态，通过坚信生命具有超越自我的崇高意义、使命感及对是非伦理的清醒理解而达成。
    stigma /ˈstɪɡmə/ 社会污名 / 偏见病耻感 p. 91
    Social shame associated with a particular circumstance, quality, or person that causes one to feel shame or embarrassment—for example, the stigma of being fired from a job.
    与某种特定境遇、生理缺陷或特定人群相关联的社会性耻辱烙印，导致当事人产生深重的自卑、内疚或社交回避。
    wellness /ˈwɛlnɪs/ 安康 / 整体健康境界 p. 85
    The achievement of the best health possible in all dimensions of one's life.
    在生命全部维度中所达成的最佳可能健康平衡状态与积极生活追求。
