    Anatomy of Falling: Why Instinctive Catching Fails

    跌倒力学图解：为何徒手硬拉硬拽会导致更致命伤害

    FIGURE 15.23 illustrates the three sequential mechanics of safely easing a falling client: A: Bring the client close to your body to unify centers of gravity and prevent facial or thoracic impact. B: Move your forward leg so the client's buttocks rest securely on your thigh, converting vertical acceleration into controlled friction. C: Lower the client smoothly to the floor by bending at hips and knees, shielding the cranium and cervical spine from impact.

    图 15.23 直观展示了协助跌倒案主顺势滑移落地的三步力学闭环： 图 A：以闪电般速度将失衡案主拉拢并紧贴操作者胸腹躯干，使双方重心合二为一，消除案主胸面部向前砸向地面的动能； 图 B：前腿跨步切入，使案主臀部稳稳落在操作者大腿股四头肌上，将垂直自由落体冲力彻底转化为受控的斜向摩擦支撑； 图 C：操作者通过深屈髋关节与膝关节缓慢下沉身躯，引导案主顺着大腿滑降至地面，双臂始终牢牢托举案主头颈部避免撞击地板。

    Falls: Causes and Instinctive Hazards

    跌倒诱发成因与本能抗拒带来的二次致命损伤

    A client may start to fall when standing or walking. If the client is weak, light-headed, or dizzy, fainting may occur. Falling may be caused by slipping or sliding on spills, waxed floors, or throw rugs or by wearing improper shoes (see Chapter 20).

    服务对象在站立或迈步行走中可能随时发生意外跌倒。当案主极度虚弱、突发眩晕或眼前发黑时，极易发生脑缺血晕厥而瞬间失控倒地。地面积水、油渍、刚打蜡的光滑地面、未固定的活动小地毯或穿戴缺乏防滑鞋底的拖鞋，均是诱发滑倒跌倒的高危外因（详见第 20 章）。

    When a client is falling, the support worker's instinct is to try to prevent the fall. However, trying to prevent a fall could cause greater harm. You could injure yourself and the client as you twist and strain to stop the fall. Or you could lose your balance, and both you and the client could fall, causing head, hip, and knee injuries to occur.

    当案主开始失衡下坠时，人类未经训练的第一本能反应往往是使出全力生拉硬拽试图“阻止跌倒”。然而，在物理力学上试图徒手硬抗一个下坠的成年人体自重，会招致毁灭性后果！工作人员会因剧烈扭转躯干导致腰椎骨折脱位或腰背肌严重撕脱；更为致命的是，剧烈拉扯会导致双方彻底丧失重心，双双以极高动能重重砸向硬质地面，引发案主发生颅脑破裂脑出血、股骨颈骨折及髋部粉碎性骨折等致命惨剧！

    p. 275

    Instead, if a client starts to fall, ease the client to the floor. By doing so, you control the direction of the fall and also protect the client's head (see __ABBR_16__15.23 on page 274). Your response after the fall will depend on whether you work in a facility with help readily available or in a private home, where you will likely be working alone (see the Focus on Home Care: When a Client Falls box).

    因此，唯一符合现代护理科学与力学法则的应对策略是：顺势而为，引导滑降！通过将案主顺腿滑引至地面，不仅完全掌控了下坠的方向与速度，更绝对保护了案主脆弱的颅脑与颈椎（图 15.23）。

    If a client falls in a facility, do not move the client or allow the client to get u__ABBR_7__ Remain calm, and reassure the client. Stay with the client and do not move the client. Call for the charge nurse to check the client for injuries, and, later, complete an incident report, as required by facility policy.

    跌倒发生后的临床处置策略，取决于工作场所的性质：在机构内部，有专业护士团队随时待命；而在私人居家照护环境中，支持工作者通常是现场唯一的专业照料者（详见专栏“居家照护聚焦：当案主跌倒时”）。在养老院或医院等机构内，案主跌倒后绝对严禁擅自拉扯扶起，亦绝不可允许案主自主挣扎站立！操作者应保持镇定，温和轻语安抚长者，寸步不离守护在案主身边，大声呼唤责任护士前来执行系统性骨骼与神经外科查体，并在后续按机构规程如实完成意外事故呈报。

    FOCUS ON HOME CARE: When a Client Falls

    居家照护聚焦：案主跌倒后的紧急处置与协助起立标准流程
    When working in a private home, you will not have a nurse present to help you if a client falls. Be aware of any procedures required by your employer in the case of a fall. Use the following as a guide.
    If a client starts to fall, ease them to the floor (see Helping the Falling Client). After the fall, check for the following signs:
    • Pain or tenderness
    • Swelling or bruising
    • Inability to move a limb or difficulty moving a limb
    • Bleeding
    • Client report of having felt or heard a bone snap or pop
    If you observe ANY of the above, or if you suspect the client has a head, neck, or back injury, DO NOT move the client. Call 9-1-1 and then your supervisor for help. Keep the client warm and calm, and stay with the client until help arrives.
    If the client is unhurt and is able to assist, help them up using the chair method:
    1. Place a sturdy chair beside the client.
    2. Support hips and assist client into a kneeling position, facing the chair.
    3. Have the client rest their forearms on the seat of the chair.
    4. Tell the client to lift one knee and place that foot flat on the floor to form a weight-bearing lever.
    5. On the count of three, help the client push up, stand, and pivot into the chair.
    6. Once the client is in the chair, let them rest before assisting them up again. Report the fall and complete an incident report.
    在私人居家环境中执业时，现场没有值班护士可以随时协助。支持工作者必须熟稔掌握雇主对居家跌倒的应急规程。
    一旦案主失足，迅速顺势滑引至地面护卫其头部。着地后立即系统筛查以下危急警讯：
    • 剧烈自发性疼痛或局部按压剧痛；
    • 局部迅速隆起肿胀、皮下青紫瘀斑或血肿；
    • 肢体无法自主活动、关节活动度丧失或呈异常外旋缩短畸形；
    • 创口活动性出血；
    • 案主自述倒地瞬间“听到或感觉到骨头清脆地断裂或弹响一声”。
    若观察到上述任何一项指征，或高度怀疑案主伤及头部、颈椎或腰背部脊椎，绝对严禁触动移动案主！立即拨打 9-1-1 急救电话，随后通报主管护士；为案主覆盖毛毯保暖防休克，柔声安抚，寸步不离陪伴至急救人员到场。
    若且唯若案主神志完全清醒、全身毫无任何疼痛创伤且自身具备辅助发力能力时，方可采用“稳固座椅阶梯法”协助其复位起立：
    1. 在案主身侧放置一张带扶手的稳重椅子；
    2. 托扶案主髋骨，协助其调整姿态为面向椅子的双膝着地跪姿；
    3. 嘱案主将双侧前臂稳稳搭在椅子座垫面上；
    4. 指导案主屈起健侧膝关节，将该侧脚掌平平踏在坚实地面上形成有力的蹬地力臂；
    5. 口数“一、二、三”，协助案主双手下压椅面同时健腿发力蹬起站立，并旋转 90° 稳稳坐入椅子中；
    6. 让案主在椅子上充分静息平复，严密观察脉搏与呼吸；立即向主管汇报并填写正式事故报告。
    p. 276

    Walking Aids

    助行辅具（Walking Aids）体系与物理治疗处方原则

    Walking aids support the body and are ordered by the physician, nurse, or physiotherapist. The type ordered depends on the client's physical condition, the amount of support needed, and the type of disability.

    助行辅具（Walking aids）是一类用于分担躯体自重负荷、扩大支撑基底并维持平衡的专业康复器具。助行辅具的选型必须由开业医师、注册护士或物理治疗师开具医嘱处方。辅具的具体型号与配置取决于案主的全身肌能状况、平衡平衡觉受损程度、所需减重的百分比以及原发性残疾的类型。

    Crutches

    拐杖类型：前臂加拿大拐（Lofstrand）与腋下拐杖（Axillary）

    Crutches are used when the client cannot use one leg or when one or both legs need to gain strength. Some clients with permanent leg weakness use crutches, usually Lofstrand crutches (__ABBR_16__15.24), which are made of met__ABBR_13__ A metal band fits around the forearm.

    拐杖（Crutches）主要适用于单侧下肢完全无法负重，或一侧/双侧下肢需要渐进性肌力重建康复的群体。

    Axillary crutches, made of wood or metal, extend from the underarm (axilla) to the ground (__ABBR_16__15.25). A regulated health care provider teaches the client to use crutches safely.

    部分伴有永久性下肢瘫痪或无力的案主长期依赖拐杖，最常用的是金属制成的前臂加拿大拐杖（Lofstrand crutches，图 15.24），其上端设有套贴在前臂上的半圆形金属箍圈。腋下拐杖（Axillary crutches）通常由优质硬木或轻质铝合金制成，从腋窝下方直接延伸至地面（图 15.25）。

    A client who needs crutches must learn to walk, climb upstairs and climb downstairs, and sit and stand using the crutches. Safety is important, as the client using crutches is at risk for falls. Follow these safety measures:

    必须由持牌物理治疗师亲自指导案主掌握拐杖的行进、上下楼梯、从椅子起立及坐下的安全动力学。使用拐杖的长者面临极高的滑脱与跌倒风险，支持工作者必须严密落实以下安全检查法则：

    • • Check the crutch tips. Report worn or torn crutch tips to your supervisor, and replace them according to policy. If the tips are wet, dry them thoroughly with a towel or paper towels.
      检查拐杖防滑底脚套：橡胶底套是与地面产生摩擦力的唯一支点。若底套磨平、出现裂口或橡胶老化硬化，必须立即向主管汇报并更换新品！若脚套沾有水渍或油污，必须使用毛巾彻底擦拭干透。
    • • Check crutches for flaws—wooden crutches for cracks and metal crutches for bends. All bolts must be tight and fully engaged.
      结构力学与坚固度全面体检：检查木质拐杖是否存在纵向隐裂；金属拐杖有无机械弯曲疲劳。所有高度调节螺栓与紧固螺母必须处于绝对旋紧闭锁状态，严防在承重时突然脱栓崩塌。
    • • Make sure the client wears well-fitted, flat, nonskid street shoes. Loose clothing may get caught between crutches and underarms or block the person's view of the feet and tips.
      穿着规范：案主必须穿戴合脚、平底且抓地力极强的防滑鞋履。严禁穿戴拖鞋！确保案主衣裤修身合体，肥大宽松的衣物极易绞入腋窝与拐杖扶手之间，或下垂遮挡案主视线造成严重绊跌。
    • • Practise safety measures to prevent falls (see Chapter 20). Keep crutches within reach of the client when not in use.
      环境防摔保障：清除地面一切杂物与水渍；当案主在椅子或床上静坐休养时，拐杖必须放置于其触手可及之处，避免案主因探身取拐而从座位跌落。

    Canes

    手杖类型：单足手杖与四足手杖（Quad Cane）规范使用

    Canes are used to help support a side of the body that is unsteady or weak, and to provide balance. Single-tip and four-point (quad) canes (__ABBR_16__15.26) are available. A cane is held on the strong (unaffected) side of the body. (For example, if the left leg is weak, the cane is held in the right hand.) Four-point canes give more support than single-tip canes do but are harder to move.

    手杖（Canes）用于为一侧无力、步态虚浮或平衡不稳的身体提供侧向支撑与平衡代偿。临床常用单足手杖（Single-tip cane）与四足手杖（Quad cane，图 15.26）。手杖持握铁律：手杖必须始终由身体健侧（未受损/强壮侧）手部握持！

    The cane tip should be placed about 15 to 25 cm (6 to 10 in.) to the side of the foot and about 15 to 25 cm (6 to 10 in.) in front of the foot on the unaffected side. The grip is level with the hi__ABBR_7__ The person walks as follows: 1. The cane is moved forward 15 to 25 cm (6 to 10 in.) (__ABBR_16__15.27, A).

    （例如：若案主左下肢中风偏瘫无力，手杖必须绝对握在右手！）。

    2. The affected leg (opposite the cane) is moved forward even with the cane (__ABBR_16__15.27, B). 3. The unaffected leg is brought forward and ahead of the cane and the affected leg (__ABBR_16__15.27, C).

    四足手杖因底部拥有宽阔的矩形支架能够提供极强的稳固支撑力，但自身相对笨重且移动步频较慢。尺寸与初始摆放位：手杖手柄高度应与案主髋骨大转子水平齐平（手臂自然微曲约 15° 至 30°）。杖尖着地点应位于健侧足部外侧约 15 至 25 厘米、前方约 15 至 25 厘米处。标准手杖行进三步法步态分解（图 15.27）： 第 1 步：手杖首先向前推进 15 至 25 厘米，橡胶底套平稳着地建立前置受力支点（图 A）； 第 2 步：迈出位于手杖对侧的患肢（受累腿），向前移动直至与手杖处于同一水平线齐平（图 B）； 第 3 步：迈出位于手杖同侧的健肢（健康腿），向前跨越手杖与患腿，成为新的行进领先点（图 C）。

    p. 277

    Walkers

    助行架（Walkers）四大支点力学与行进规范

    A walker is a four-point walking aid (__ABBR_16__15.28). It gives more support than a cane does. Most people feel safer and more secure with a walker than with a cane.

    助行架（Walker）是一种具备四个地面接力支点的全包围立体式助行器（图 15.28）。它所提供的承托面积与稳定性远远凌驾于任何手杖之上。

    There are different kinds of walkers. The standard walker is picked up and moved about 15 to 20 cm (6 to 8 in.) in front of the client. The client then moves the affected leg and foot and then the unaffected leg and foot up to the walker (__ABBR_16__15.29, A and B).

    对于伴有双侧下肢无力、严重躯干共济失调或跌倒恐惧症的长者而言，助行架能赋予其最顶级的安全感与自信。助行架主要分为两大类： 1. 标准固定式助行架（Standard walker）：整体无轮子，需案主双手同时提起架子，平稳向前推移约 15 至 20 厘米使四脚稳稳落地，随后案主首先迈动患侧下肢步入架内，紧接着迈动健侧下肢跟进齐平（图 15.29 A 与 B）； 2. 滚轮助行车（Wheeled walker / Rollator）：前两脚装有轮子，后两脚配置橡胶防滑脚套或手刹制动系统（图 15.30）。

    A wheeled walker (also called a rollator) has wheels on the front legs and rubber tips on the back legs (__ABBR_16__15.30 on page 278). The client pushes the walker ahead about 15 to 20 cm (6 to 8 in.) and then walks up to it. The rubber tips on the back legs prevent the walker from rolling away.

    案主无需费力提起架子，只需平稳向前推移 15 至 20 厘米，随后再举步向前走入车框内。后腿的防滑橡胶底套或下压自锁装置能够有效防止助行车在案主站立倚靠时意外向前滑脱失控。

    p. 278

    Braces and Orthotics

    矫形支具（Braces / Orthotics）与局部皮肤压疮巡查防护

    Wheeled walkers often have a padded seat in the front which allows the client to sit and rest when required. Baskets, pouches, and trays can be attached to walkers (see __ABBR_16__15.28). The attachment is used to carry needed items. These help the client to be more independent and not have to rely on others.

    现代滚轮助行车前方通常集成有翻转式软垫座椅，使体力不支的长者在走廊中途随时能够坐下休养。车身可挂载专用储物挂篮、拉链布袋及平整托盘（图 15.28）。储物配件使长者能够自主携带眼镜、水杯或随身物品，极大增强了日常独立性，更重要的是彻底解放了长者的双手，确保其双手随时能百分之百牢固握持手柄！

    The attachment also keeps the hands free to grip the walker securely. The client uses the walker for support when moving from a standing to a sitting position. Assist clients with walkers, as needed (BOX 15.4). A brace (orthotic) is an apparatus—metal, plastic, or leather—worn to support or align affected body parts or to prevent or correct problems with the musculoskeletal system (see Chapters 32 and 33).

    案主在站立和入座转换时同样需要助行架的稳定支承（详见专栏 15.4）。支具与矫形器（Braces / Orthotics）： 支具是由硬质高分子塑料、轻质合金或特制皮革制成的外固定医疗器械，用于支撑或对齐无力偏瘫的身体部位，阻断关节异常活动并纠正骨骼肌肉畸形（图 15.31）。踝足矫形器（Ankle-Foot Orthosis, AFO，图 15.32）采用 L 形硬塑构型，预先嵌入案主鞋垫内部，将瘫痪下垂的足部穿入并将后跟紧密贴合到底，通过魔术贴绑带牢固固定在小腿骨迎面骨上，强制维持踝关节处于 90° 中立位，彻底根治足下垂拖地迈步困难。高风险皮肤完整性防护：支具直接紧贴皮肤并对踝骨、跟腱、腓骨头及膝关节骨突部位施加持续性剪切与压迫。

    A brace is applied over the ankle, knee, or back (__ABBR_16__15.31). An ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) is positioned in the shoe (__ABBR_16__15.32); then the foot is inserted, and the device is secured in place with a Velcro stra__ABBR_7__ Skin and bony points under the braces should be kept clean and dry to prevent skin breakdown. Report redness or signs of skin breakdown and any complaints of pain or discomfort. In facilities, the nurse assesses the skin under braces during every shift. The care plan tells you when to apply and remove a brace.

    受压区域皮肤必须始终保持绝对清洁与干燥，谨防破溃发炎！一旦发现受压处皮肤发红、发白、压疮先兆或案主主诉剧烈局部夹痛，必须立即向主管护士呈报！在养老照护机构中，注册护士必须在每班查房时对支具下的皮肤实施全面专业评估。个性化护理计划会明文严格规定每天佩戴与解开支具的具体时间表。

    p. 279

    BOX 15.4: Helping Clients With Walkers to Sit and Stand

    专栏 15.4：使用助行架案主入座轮椅、床边与起立防倾覆安全规程
    Helping the Client Sit on a Chair, Wheelchair, or Toilet:
    • Lock the wheels of the wheelchair.
    • Ask the client to stand with their back to the chair, wheelchair, or toilet.
    • Ask the client to back up with the walker until their knees (or backs of legs) touch the seat.
    • Ask the client to take one hand off the walker and reach back to grasp the armrest or grab bar. Then reach with the other hand.
    • Help the client slowly sit down. The buttocks should be at the back of the seat.
    • If armrests or grab bars are not available, support the client as they sit down. (Use a transfer belt if the client is weak or unsteady.)
    • Move the walker away from the client so it does not block movement or cause tipping.

    Helping the Client Sit on a Bed:
    • Use a transfer belt if client is weak. Raise head of bed to sitting position.
    • Ask client to stand with back to bed near the middle.
    • Back up with walker until knees touch the bed mattress.
    • Ask client to reach for the bed with one hand, then the other, and assist client to sit down slowly.

    Helping the Client Move From Sitting to Standing:
    • Place the walker directly in front of client where they can reach it with ease.
    • Let client position the walker; ask client to scoot to the edge of the seat or bed.
    • Help client rise to a standing position, as needed.
    • CRITICAL SAFETY RULE: DO NOT let the client pull themselves up with the walker! The walker will tip backward and cause a severe fall. The client MUST push down on the mattress or chair armrests with both hands, gain footing and balance, and THEN transfer their hands to the walker grips.
    协助使用助行架案主坐入普通椅子、轮椅或马桶：
    • 轮椅双侧刹车制动器必须全部牢固锁死！
    • 指导案主背对椅子、轮椅或座便器站立；
    • 引导案主稳妥操纵助行架缓慢向后倒退，直至双腿后侧（膝窝或小腿后侧）切实触碰到座椅边缘；
    • 嘱案主松开一只手脱离助行架手柄，向后伸展去牢牢抓握椅子扶手或墙壁安全抓杆；紧接着另一只手同样向后扶稳另一侧扶手；
    • 协助案主弯屈膝盖平稳缓慢入座，确保臀部饱满紧贴椅背最深处；
    • 若座椅无扶手，支持工作者必须双手握紧其移位带，以优良身体力学托扶其下沉入座；
    • 将助行架移至案主身侧安全区域，防止阻碍其双腿或在探身时意外绊倒。

    协助案主平稳坐入病床：
    • 虚弱案主规范佩戴移位带；预先将床头摇升至半坐卧位；
    • 案主背对病床中段站立，倒退迈步直至双膝后弯触碰到床垫边缘；
    • 案主双手依次向后支撑在坚实床垫面上，支持工作者屈膝协助其平缓坐上床沿。

    协助案主由坐姿发力站立（生命安全禁令）：
    • 将助行架摆放在案主正前方触手可及之处；
    • 引导案主向前挪动身体至座椅或床沿边缘，双脚向后微收平踏地面；
    • 致命力学安全铁律（绝对禁止）：严禁允许案主抓住助行架手柄借力把自己向上“拽拉”起立！助行架上部受向后拉力会瞬间向后翻覆砸在长者身上，诱发灾难性跌倒！案主双手必须用力向下推压床垫或椅子坚固扶手，依靠下肢蹬地与双臂下推将自身推立起来，完全站稳并找回平衡后，方可将双手依次转移握持到助行架手柄上！
    p. 280

    CHAPTER REVIEW: KEY POINTS

    第 15 章全真核心知识点权威总结回顾
    • • Being active is important for physical and mental well-being. Inactivity, whether mild or severe, affects not only the normal functions of all body systems but also the client's mental sense of well-being.
      保持机体活动对身体与心理健康至关重要。无论是轻度还是重度缺乏活动，不仅会破坏全身所有生理系统的正常功能，更会直接削弱案主的心理健康感与生命尊严。
    • • Bed rest is ordered by a physician to reduce physical activity, reduce pain, encourage rest, regain strength, promote healing, or a combination of these.
      卧床休息是由医师开具的医疗医嘱，旨在限制体力消耗、缓解剧烈疼痛、促进入睡休养、蓄积身体力量、促进创面与疾病愈合，或达到上述多重目标的综合疗效。
    • • Complications of bed rest are contractures, atrophy, orthostatic hypotension, and syncope, which can become permanent without timely intervention.
      长期卧床的典型严重并发症包括关节挛缩、肌肉萎缩、体位性低血压和晕厥（昏厥）；若缺乏及时规范的干预，挛缩等肌骨畸形将变为不可逆的永久性致残。
    • • A support worker must keep in mind important safety measures when moving a client from a lying position to sitting, from sitting to standing, and from standing to walking, and while using walking aids.
      支持工作者必须牢固树立阶梯式过渡安全意识：从平卧到床边端坐、从坐位到站立、从站立到行走及使用助行辅具的每个阶段，必须严密防范体位性低血压与跌倒发生。
    • • Your role as a support worker may include providing range-of-motion exercises to your client to reduce the effects of bed rest and to maintain or improve the mobility of joints.
      支持工作者的职业职责包括依据护理计划为案主提供专业关节活动度（ROM）训练，最大化抵消卧床负面损伤，维护并改善骨骼关节的屈伸活动机能。
    • • The care plan and the supervisor or physiotherapist will give you instructions for the exercises; never force a joint beyond resistance or pain.
      护理计划、主管护士或物理治疗师会明确下达训练关节与频次指令；在操作中严禁强行将关节推过阻力点或达到引起案主疼痛的极值。
    • • If your client starts to fall while walking, you must protect your client and yourself from injury by easing the client safely down your leg to the floor.
      若服务对象在步行中突然失控跌倒，切忌本能硬抗拉扯，必须立即扩大自身支撑面，将案主收拢贴近躯干，顺势顺着操作者的大腿轻柔滑移降至地面以护卫头部。
    • • Walking aids include crutches, canes, walkers, and wheeled rollators. Do not adjust any walking aids without direction from your supervisor.
      助行辅具包括腋下/加拿大拐杖、单足/四足手杖、标准助行架及滚轮助行车；未经专业主管或理疗师评估指令，支持工作者严禁擅自调整任何助行辅具的高度与螺栓。

    CRITICAL THINKING IN PRACTICE

    临床批判性思维修炼：双小时高频 ROM 训练的日程融合与漏训后果

    A client's care plan instructs the staff to perform ROM exercises on the client's right arm and leg every 2 hours. How could these exercises be done? What can happen if they are not performed effectively and often enough?

    【临床批判性思维修炼】案主的个性化护理计划明确指示工作人员：必须每隔 2 小时对案主的右侧上肢与下肢执行一次完整的关节活动度（ROM）训练。这项操作应当如何科学高效地融入日常照护节奏中？如果工作人员因工作繁忙未有效执行或频次不足，会对案主造成怎样无法挽回的生理病理后果？

    Clinical Analysis & Protocol: 1. Integration into Daily Care: ROM exercises can be seamlessly integrated with scheduled repositioning rounds (which must occur at least every 2 hours), after incontinence care, or during dressing/bathing activities.

    【专家临床思维精析与实务应对】： 1. 融入日常护理节律：每 2 小时的 ROM 训练应当与机构强制执行的“每 2 小时翻身与体位重置（Repositioning）”轮转机制无缝捆绑。在协助案主更换失禁卧具、擦浴更衣或翻身垫枕时，同步开展患侧上肢与下肢各关节的屈伸回旋。

    Communicating with the client, playing preferred relaxing music, and warming up the joints can ensure compliance and comfort. 2.

    操作前营造舒缓氛围，结合轻柔背景音乐，将枯燥的训练转化为高质量的身心互动。

    Pathological Consequences of Neglect: Muscle contractures can begin forming in as little as 48 to 72 hours in immobile joints. Skipping or rushing through ROM causes muscle fibres to shorten, tendons to fibrose, and cartilage to degenerate. The joint becomes permanently frozen into an abnormal flexion posture (__ABBR_0__, footdrop, clenched fist, elbow flexion contracture), causing permanent deformity, intractable pain, severe hygiene challenges in skin folds, and total loss of independent function.

    2. 忽视训练的致命后果：对于瘫痪或失能肢体，肌肉与关节在缺乏活动后，短短 48 至 72 小时内即可启动纤维化挛缩进程！若未达到有效频次与深度，肌纤维将发生不可逆短缩，关节周围韧带钙化固着，最终恶化为永久性骨骼关节畸形（如严重马蹄内翻足垂足症、鹰爪指指屈挛缩、肘关节强直等）。这不仅造成永久残疾与顽固性牵拉剧痛，还会因掌心与腹股沟等皮肤皱褶无法展开清洁而滋生深度破溃感染，造成不可逆的医疗灾难。

    Chapter 15 Practice Exam · Pages 280–281 Mobility Exam
    KNOWLEDGE CHECK · INTERACTIVE PRACTICE

    第 15 章全真自测复习题与详尽职业精解

    原版 14 道标准自测题（Pages 280–281，包含 9 道核心单项选择题 Q1–Q9，与 5 道正误判断题 Q10–Q14，全面涵盖卧床医嘱生理目的、足托板与转子卷防畸形力学、被动 ROM 操作主体与安全红线、拐杖/手杖/助行架三步法步态分解、跌倒顺势滑移保护以及支具骨突压疮筛查）。选项设置双向兼容类名 quiz-opt eq-opt，点击选项即时验证正误，并附教材第 281 页原版权威官方答案及临床深度精解。

    QUESTION 01 待作答
    Ms. Porter is on bed rest. Which statement is true?
    【单项选择题】波特女士因病遵医嘱处于卧床休息（Bed rest）状态。关于卧床休息的临床陈述，以下哪一项是完全正确的？
    A
    She has orthostatic hypotension.
    她必然已经患上了体位性低血压
    B
    Bed rest helps reduce pain and promotes healing.
    卧床休息有助于减少身体耗能、缓解疼痛并促进机体组织愈合
    C
    Everything will be done for her.
    必须由护理人员包办替她完成所有一切日常活动
    D
    Bed rest is not the cause of contractures.
    卧床休息绝不可能会诱发关节挛缩
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is B. Textbook page 260 explicitly states that bed rest is ordered by a physician to reduce physical activity, reduce pain, encourage rest, regain strength, and promote healing. It is not an order to rob the client of all independence (C is false), and immobility from bed rest is a primary cause of contractures (D is false).
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：B。教材第 260 页明确指出：医师开具卧床医嘱的核心治疗目的是限制体力消耗、减轻疼痛、促进入睡休养、蓄积体能并加速创面与疾病愈合。卧床绝不意味着剥夺案主残留的主动能力（C 错误）；长期卧床制动恰恰是诱发关节挛缩的核心诱因（D 错误）。
    QUESTION 02 待作答
    Which helps prevent permanent plantar flexion?
    【单项选择题】在临床体位与支撑辅具管理中，以下哪一种装备能够有效预防永久性足跖屈（足下垂/垂足症）的发生？
    A
    Bed boards
    床板（Bed boards）
    B
    A footboard
    足托板（Footboard）
    C
    Trochanter rolls
    转子卷（Trochanter rolls）
    D
    Hand rolls
    手卷握把（Hand rolls）
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is B. Textbook page 263 confirms that footboards are placed at the foot of mattresses so that the soles of the feet are flush against it, maintaining the feet in normal anatomic alignment and preventing plantar flexion, which can lead to permanent footdrop.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：B。教材第 263 页明确指出：足托板（Footboard）垂直安装于床尾床垫上，案主双足底平整紧贴板面，使踝关节保持 90° 中立位，阻断足部受重力牵拉下垂，从根源上杜绝永久性足下垂（Footdrop）。
    QUESTION 03 待作答
    Which prevents the hip from turning outward?
    【单项选择题】为了防止仰卧位案主的髋关节与大腿发生异常向外旋展（外旋/External rotation），应当使用的专业体位辅具是：
    A
    Bed boards
    床板（Bed boards）
    B
    A footboard
    足托板（Footboard）
    C
    A trochanter roll
    转子卷（Trochanter roll）
    D
    A leg brace
    腿部支具（Leg brace）
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is C. Textbook page 263 states that trochanter rolls prevent the hips and legs from turning outward (external rotation). They are made by rolling up folded sheets or towels and tucking them alongside the client from hip to knee.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：C。教材第 263 页规定：转子卷（Trochanter roll）由床单或毛巾紧密卷制而成，垫塞于案主髋骨大转子至膝关节外侧，专门阻挡股骨头与髋关节向外侧滑落旋转（外旋），维持下肢中立对线。
    QUESTION 04 待作答
    A contracture is:
    【单项选择题】在医学康复与长期照护领域，对“关节挛缩（Contracture）”的标准病理学定义是：
    A
    The loss of muscle strength as a result of inactivity
    因长期缺乏活动而导致的肌肉力量减退
    B
    The lack of joint mobility caused by the shortening of a muscle
    因肌肉异常短缩纤维化而导致的关节活动度丧失与永久畸形
    C
    A decrease in the size of a muscle
    肌纤维体积与横截面积的病理性缩小
    D
    A blood clot in the vascular system
    深静脉血管系统中形成的血液凝块（血栓）
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is B. Textbook page 261 defines a contracture as the lack of joint mobility caused by the abnormal shortening of a muscle, resulting in a permanent deformity. Muscle strength loss is weakness, muscle size decrease is atrophy (C), and blood clot is thrombus (D).
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：B。教材第 261 页明确界定：关节挛缩（Contracture）是指由于肌肉异常短缩引起关节丧失活动机能并导致永久性关节畸形固着。肌纤维变小属于肌肉萎缩（Atrophy，选项 C），血管内血块属于血栓（Thrombi，选项 D）。
    QUESTION 05 待作答
    Passive range-of-motion (ROM) exercises are performed by:
    【单项选择题】被动关节活动度训练（Passive ROM exercises）在临床实操中的实施主体是：
    A
    The client independently
    由案主本人完全自主独立完成
    B
    A health care team member (or caregiver)
    由医疗护理团队成员（或照护工作者）双手施加外力完成
    C
    The client with the assistance of someone else
    由案主自身发力并在他人协助下共同完成
    D
    The client with the use of a trapeze
    由案主借助床上悬吊提臂架拉动完成
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is B. Textbook page 264 explains that passive ROM exercises involve a health care team member moving the joints of the client through their range of motion without the client actively participating in joint movement. Active-assistive is described in C, and Active is described in A.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：B。教材第 264 页指出：被动关节活动度训练（Passive ROM）是指案主完全不产生自主肌肉收缩，由护理人员用双手托扶带动其关节完成全范围屈伸与旋转。案主完全自主完成属于主动训练（A），案主发力加外力辅助属于主动辅助训练（C）。
    QUESTION 06 待作答
    ROM exercises are ordered for Ms. Porter. You should avoid doing one of the following:
    【单项选择题】主管护士为波特女士安排了关节活动度训练。支持工作者在实操过程中必须绝对避免（Avoid）出现的违规高危动作是：
    A
    Supporting the body part being exercised
    双手妥善托扶并支撑正在受训的肢体部位
    B
    Moving the joint slowly, smoothly, and gently
    以缓慢、匀速、轻柔的手法移动各关节
    C
    Forcing the joint through full range of motion
    遇到阻力时强行用力将关节扳至完全拉直极限
    D
    Exercising only the joints indicated by your supervisor
    严格仅仅训练主管与护理计划指定要求活动的关节
    标准权威答案： 选项 C
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is C. Textbook page 266 Box 15.3 emphasizes: 'Do not force a joint beyond its present range of motion or to the point of pain.' Forcing a stiffened joint causes serious soft tissue tears, joint dislocation, and muscle strain.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：C（本题选必须避免项）。教材第 266 页 Box 15.3 黄金操作铁律：严禁超越关节当前实际阻力点或达到引起疼痛的程度而强行扳动！强行外力会导致肌腱韧带撕裂、关节脱位并造成剧烈创伤性疼痛。
    QUESTION 07 待作答
    Flexion involves:
    【单项选择题】解剖学运动术语中的“屈曲（Flexion）”具体指的是肢体部位的哪一种动作形式？
    A
    Bending the body part
    使身体部位或关节发生弯曲
    B
    Straightening the body part
    使身体部位或关节拉开伸直
    C
    Moving the body part toward the midline of the body
    使身体部位朝向人体正中线靠拢
    D
    Moving the body part away from the midline of the body
    使身体部位向远离人体正中线方向移开
    标准权威答案： 选项 A
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is A. Textbook page 260 and Box 15.2 define flexion as bending a body part. Straightening is extension (B), moving toward midline is adduction (C), and moving away from midline is abduction (D).
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：A。教材第 260 页术语表及 Box 15.2 权威定义：屈曲（Flexion）是指使关节弯曲使相邻骨段角度缩小的动作。伸展为伸直（B），内收为靠近中线（C），外展为远离中线（D）。
    QUESTION 08 待作答
    You are getting a client ready to walk using a crutch. You should do the following:
    【单项选择题】在协助服务对象准备使用拐杖（Crutches）行走前，支持工作者必须严格执行的安全检查措施是：
    A
    Ensure the client wears loose clothing
    确保案主穿戴宽松肥大的衣物
    B
    Have the client wear soft slippers
    让案主穿舒适的软底平拖鞋
    C
    Get any available pair of crutches from physical therapy
    从理疗室随手拿取一副未经尺寸调节的拐杖
    D
    Ensure that the bolts on the crutches are tight
    全面检查并确保金属拐杖上的所有调节螺栓牢牢拧紧锁定
    标准权威答案： 选项 D
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is D. Textbook page 276 lists safety measures for crutches: check crutch tips, check wooden crutches for cracks and metal crutches for bends, and ensure all bolts are tight. Loose clothing (A) can catch and cause falls; slippers (B) are dangerous slip hazards; crutches must be individually fitted (C is wrong).
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：D。教材第 276 页拐杖安全检查规程明确要求：金属拐杖的所有紧固螺栓必须处于绝对拧紧闭锁状态，橡胶防滑脚套必须干燥无破损。宽松衣物（A）极易卷入腋下导致跌倒；拖鞋（B）缺乏脚后跟支撑容易滑倒；拐杖必须专人定制调准高度绝不可随意乱用（C 错误）。
    QUESTION 09 待作答
    A single-tip cane is used:
    【单项选择题】关于单足手杖（Single-tip cane）的临床持握与使用规范，以下陈述正确的是：
    A
    At waist level with an extended arm
    在腰部水平高度使用并保持手臂完全伸直
    B
    On the strong (unaffected) side of the body
    必须始终握持于案主的健侧（未受损/强壮侧）手掌中
    C
    On the weak (affected) side of the body
    始终握持于案主的患侧（无力/瘫痪侧）手掌中
    D
    On either side depending on the client's mood
    由案主根据个人喜好随意换手在左右任意一侧使用
    标准权威答案： 选项 B
    Clinical Rationale: The correct answer is B. Textbook page 276 states that a cane is held on the strong (unaffected) side of the body. For example, if the left leg is weak, the cane is held in the right hand, so that as the cane and weak leg advance together, they create a wide, stable base of support.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】标准答案：B。教材第 276 页手杖使用金科玉律：手杖必须始终由身体健侧（未受损侧）手部握持（例如左腿无力，手杖必须握在右手）。当手杖与患腿同步前移时，健侧手能与患下肢形成宽大稳定的三角形力学支撑面。
    QUESTION 10 待作答
    A single-tip cane and a four-point cane give equal support. (T / F)
    【正误判断题】单足手杖与四足手杖（Four-point quad cane）为案主提供的支撑力与平衡稳定性是完全等同的。（对 / 错）
    T
    True
    正确（True）
    F
    False
    错误（False）
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: This statement is FALSE (F). Textbook page 276 explicitly notes: 'Four-point canes give more support than single-tip canes do but are harder to move.'
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】判断：错误（False）。教材第 276 页明确指出：四足手杖（Quad cane）拥有四根触地支脚形成宽阔的四边形支撑基底，其提供的支撑与防摔稳固度显著高于单足手杖，但移动时相对沉重繁琐。
    QUESTION 11 待作答
    When a cane is used, the feet are moved first. (T / F)
    【正误判断题】在使用手杖辅助迈步行进时，案主应当首先迈动双脚向前，随后再将手杖移向前。（对 / 错）
    T
    True
    正确（True）
    F
    False
    错误（False）
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: This statement is FALSE (F). Textbook page 276 specifies the correct 3-step gait: 1. The cane is moved forward first 15 to 25 cm. 2. The affected leg is moved forward even with the cane. 3. The unaffected leg is brought forward ahead of the cane.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】判断：错误（False）。教材第 276 页规范的手杖行进步态三步法：第 1 步必须首先将手杖向前移动 15 至 25 厘米建立前沿支点；第 2 步迈出患侧肢体与手杖齐平；第 3 步迈出健侧健肢超越手杖向前推进。
    QUESTION 12 待作答
    Mr. Jameel uses a walker. First, he moves the walker in front of him. Then, he moves his feet forward. (T / F)
    【正误判断题】贾米尔先生使用标准助行架行走。首先，他将助行架推移至身前约 15 至 20 厘米处；随后，他再迈动脚步向前步入架内。（对 / 错）
    T
    True
    正确（True）
    F
    False
    错误（False）
    标准权威答案： 选项 T
    Clinical Rationale: This statement is TRUE (T). Textbook page 277 confirms that with a standard walker, the walker is moved about 15 to 20 cm in front of the client, and then the client moves the affected leg and foot, followed by the unaffected leg, up to the walker.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】判断：正确（True）。教材第 277 页明确指出标准助行架的操作步骤：首先将助行架稳稳提举前移 15 至 20 厘米使四脚平稳着地，随后案主再向前迈步进入架内，确保重心全程落在四脚框架内。
    QUESTION 13 待作答
    Mr. Jameel starts to fall. You should try to prevent the fall. (T / F)
    【正误判断题】当贾米尔先生在行走中突然重心失控下坠开始跌倒时，支持工作者应当本能地使出全力抱住他以阻止他倒下。（对 / 错）
    T
    True
    正确（True）
    F
    False
    错误（False）
    标准权威答案： 选项 F
    Clinical Rationale: This statement is FALSE (F). Textbook page 274 warns: 'When a client is falling, the support worker's instinct is to try to prevent the fall. However, trying to prevent a fall could cause greater harm.' The worker could injure their own back and both could crash violently. Instead, the worker must ease the client down their leg to the floor.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】判断：错误（False）。教材第 274 页致命警示：当案主失控跌倒时，用蛮力硬拉硬抗阻止跌倒不仅无法挽回体重冲击，反而会造成操作者急性腰肌韧带撕脱及双方双双重重跌落导致颅脑和骨盆粉碎骨折！正确做法是顺势贴靠，顺着大腿将其平稳安全滑移降至地板并保护头部。
    QUESTION 14 待作答
    A client has a brace. Bony areas need protection from skin breakdown. (T / F)
    【正误判断题】服务对象穿戴了下肢或脊柱矫形支具（Brace）。受支具压迫摩擦的骨突隆起部位需要重点防护以防皮肤破损溃烂。（对 / 错）
    T
    True
    正确（True）
    F
    False
    错误（False）
    标准权威答案： 选项 T
    Clinical Rationale: This statement is TRUE (T). Textbook page 278 states that skin and bony points under braces should be kept clean and dry to prevent skin breakdown, and must be assessed for redness, irritation, and discomfort every shift.
    临床实操解析与知识点溯源：
    【权威解析】判断：正确（True）。教材第 278 页明确指出：支具（如踝足矫形器 AFO、下肢长支具等）由硬质塑料与金属制成，其下方的踝骨、胫骨粗隆等骨突处承受长期集中剪切压力，必须保持绝对清洁干燥，每班严格巡查发红与压疮征兆。

    OBJECTIVES

    本章核心研习目标

    After reading this chapter, the learner should be able to do the following:

    完成本章节的学习与实操研训后，学习者应当能够全面达成以下各项专业知识与核心护理技能目标：

    • • Differentiate between rehabilitative care and restorative care.
      深入辨析并明确区分“康复护理（Rehabilitative Care）”与“恢复性照护（Restorative Care）”的内涵与主从界限。
    • • Describe the goals of rehabilitation and restorative care.
      系统阐述康复护理与恢复性照护的四大核心临床医疗与生活品质目标。
    • • Explain how rehabilitation involves the whole client across all health dimensions.
      详尽论述康复医疗如何贯穿案主身体、情绪、社交、智力及精神五大维度的“全人照护”。
    • • Explain the family's vital role in the rehabilitation process.
      深刻阐明家庭成员在长期康复与恢复性照护全周期中所发挥的支柱性关键作用。
    • • Explain the role of therapy, functional training, and assistive devices in rehabilitation.
      阐述物理/作业/言语疗法、功能训练及自理辅助用具在功能重构中的协同价值。
    • • Describe the various rehabilitation settings across the healthcare continuum.
      系统描述医院急性期康复病区、专科机构、长期照护院舍及社区居家照护等执业场景。
    • • Explain the role and collaboration of the multidisciplinary rehabilitation team.
      详述涵盖案主、家属、医师、护士、治疗师及支持工作者的多学科康复团队的协作机制。
    • • Describe the overall systemic and socioeconomic benefits of rehabilitation and restorative care.
      全面概括康复与恢复性照护对案主独立性赋能、减轻家庭负担及优化医疗体系成本的综合效益。

    GLOSSARY

    KEY TERMS · 本章核心专业术语表

    6 核心词汇
    英文术语 / 国际音标 中文对照 / 出处 教材标准学术释义与职业界定
    prostheses /prɑːsˈθiː.siːz/ 假体 / 假肢（单数：prosthesis） p. 289
    (singular, prosthesis) Artificial replacements for missing body parts.
    （单数形式为 prosthesis）用于替代机体缺失部位（如下肢、上肢、手部、眼球或乳房）的外观与生理功能的人工生物力学仿生替代装置。
    reablement program /riːˈeɪ.bəl.mənt ˈproʊ.ɡræm/ 赋能自立康复计划（重赋权方案） p. 293
    A program designed for individuals who do not need acute hospital care but cannot yet manage at home or are struggling in their home to regain strength, endurance, functioning, and independence.
    专门面向无需急性住院治疗、但在出院后难以独自居家生活或在家中力求恢复体力、耐力与自理机能的失能长者而设计的短期集约化社区赋能康复方案。
    rehabilitative care /ˌriː.həˈbɪl.ə.teɪ.tɪv ker/ 康复护理 p. 283
    The process of restoring a person to the highest possible level of functioning through the use of therapy, exercise, and other methods to maintain or slow the decline of functioning.
    借助多学科疗法、科学运动及适应性手段，促使经历疾病、创伤或手术的个体恢复至最高可能生理与生活机能水平，遏制机能衰退并捍卫自立尊严的综合性医疗护理过程。
    rehabilitation robotics /ˌriː.həˈbɪl.əˈteɪ.ʃən roʊˈbɑː.tɪks/ 康复机器人学 p. 285
    Robotics and technology used in rehabilitation medicine that include wheelchair biomechanics, new technologies to assess spinal structure and function, assistive robotics, and the use of virtual reality.
    应用于现代康复医学领域的先进智能机器人与工程技术，涵盖智能轮椅生物力学、脊柱力线评估系统、外骨骼智能助行机器人及虚拟现实交互康复设备。
    restorative care /rɪˈstɔːr.ə.tɪv ker/ 恢复性照护 p. 283
    Care aimed at preventing health deterioration, maintaining or improving a client's quality of life, and restoring the client to their previous functional level as much as possible.
    主要由护士与支持工作者主导开展的日常连续性照护，旨在防止健康不可逆恶化、维持并增进生命品质，并在最大限度内协助案主找回并保持既往的功能独立状态。
    virtual reality /ˈvɝː.tʃu.əl riˈæl.ə.ti/ 虚拟现实（VR） p. 285

    REHABILITATIVE CARE VERSUS RESTORATIVE CARE

    康复护理（Rehabilitative Care）与恢复性照护（Restorative Care）辨析

    Injury or health challenges can affect a person's ability to lead a productive life. For example, after a stroke, some people are unable to walk or to communicate like they once could. Those clients may benefit from rehabilitation care and restorative care services.

    严重的躯体创伤或重大疾病冲击，会深刻剥夺一个个体过上富有成效与自主尊严生活的能力。例如，脑卒中（中风）发作后，许多案主会瞬间丧失独立行走或清晰言语交流的机能。这部分群体将极大受益于专业的康复护理（Rehabilitation care）与恢复性照护（Restorative care）服务。

    People may require rehabilitative and restorative care following an acute injury or illness, or it may be part of the treatment for a lifelong disability, chronic condition or illness, or degenerative condition. Rehabilitation refers to a broad range of interventions that address the client's medical care needs, therapeutic needs, psychosocial needs, or a combination of these needs and would be part of a client's care plan. It is delivered in homes, community-based locations, long-term care homes, and hospitals.

    人们既可能在急性创伤或重症发作后需要集约化康复，康复亦是应对终身残疾、慢性进展性疾病或退行性病变长期管理的核心支柱。康复涵盖广泛的临床干预矩阵，精准回应案主的医疗需求、物理与作业治疗需求及社会心理需求。康复服务普遍开展于案主私人家居、社区日间中心、长期照护院舍及综合医院康复科病房中。

    Rehabilitative care is the process of restoring a person to the highest possible level of functioning through the use of therapy, exercise, and other methods. The aim of such care is to slow the decline of functioning or support clients in maintaining or functioning at a higher capacity to maintain their quality of life and independence.

    康复护理（Rehabilitative care）是指借助专业物理疗法、针对性机能锻炼及辅助技术，促使案主恢复至最高可能生理与生活机能水平的过程。其核心宗旨在于延缓机能衰退进程，或支持案主维持在更高的机能储备状态，以最大化捍卫其生活品质与自立尊严。

    For some clients, the goal is to return to work, while some others may work toward resuming the self-care needs and perform the activities of daily living (ADLs) that they were able to perform in the past. This type of care is usually provided by nurses, physiotherapists, physiotherapy assistants, and support workers.

    对于年轻伤患，终极目标往往是重返工作岗位（Return to work）；而对众多失能长者而言，目标则是重新掌握洗漱穿衣等日常生活自理活动（ADLs）。

    Restorative care is also aimed at preventing health deterioration and maintaining or improving a client's quality of life, but it is also aimed at restoring the client to their previous functional level whenever possible. Whereas more health care providers are on the team for a client in rehabilitative care, restorative care usually involves only the client and family, nurses, and support workers. Therapists and other professionals may be consulted as needed.

    该类照护由注册护士、物理治疗师（PT）、物理治疗助理（PTA）及支持工作者（PSW）紧密协同提供。恢复性照护（Restorative care）同样聚焦于防止健康发生继发性滑坡、维持并提升生命质量，更力求在最大限度内协助案主找回并巩固既往已恢复的自理机能。两者的核心团队配置存在清晰主从分工：康复护理通常由大型多学科医疗专家团队深度介入；而恢复性照护则高度聚焦于日常生活场景，主要由案主本人、家属、责任护士及基层支持工作者共同承担，物理治疗师等专家则按需提供顾问指导。

    GOALS OF REHABILITATIVE AND RESTORATIVE CARE

    康复与恢复性照护的四大核心临床医疗与自立目标

    Most clients largely want to reduce their reliance on others and to become more independent. The goals of rehabilitation and restorative care for any client are based on the client's condition, and may include the following:

    绝大多数服务对象内心深处都渴望摆脱对他人无休止的依赖，重获身心独立。针对任何具体个案，康复与恢复性照护方案的拟定均基于案主的病理伤情与残存机能，系统涵盖以下四大核心支柱目标：

    • • To restore function to former levels. A full restoration of function is the goal for most clients with acute or temporary conditions. For example, a healthy client with a simple leg fracture aims for full recovery.
      促使机能完全恢复至病前水平（To restore function to former levels）：对于遭遇急性暂时性创伤的大多数健康个体而言，彻底恢复伤前全部机能是最直接的目标。例如一位骨质健康的年轻长者发生单纯性下肢闭合性骨折，康复目标就是百分之百回归无痛行走与负重。
    • • To improve functional abilities. A return to former levels of functioning is not possible for some clients. Instead, they aim to improve their abilities to the best extent possible. For example, they may want to work on mobility skills or carrying out ADLs independently.
      最大化改善现有功能潜力（To improve functional abilities）：对于某些重症中风或严重截瘫案主，彻底回到病前状态在医学上已无可能；此时的目标转变为在当前解剖局限下，将残存的代偿潜能挖掘至极致。例如通过强化健侧肢体代偿，掌握轮椅独立位移或单手进食洗漱穿衣等 ADL 技能。
    • • To learn new skills. Some clients need to learn new skills to adjust to their disability or limitations. For example, Mr. Liptak's larynx was surgically removed because of cancer, and he is not able to speak anymore. His goal is to learn to communicate using, for example, sign language or electronic speech devices.
      习得全新适应性代偿技能（To learn new skills）：部分案主需要掌握前所未有的生活方式以适应终身性身体缺损。例如利普塔克先生（Mr. Liptak）因喉癌晚期接受了全喉切除手术而永久丧失发声功能，其康复核心目标就是系统研习手势手语、食管发音法或使用电子人工喉进行有效人际交流。
    • • To prevent further disability and illness. Complications that cause further disability and illness must be prevented. For example, immobility can lead to pressure ulcers or contractures, so proper skin care, exercise and activity, good alignment, and frequent repositioning are essential.
      阻断继发性二次残疾与合并症（To prevent further disability and illness）：必须动用一切临床手段掐断由制动引发的恶性循环！例如长期卧床极易并发压疮、不可逆关节挛缩与深静脉血栓，必须通过定时翻身垫枕、被动 ROM 训练与皮肤减压予以彻底防范。
    p. 284

    Individualized Rehabilitation Goals: Five Client Profiles

    个性化康复目标规划：五位不同年龄与病损案主案例分析

    Consider the rehabilitation goals of the following clients across different lifespans and clinical challenges:

    深入体悟以下五位具有代表性的服务对象，其因年龄、原发病理与生活诉求差异而展现出的鲜明康复目标：

    • • Chantal, 17, was in a car accident, which left her with hemiplegia (paralysis of one side of the body). She needs to maintain her current range of motion (ROM), adapt to a wheelchair, and perform self-care.
      尚塔尔（Chantal，17 岁）：在一场惨烈车祸中幸存，导致单侧肢体偏瘫（Hemiplegia）。其康复核心在于维持受累肢体的关节活动度（ROM）防挛缩，熟练掌握手推轮椅操控操控技巧，并攻克单侧自理独立性。
    • • Mr. Cunningham, 27, is addicted to cocaine. His goals include restoring healthy physical and psychological functions and preventing a relapse into addiction. He will learn how to avoid situations in which drugs are present, and he will be encouraged to join Narcotics Anonymous (NA).
      坎宁安先生（Mr. Cunningham，27 岁）：罹患可卡因药物成瘾。其康复重心在于系统修复受损的心身脏器功能，彻底防范复吸复发；学习识别并主动规避毒品诱惑高危社交场景，融入戒毒互助同侪组织（NA）。
    • • Mr. Khan, 49, has had a heart attack (myocardial infarction). His goal is to prevent another heart attack. His rehabilitation program should include counselling, which will recommend exercise, healthy eating, and stress management techniques.
      汗先生（Mr. Khan，49 岁）：突发急性心肌梗死（心肌梗死）。其心脏康复目标在于严防二次心梗致命复发；方案涵盖专业心肺耐力运动处方、低脂低盐地中海饮食营养指导及心理减压干预。
    • • Mr. Egri, 68, had a stroke that resulted in hemiplegia and severe speech impairment. He needs to learn communication methods and to restore function. Prevention of another stroke through medication, exercises, and a healthy diet is a goal as well. His family needs to learn how to help with his care.
      埃格里先生（Mr. Egri，68 岁）：罹患急性脑卒中并发右侧偏瘫与严重运动性失语症。其核心在于重建功能性交流通道、恢复患肢肌力，并通过规律服药与抗栓管理防范脑卒中复发；全家人同步受训掌握家庭协助技能。
    • • Mrs. Boucher, 82, fractured her hip in a fall. Her goal is to remain in her own home. She needs to restore her ability to function at former levels. She also needs to take measures to prevent another fall.
      布歇太太（Mrs. Boucher，82 岁）：跌倒导致股骨颈骨折手术。她的最高人生诉求是“继续住在自己熟悉的家中安享晚年（Aging in place）”。她需要重塑步态平衡能力以找回伤前自理水准，并全面排查居家跌倒隐患。

    FOCUS ON OLDER PERSONS: Rehabilitation Challenges

    长者照护聚焦：高龄案主康复进程迟缓机制与节奏调控法则
    Rehabilitation often takes longer for older clients than for others. Age-related changes affect healing, mobility, vision, hearing, and other functions. Older clients often have chronic health problems that slow down their recovery. They are also at risk for injuries. Because older clients do not tolerate long or fast-paced programs, their rehabilitation is usually slow.
    For clients who are too weak to perform ADLs, restorative care may involve measures that promote:
    • Self-care (adaptive feeding, grooming)
    • Elimination (bladder/bowel retraining)
    • Positioning (alignment, pressure injury prevention)
    • Mobility (assisted transfers, dangling)
    • Communication (hearing aid checks, speech pacing)
    • Cognitive function (reality orientation, memory cues)
    • Preventing unnecessary decline in function.
    相较于年轻群体，高龄长者的康复周期呈现出显著的漫长与曲折。衰老带来的生理退行性衰变波及成纤维细胞增殖、骨痂愈合速率、步态力学平衡、视力敏锐度及听觉辨析力。长者普遍伴有高血压、冠心病、糖尿病等多系统慢性合并症，显著拉长机体机能修复窗口。高龄长者骨质疏松严重，极其脆弱易伤。老年心肺脏器无法承受高强度或快节奏的高压训练，因此长者的康复进程必须遵循“小步慢跑、匀速耐受、极度耐心”的基本原则。
    对于极度衰弱长者，恢复性照护的重点在于保全基础生命尊严：• 基础自理；• 排泄机能重塑；• 防畸形体位管理；• 安全位移；• 言语沟通支持；• 认知机能维持；• 坚决阻断非必要的功能滑坡。

    Emphasis on the Whole Person

    身心社智灵：全人康复（The Whole Person）五大生命维度

    Illness and disability can affect a client's physical, emotional, social, intellectual, and spiritual health, so restorative care is aimed at the whole person. It addresses all dimensions of health, not just the physical one: • Physical health: Monitored continuously; ROM exercises prevent contractures; pain management avoids opioid misuse. • Emotional and social health: Family counselling; community re-entry. • Intellectual health: Cognition, memory, speech, organization. • Spiritual health: Pastoral counselling respecting faith.

    躯体疾病与残疾绝非孤立的局部生物学事件，它会剧烈动摇案主的心理防线、撕裂人际社交纽带、阻滞智力认知并撼动其精神生命支柱。因此，现代康复与恢复性照护必须坚定秉持“全人理念（The whole person）”，系统统筹五大核心维度： 1. 躯体健康（Physical health）：由多学科团队与家属合力持续监测生命体征与 ADL 自理能力；严格执行被动 ROM 训练以阻断挛缩；极其关键的是，科学指导案主进行非药物疼痛管理，坚决阻断对阿片类强效止痛药或酒精的病理性滥用与依赖； 2. 情绪与社交健康（Emotional & Social health）：提供家庭专业心理疏导，协助案主平稳重建社交圈并重返社区与职场； 3. 智力认知健康（Intellectual health）：系统测评思维逻辑、近期记忆、言语表达及事务规划能力，制定认知康复策略； 4. 精神信仰健康（Spiritual health）：尊重并满足案主的宗教信仰诉求，引入神职人员与心灵关怀顾问陪伴支持。

    p. 285

    REHABILITATION SETTINGS

    康复医疗与恢复性照护全链条执业场景

    BOX 16.1: Common Health Problems Requiring Rehabilitation

    专栏 16.1：临床上最常需要康复介入的重大疾病与创伤谱系
    • Acquired brain injury (traumatic and non-traumatic)
    • Alcoholism and substance use disorders
    • Amputation (upper and lower extremity)
    • Brain tumour
    • Burns (extensive thermal and chemical injuries)
    • Cerebral palsy (pediatric and adult)
    • Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
    • Mental illness (depression, schizophrenia, PTSD)
    • Myocardial infarction (heart attack)
    • Parkinson's disease
    • Spinal cord injury (paraplegia and tetraplegia)
    • Spinal cord tumour
    • Stroke (ischemic and hemorrhagic CVA)
    • Substance abuse
    • 获得性脑损伤（ABI，包括创伤性脑挫裂伤与非创伤性缺氧性脑病）
    • 酒精依赖与成瘾性精神障碍
    • 截肢术后（上肢及下肢大截肢）
    • 颅内脑部恶性与良性肿瘤
    • 大面积重度烧伤（热力及化学烧伤瘢痕挛缩期）
    • 脑性瘫痪（小儿脑瘫及成人期继发畸形）
    • 慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD，肺康复体系）
    • 重性精神障碍（抑郁症、精神分裂症、创伤后应激障碍 PTSD）
    • 急性心肌梗死（心梗术后心脏康复）
    • 帕金森病（运动迟缓与步态冻结）
    • 脊髓损伤（截瘫与高位四肢瘫）
    • 椎管内脊髓肿瘤术后
    • 脑卒中（脑梗死与脑出血中风偏瘫）
    • 药物与处方药滥用成瘾

    Hospitals: Most hospitals have dedicated rehabilitation units for inpatients and outpatients focusing on stroke, brain and spinal cord trauma, cardiac/pulmonary rehab, and complex surgical wound healing. Currently, the use of robotics in rehabilitation has been the focus of worldwide research.

    1. 综合医院康复科病区（Hospitals）：设有住院部与门诊部，重点收治脑损伤、中风偏瘫、脊髓截瘫、心肺功能衰竭及复杂糖尿病难愈性创面患者。当今世界康复科研的最前沿聚焦于康复机器人学（Rehabilitation robotics，图 16.1）。

    At the University of Alberta's Faculty of Rehabilitation, an interdisciplinary group focuses on rehabilitation robotics (__ABBR_16__16.1), researching wheelchair biomechanics, spinal assessment, assistive robotics, and virtual reality (VR) simulation environments. In the future, adaptive robotic exoskeletons in homes and clinics will be standard care.

    例如加拿大阿尔伯塔大学（University of Alberta）康复医学系跨学科科研团队，致力于研发轮椅生物力学底盘、脊柱受力传感器、外骨骼智能助行机器人以及沉浸式虚拟现实（Virtual Reality, VR）神经反馈系统。未来，家用轻量化外骨骼机器人将彻底融入社区居家康复日常。

    Specialized Facilities: Focus on specialized domains such as psychiatric disorders, trauma centers, and addiction retreat centers. Long-Term Care Facilities: Provide restorative care driven by PSWs and nurses to keep residents functioning. Community and Home Care: Home-based rehabilitation allows clients to recover in familiar surroundings, while adult day programs teach life skills, social interaction, and vocational re-entry.

    2. 专科康复医疗中心（Specialized Facilities）：深耕特定专科领域，如专科戒毒脱瘾中心、重性精神康复疗养院或工伤职业康复中心。3. 长期照护院舍（Long-term Care）：以护士与支持工作者为主导开展“恢复性照护”，保全长者自主进食与如厕机能。4. 社区居家照护与日间中心（Community & Home Care）：使长者免除住院离家之苦，在熟悉的家庭环境中重塑自理；日间照料中心则提供生活技能重塑、同侪社交与职业复训。

    FOCUS ON HOME CARE: Home Assessment for Safe Independent Living

    居家照护聚焦：出院前多学科居家无障碍安全评估规程
    After the rehabilitation team assesses the client's home (BOX 16.2), the case manager or occupational therapist discusses with the client and family any safety risks and health hazards identified. You may be asked to assist a team member to complete the assessment.
    If necessary, modifications are made to make the home environment appropriate (e.g., widening doors, installing ramps, adding grab bars). The support worker should continue to be on the lookout for any safety risks during future visits and gently suggest changes to ensure safety. Any identified hazards must be reported immediately to your supervisor.
    在案主从康复病区出院返家前，个案经理（Case Manager）与作业治疗师（OT）会亲自上门开展详尽的居家环境实地勘察（详见专栏 16.2），并与案主及家属闭门研讨所发现的隐形危险源。支持工作者常被指派协助治疗师完成现场测量与设备测试。
    根据评估结论，对住宅施行针对性无障碍改造（如门框加宽以容纳轮椅、室外台阶改建缓坡道、卫生间加装防滑安全抓杆等）。在后续的日常上门照护中，支持工作者必须保持敏锐的职业警觉，随时捕捉新出现的滑跌隐患，并第一时间通报主管护士协助整改。
    p. 286

    BOX 16.2: Rehabilitation Team Home Review for a Client Who Is Recovering From a Stroke (Part 1)

    专栏 16.2：脑卒中（中风）偏瘫案主居家无障碍环境实地全真审核清单（第一部分：室外、室内、厨房与卫浴）
    Outdoors:
    • Parking area location and distance to entrance door
    • Mailbox accessibility
    • Vehicle parking location and width of car doors for transfers
    • Ability to turn keys, open and close entrance doors
    • Necessity of ramps and handrails along walkways
    • Adequate illumination at all exterior entrances
    • Access to private or public adapted transportation; ability to operate vehicle
    • Ramp slope, width, and sidewalk surface integrity

    Indoors:
    • Removal of obstructions, throw rugs, and cords on floors
    • Presence and location of steps inside the house
    • Furniture arrangement and accessibility without blocking navigation
    • Telephone locations and emergency accessibility
    • Ability to raise and lower windows
    • Flooring materials (low-pile wall-to-wall carpeting, non-glare tile, hardwood)
    • Full wheelchair turning radius throughout corridors
    • Location of main fuse or circuit-breaker box
    • Ability to independently control thermostat and heating
    • Doorways and halls wide enough (minimum 81-91 cm / 32-36 in.) for wheelchair
    • Operational elevator in multi-story residential buildings

    Kitchen:
    • Unhindered access to stove, sink, cupboards, refrigerator, and counters
    • Lowered height of sink and prep counters; open roll-under knee space beneath sink
    • Easy-grip lever faucets operable without twisting wrist
    • Safe access to microwave oven and front-mounted stove control knobs
    • Ergonomic arrangement of utensils within easy forward reach

    Bathroom:
    • Adapted heights of sink, toilet seat, shower stall, and bathtub
    • Reachable lever-action water faucets operable with one hand
    • Adequate turning space for wheelchair or mobility devices
    • Barrier-free transfer into tub or shower (curbless roll-in stall)
    • Heavy-duty, wall-anchored grab bars beside toilet, bathtub, and inside shower

    Bedroom:
    • Ideal height of bed mattress matched to wheelchair seat for level transfers
    • Accessible closet rods, pull-down hangers, and reachable drawers
    • Safe bed transfer clearance and unblocked wheelchair turning radius
    • Proximity to the nearest adapted bathroom for nighttime elimination
    室外进出通道（Outdoors）：
    • 停车位具体位置及停车点至住宅入户大门的实际行走距离；
    • 室外信箱的高度与开启便利性；
    • 私家车停靠位置，车门开启角度与净开度是否满足轮椅无缝转移；
    • 案主单手插钥匙、旋转锁芯及推拉厚重大门的能力；
    • 室外台阶处是否急需浇筑或搭建无障碍缓坡斜道与双侧安全扶手；
    • 所有出入口走廊在夜间是否具备充足均匀的防眩采光照明；
    • 案主对无障碍公共交通或轮椅出租车的获取便利度；自身驾车能力；
    • 斜坡坡度（国际标准坡度比不小于 1:12）、净宽及人行道路面平整防滑度。

    室内通用动线（Indoors）：
    • 地面绝对彻底清除杂物堆积、散落电线及所有未固定的小块防滑地毯！
    • 住宅内部是否存在阶梯落差；具体分布位置；
    • 家具空间布局是否宽敞合理，有无阻碍助行辅具通过；
    • 室内固定电话及一键紧急呼叫铃的安装位置；
    • 案主自主开启或关闭采光窗户的能力；
    • 地面材质评估（推荐低绒紧密地毯、防滑亚光地砖或平整硬木地板）；
    • 住宅全屋动线是否具备满足轮椅 360° 原地调头的回转半径（≥150 cm）；
    • 总电源空气开关/保险丝电箱的具体位置与紧急切断便利度；
    • 案主自主调节室内恒温器（Thermostat）与暖气的能力；
    • 室内所有门廊与走廊净宽是否足够轮椅通行（净宽建议 ≥81-91 厘米）；
    • 多层公寓楼宇内是否配有稳定运行的无障碍电梯。

    厨房操作区（Kitchen）：
    • 炉灶、水槽、储物壁橱、冰箱及料理台是否处于案主轮椅端坐平视可达范围内；
    • 水槽与操作台台面是否降至适合轮椅端坐的人体工效学高度；水槽下方是否预留镂空的进深空间以便轮椅双腿滑入；
    • 水龙头是否改装为免扭转的加长单手柄扳压式阀芯；
    • 微波炉摆放高度是否合理安全；炉灶控制旋钮是否位于前方边缘（严禁伸手越过燃烧器去拧旋钮）；
    • 常用调味品及餐具是否按使用频次集中置于前沿低位抽屉内。

    卫生间卫浴区（Bathroom）：
    • 洗脸盆、座便器坐圈、淋浴房地台及浴缸的精准离地高度；
    • 案主单手触及并自如开关冷热水混合龙头阀芯的能力；
    • 卫生间内部净空间是否允许轮椅顺畅进出与 180° 旋转调头；
    • 案主自主进出浴缸或淋浴房的实际能力（极度推荐无门槛直入式淋浴房）；
    • 马桶侧方、淋浴花洒旁及浴缸内侧墙体龙骨上，是否已通过膨胀螺栓牢固锚固了专业安全防滑抓杆（Grab bars）！

    卧室起居区（Bedroom）：
    • 床垫上表面离地高度是否与轮椅座垫高度严格调平，以实现平齐水平过桥转移；
    • 衣柜挂衣杆是否改装为可下拉式液压衣架，抽屉滑轨是否轻柔顺滑；
    • 案主在床沿自主起立与回床就寝的力学稳定性；
    • 床周空间是否确保轮椅能够直接贴靠床沿并自如开出；
    • 卧室距离最近的独立无障碍卫生间之间的动线距离与夜间地脚感应照明。
    p. 287

    BOX 16.2: Rehabilitation Team Home Review for a Client Who Is Recovering From a Stroke (Part 2: Safety & Emergency Protocol)

    专栏 16.2：中风案主居家无障碍环境审核清单（第二部分：生命安全防灾与应急疏散通道）
    Safety:
    • Highly visible and reflective house number visible from street for ambulances
    • Deadbolts and locks providing security while remaining easy for client to unlock
    • Peephole or video intercom allowing client to screen visitors safely
    • Steps, porch, and entryway illuminated and sheltered from rain, ice, and snow
    • Heavy rubber-backed nonslip entrance doormats flush with threshold
    • Emergency telephone numbers (9-1-1, poison control, supervisor) posted by phones
    • Anti-scald thermostatic mixing valves limiting hot water temperature to ≤49°C
    • Childproof tamper-resistant covers on low electrical outlets
    • Functional smoke and carbon monoxide detectors on every level, tested regularly
    • Unobstructed rapid emergency egress routes out of the dwelling
    • Strict fire-safety precautions if medical oxygen is used in the home
    • Bedside access to phone, TV, emergency call pendant, and lighting controls
    • Safe clearance for space heaters (minimum 1 metre from drapery and bedding)
    • Sound cognitive judgement regarding cooking safety and stove shutdown
    • Multi-purpose dry chemical fire extinguishers in kitchen and near fireplaces
    • Safe methods for disposing of blood, bodily fluids, contaminated dressings, and sharps
    • Animal- and pest-proof outdoor garbage storage containers.
    生命安全防灾与应急疏散（Safety）：
    • 房屋门牌号码在夜间是否具备高反光涂层或专属灯光直射，确保急救救护车（EMS）在黑夜中能在第一时间内精准定位；
    • 防盗门锁与插销在提供严密安防的同时，偏瘫案主单手能否迅速扳开解锁；
    • 大门上是否装有与轮椅高度齐平的低位广角猫眼，或配有双向可视对讲监控屏；
    • 室外台阶、门廊及雨棚是否能有效阻挡雨雪冰霜聚集，杜绝结冰滑倒；
    • 入户门外是否铺设厚重防滑橡胶底垫，且边缘高度与门槛平滑过渡；
    • 9-1-1 急救电话、安省中毒控制中心及主管护士直线电话是否放大字号压塑张贴于座机旁；
    • 卫生间热水器是否加装恒温混水阀（水温绝对限制在 ≤49°C 以防烫伤烫破）；
    • 墙壁低位电源插座是否配有绝缘防触电安全保护盖；
    • 房屋每一楼层是否装有灵敏的光电感烟火灾报警器与一氧化碳探测器并按月测试；
    • 发生火灾险情时，案主从卧室及客厅快速撤离至室外开阔地的逃生通道是否毫无阻碍；
    • 若室内使用医用氧气机或氧气瓶，是否建立“严禁烟火与静电防爆”铁律；
    • 案主在床上仰卧时，床头是否伸手即可抓握手机、电视遥控器、救命呼叫挂坠及照明开关；
    • 若使用移动取暖器，是否严格与窗帘、床单被褥保持至少 1 米以上安全净距；
    • 评估案主前额叶对烹饪用火用电是否具备清晰准确的风险预判与关火记忆力；
    • 厨房及壁炉旁是否常备经过定期年检的高效干粉灭火器；
    • 案主或家属能否规范安全处置沾染血液、体液、排泄物的污染敷料与医疗锐器；
    • 室外生活垃圾桶是否具备防浣熊与害虫撬开的密封机械锁扣锁闭装置。

    THE REHABILITATION PROCESS

    康复医疗流程、周期性与全人协同

    Rehabilitation can be a short process; for example, a healthy client with a shoulder injury may need to do only a few simple exercises regularly for a few weeks until recovery is complete. However, rehabilitation is often a long, difficult process. The Case Study: Rehabilitation Following a Brain Injury box shows the rehabilitation process for a client who has experienced a serious brain injury.

    康复的临床历程具有极大的个体差异性：对于一位偶发肩关节扭伤的健康青年，可能仅需在理疗师指导下规律完成数周的被动与抗阻拉伸即可告愈；然而，对于遭遇毁灭性颅脑外伤、中风偏瘫或截瘫的案主而言，康复是一场旷日持久、布满生理痛苦与心智煎熬的漫长战役！“案例研习：杰弗里·谭严重脑损伤全周期康复”深度再现了一位严重神经创伤伤患长达数年的全人康复真实历程。

    The Rehabilitation Team

    多学科康复团队（Multidisciplinary Team）运作与案主核心地位

    Rehabilitation requires a multidisciplinary team effort. Members of the team can vary, depending on the client's needs and the setting where the rehabilitation is being conducted. The team usually includes the client, family members, physicians, nurses, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, physiotherapy assistants, support workers, and others—who all can help the client regain function and independence.

    现代康复医疗绝非任何单一专业人员能够独力完成，必须依托高度紧密协作的多学科团队（Multidisciplinary Team）。团队架构依案主伤情动态组合，其最核心成员由案主本人及家庭直系亲属奠基，吸纳神经/骨科专科医师、康复医学专家（Physiatrist）、注册护士、物理治疗师（PT）、作业治疗师（OT）、理疗助理（PTA）、言语病理学家（SLP）、心理学家、社工及一线支持工作者（PSW）。

    The team meets often to discuss the client's progress, and changes are made in the rehabilitation care plan, as needed. The client and family attend the meetings whenever possible. The importance of family involvement and support throughout the client's rehabilitation process cannot be overemphasized.

    团队定期召开多学科个案研讨会（Care conferences），依功能恢复曲线动态迭代护理计划。案主与家属全程受邀列席研讨会。家庭的深度介入与情感支柱作用，构成了康复能否最终成功的生命线！

    All aspects of rehabilitation are interconnected. For example, following a stroke, __ABBR_3__ Silva learns how to care for himself (physical health) and how to follow instructions (intellectual health), which increases his self-esteem (emotional health); family and friends visit often (social health), and his spiritual advisor visits every week (spiritual health). The rehabilitation team encourages the client to control as many aspects of care as possible—being a key member of the rehabilitation team gives the client some control.

    全人健康的五个维度在康复中紧密互锁：例如中风案主席尔瓦先生（Mr. Silva），通过重新掌握单手穿衣自理（躯体健康）与理解康复指令（智力健康），极大重塑了前额叶尊严与自我效能感（情绪健康）；亲朋好友的频繁探视与鼓励（社交健康）以及每周神职人员的心灵陪伴祈祷（精神健康），共同汇聚成了促使神经突触重塑代偿的强大内驱力。康复团队始终鼓励案主成为自身医疗计划的最高决策者，这种自主掌控感是战胜绝望的灵魂解药。

    p. 288

    CASE STUDY: Rehabilitation Following a Brain Injury (Jeffrey Than, 34)

    实战案例研习：杰弗里·谭（Jeffrey Than，34 岁）严重创伤性脑损伤（TBI）全周期多学科康复全景纪实
    Jeffrey Than, a 34-year-old high school teacher, was cycling to school when he was struck by a van. He sustained a severe blow to the cranium, traumatic brain injury (TBI), and multiple fractures. After emergency neurosurgery and orthopedic repair, he was admitted to the ICU. Because he had suffered a serious brain injury, he could not speak or recognize his family.
    After 10 days in the ICU, he was moved to the acute care unit for 2 months. Eventually, Mr. Than was transferred to the hospital's specialized rehabilitation unit, and 3 months later, he was discharged home. He received home-based and community rehabilitation for the next 6 months.
    During his long rehabilitation, Mr. Than's multidisciplinary rehabilitation team worked collaboratively with him and his family:

    • Mr. Than and his family: Made decisions regarding rehabilitation goals; actively involved in every aspect of care; learned new skills and relearned old skills.
    • Neurosurgeon & Orthopedic surgeon: Led surgical repair and managed post-surgical medical stability.
    • Nurses: Coordinated and provided nursing care at every clinical stage.
    • Specialist in rehabilitation medicine (Physiatrist): Led and coordinated the comprehensive rehabilitation program.
    • Neuropsychologists: Evaluated cognitive processing, memory, emotions, and personality changes; planned behaviour-management therapy.
    • Social workers: Arranged adult day programs, provided family crisis counselling, and coordinated funding.
    • Case manager: Coordinated the transition to home care and headed the adult day program integration.
    • Occupational therapists (OT): Assessed ADL performance; conducted pre-discharge home assessment; provided adaptive devices.
    • Physiotherapists (PT): Evaluated muscular strength, joint flexibility, and balance; used robotics and simulation technologies; taught gait mobility.
    • Physiotherapy assistants (PTA): Reinforced mobility exercises and guided assistive equipment practice.
    • Speech-language pathologist (SLP): Tested speech, receptive language, and swallowing; taught communication strategies.
    • Family physician: Provided long-term outpatient medical follow-up after discharge.
    • Support workers (PSW): Assisted with personal hygiene and daily ROM exercises; assisted with meal preparation and eating; helped with home physiotherapy routines; provided critical observations at case conferences regarding Mr. Than's progress and concerns.
    • Volunteers: Assisted with household tasks and provided companionship when family members were away.
    34 岁的高中化学教师杰弗里·谭（Jeffrey Than）在骑自行车上班途中不幸遭遇小型货车剧烈撞击。头部遭受致命性重创，导致严重创伤性脑损伤（TBI）并伴随全身多发性骨折。经急诊开颅血肿清除及骨折内固定术后，在 ICU 抢救 10 天，完全失语且无法辨识双亲与妻子。随后转入急性病房救治 2 个月，病情平稳后移送至专科神经康复病房系统康复 3 个月，最终顺利出院并在社区与家中持续接受了长达 6 个月的密集恢复性照护。
    在这场历时近一年的艰苦康复战役中，多学科康复团队展现了无与伦比的协同作战：

    • 谭先生及其家属：在每个阶段担任核心决策者，全面参与照护全流程，重新研习并掌握失能照料与自我康复技能；
    • 神经外科与骨科主刀医师：主导急诊手术抢救，监控术后骨愈合与颅内压生理稳定；
    • 临床护士团队：在急性期、康复期全流程协调并落实专业临床护理；
    • 康复医学专科医师（Physiatrist）：全面统筹领导多学科康复处方与整体治疗规划；
    • 神经心理学专家（Neuropsychologists）：精准测评伤后前额叶智力、近期记忆、情绪调控及性格异变；制定神经行为干预方案；
    • 医务社工（Social workers）：协助联络成人日间照料项目，开展家庭心理危机干预，申请公共伤残救济基金；
    • 个案管理师（Case manager）：无缝衔接出院居家照护转介，主持日间机构接管过渡；
    • 注册作业治疗师（OT）：系统评估日常自理（ADLs）缺陷；出院前亲自上门开展住宅无障碍适老化评估与改造；处方自理辅助装备；
    • 注册物理治疗师（PT）：深入测评肌力、关节活动度及前庭平衡觉；运用外骨骼机器人与虚拟现实仿真技术开展神经康复；处方步态训练；
    • 物理治疗助理（PTA）：根据物理治疗师指令，现场督导协助案主重复巩固活动度训练与辅具操作；
    • 注册言语语言病理学家（SLP）：系统筛查运动性失语与构音障碍，严密评估安全吞咽机能；指导家属掌握非语言替代交流策略；
    • 社区家庭全科医师：出院后负责全生命周期慢病管理与常规随访体检；
    • 个人支持工作者（PSW）：每日贴身协助个人洗漱、更衣与被动 ROM 训练；协助准备软质营养膳食并提供进食协助；督导家属落实居家理疗练习；作为与案主接触最持久的人员，定期在多学科研讨会上提交关于谭先生功能进步、情绪波动及家属真实顾虑的最权威第一手观察报告；
    • 社区志愿者（Volunteers）：协助分担日常家务繁重杂物，在家人外出时提供温暖的床旁陪伴与心理倾听。
    p. 289

    Role of the Family

    家庭在康复历程中的支柱性作用与家庭辅导

    Rehabilitation of clients also involves their family members, who need to learn about the illness, injury, or disability and how to care for their loved ones. Family support and involvement in the client's care can play a crucial part of the client's rehabilitation success. Care often involves helping the client practise new skills.

    服务对象的康复绝非个体的孤立事件，它深深卷入并重构着整个家庭系统的运转。家庭成员必须系统研习疾病病理、创伤机制与残疾特征，掌握科学照料所爱之人的专业技能。亲属深沉的情感支柱与全程参与，往往是决定康复成败的最关键生理心理催化剂。在日常照料中，家属需要每日督促并陪伴案主反复操练新习得的代偿技能。

    The family also learns new skills—for example, how to communicate with a spouse who has lost the ability to speak, how to cope with the behaviour of a teenager with a mental health disorder, or how to dress a child with physical disabilities. Counselling is provided, as needed, to help the family cope with changes affecting them. Families dealing with the rehabilitation of a member with a chronic health problem will need constant support from team members because the challenges to a normal family life can be overwhelming, and family members need to know that the team is listening to their concerns.

    家属自身亦必须攻克前所未有的相处技巧——例如学习如何利用手势图卡与罹患失语症的伴侣展开有效交流、如何理性应对出现冲动行为障碍的青春期精神创伤患儿、或如何以符合人体工效学的体位为脑瘫残疾儿童穿戴衣裤。多学科团队按需向家属提供危机心理疏导。长期照料慢性严重伤残亲属对传统家庭节奏构成了毁灭性重创与极度疲劳，家属极需来自康复团队的持续性赋能与喘息倾听，让家属真切感受到自身的焦虑与呼声始终被团队庄严重视。

    Therapy and Training

    功能疗法、技能重塑与适应性辅具训练

    The professionals on the rehabilitation team choose the therapy and training needed to meet the client's goals. The client is taught how to improve a skill or how to perform a task and practises what was learned either independently or with a caregiver or a family member.

    多学科康复团队中的注册专家根据案主的个性化目标，开具精准的功能疗法与动作重构处方。案主在专业指导下学习如何改善特定机能或完成复杂的 ADL 自理动作，并在随后的日常生活中由支持工作者或亲属陪伴反复强化巩固。

    You may be required to help clients practise skills or tasks. The client's therapy and training may involve learning to use self-help devices. Specific equipment to meet the client's needs is obtained, and the client is taught how to use it:

    支持工作者的一项核心职业使命，便是督导并协助案主在日常起居中反复操练已学技能。康复训练极其依赖现代自理辅助器具（Self-help devices）。团队会为案主量身配置最适宜的装备并实施适应性培训：

    • • Prostheses—Prostheses are artificial replacements for missing body parts (e.g., feet, knees, lower limbs, upper limbs, hands, breasts, and eyes). The goal for a prosthesis is to be like the missing body part in function and appearance. Artificial limbs are made from wood, aluminum, and plastic, and most are powered by the client's own muscles in the stump or nearby muscles. Physiotherapists strengthen these muscle groups. Support workers help clients adapt to wearing the prosthesis and provide skin care to the amputation stump.
      假体与假肢（Prostheses）：用于替代人体缺失部位（如人工足、膝关节、下肢、上肢、仿生机械手、义乳及义眼）的生物力学装置。其终极目标是力求在外观力线与生理功能上最大限度逼真替代原生肢体。假肢通常由碳纤维、钛铝合金及高分子塑料复合制成。现代假肢主要依托残肢末端肌肉（Stump muscles）或邻近大肌群的自主收缩进行肌电信号驱动，物理治疗师（PT）会专门强化这部分核心肌力。支持工作者负责协助案主日常穿戴扣合假肢，并每日严密巡查截肢残端皮肤（严防出现压红、水泡及深层压疮感染）。
    • • Orthotics—An orthotic is an apparatus worn to support and align parts of the musculoskeletal system and prevent or correct problems associated with it (e.g., splints, foot supports, knee and back braces). The client learns to put on, use, and care for the orthotic. Support workers assist with application and safe mobility practice.
      矫形器与支具（Orthotics）：佩戴于体表用于支撑、矫正肌骨力线并阻断病理畸形的外固定器械（如防指屈挛缩手部功能夹板、踝足矫形器 AFO、膝关节锁定支架及胸腰椎坚固背架等）。案主需掌握佩戴与维护要领，支持工作者负责协助穿脱并在步态训练中全程护卫。
    • • Eating and drinking devices—These include glass holders with adapted grips, plate guards (curved raised rims that prevent food from sliding off the plate), and utensils with curved, weighted handles or palm cuffs for clients with tremors or grip deficits.
      适应性进餐饮水用具：专为震颤麻痹或握力缺失案主研发。涵盖防倾倒双耳杯托、餐盘防溢边缘卡圈（Plate guards，防止案主用汤匙舀食物时滑落盘外）、加粗加重或折弯手柄的特殊勺叉，以及可固定于手掌虎口的魔术贴绑带餐具。
    • • Self-care devices—These include electronic toothbrushes, long-handled combs, hair washers, long-handled sponges for bathing, and bathing mitts with built-in soap holders (FIGURE 16.2), as well as devices that assist with dressing, cooking, and telephone communication.
      个人自理专用辅助工具：包括声波电动牙刷、专为肩关节活动受限者定制的加长弯柄梳子与毛刷、洗头器、长柄沐浴海绵以及内置肥皂防滑卡槽的洗澡手套（图 16.2），极大消除了案主在晨间洗漱擦浴时对外界的绝对依赖。
    p. 290

    __ABBR_16__16.3 illustrates ingenious self-care assistive devices designed to restore daily functional autonomy: A. A button hook and zipper pull: Used by clients with fine motor deficits or hemiplegia to button and zip clothing independently with one hand. B.

    图 16.3 生动展示了现代作业治疗中用于重构日常自理机能的巧妙辅助工具： 图 A：扣钮器与拉链辅助钩（Button hook）：专为手指精细动作失调或中风偏瘫案主设计，使案主单手即可轻松穿拉衬衫纽扣与衣裤拉链； 图 B：穿袜器（Sock assist）：采用弧形柔性塑料模具，预先将短袜或长筒袜套在塑料槽外，案主将其抛掷地面，双脚踏入后双手拉扯两侧尼龙拉绳，袜子便顺势紧密包裹足底与小腿，彻底免除了弯腰超过 90° 的高危脱位动作； 图 C：长柄鞋拔与脱鞋器（Shoe remover）：无需剧烈深屈髋关节即可从容穿脱鞋履； 图 D：多功能长柄取物夹（Reachers）：轻量化杠杆抓取夹，案主端坐轮椅上即可轻松夹取高处壁橱调料瓶或捡拾地面掉落的钥匙，彻底消除了弯腰探身坠地骨折风险； 图 E：球形门把手力矩转换器（Doorknob turner）：套装在传统圆形门锁上的加长杠杆手柄，极度适合重度手部类风湿关节炎无法扭动圆锁的虚弱案主。

    A sock assist: A flexible plastic mold where a sock or stocking is fitted over the curved core; the client drops it to the floor and pulls on cords to slide the foot into the sock without bending the hip past 90 degrees. C. A shoe remover (shoehorn/boot jack): Enables taking off shoes without strain on hips and knees.

    D. Reachers: Lightweight mechanical grabbers that allow clients to retrieve objects from high shelves or off the floor without bending or risking falls. E. A doorknob turner: An extended lever sleeve attached over circular doorknobs to increase mechanical leverage for clients with severe arthritis.

    Devices to Aid Mobility

    助行辅具与轮椅转移过桥滑板（Transfer Board）

    Devices to aid mobility include crutches, canes, walkers, and braces, as well as wheelchairs for some clients (see Chapter 15). If possible, clients in a wheelchair learn how to transfer themselves to and from the chair using a transfer board (FIGURE 16.4), which helps a person move from one seat to another without weight-bearing on the legs. The client also learns to transfer to and from the bed, toilet, bathtub, sofas, and cars.

    助行与位移装备系统涵盖拐杖、手杖、助行架、下肢矫形支具以及高定制轮椅（详见第 15 章）。对于双下肢截瘫或严重无力而上肢残存推撑肌力的轮椅案主，必须系统研习移位滑板（Transfer board，图 16.4）的过桥转移技术！移位板是一块表面光滑平整的坚硬板桥，两端分别搭扣于轮椅座垫与目标平面（如病床、马桶坐圈、汽车座椅或浴缸凳）之间。案主无需双下肢承重立起，只需依靠双臂支撑和臀部水平顺滑挪移，即可独立在不同座椅之间实现无缝平行位移。

    Other Specialized Equipment

    肠内营养管饲与机械通气等生命支持装备的长期适应

    Some clients need specialized life-sustaining medical equipment: • Enteral nutrition feeding tubes (see Chapter 28) for clients with permanent dysphagia. • Mechanical ventilation (see Chapter 39) for clients with cervical spinal cord trauma or neuromuscular diseases (e.g., ALS). Some clients are eventually weaned from the ventilator, while others must adapt to lifelong mechanical ventilation in home settings.

    部分伴有严重全身创伤或终末期神经肌肉退行性疾病的案主，需要借助专科维生医疗设备维持生存：• 胃造瘘或空肠营养管饲（Feeding tubes，详见第 28 章），用于完全丧失吞咽机能的脑干卒中或颅脑重创伤患；• 机械通气呼吸机（Mechanical ventilation，详见第 39 章），用于高位颈髓横断截瘫或进行性肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS，渐冻症）案主。部分案主经脱机训练可拔管自主呼吸，而另一部分群体则必须在支持工作者协助下适应终身居家机械通气生活。

    ASSISTING WITH REHABILITATION AND RESTORATIVE CARE

    支持工作者在康复与恢复性照护中的协助职责与同理心

    As a support worker, you will encounter a number of clients who are undergoing some form of rehabilitation or restorative care, some of whom will be adjusting to overwhelming change in their lives. Rehabilitation is often slow and frustrating because improvement may not be seen for weeks or months. Some clients improve quickly at first, but the pace of improvement may then slow (plateau phase), causing great frustration and hardship to clients, so you must be patient, supportive, and empathetic (see the Providing Compassionate Care box).

    作为一线支持工作者，你将在执业生涯中遇到大量经历不同程度康复与恢复性照护的服务对象。他们中的每一个人，都在咬紧牙关适应人生突如其来的毁灭性剧变。康复绝非笔直上升的坦途，而是一段充斥着极度沮丧与漫长煎熬的心路历程——神经突触的重构与软组织修复往往数周乃至数月都看不到任何肉眼可见的突破！许多案主在急性期初期功能进步迅速，但随后不可避免地陷入漫长的“功能平台期（Plateau phase）”，机能停滞不前甚至出现周期性倒退。这极易诱发案主发生崩塌式的绝望、抑郁与愤怒。支持工作者必须具备钢铁般的专业耐心、深沉的同理心与情感托底能力（详见“以同理心提供慈爱康复照护”专栏）。

    p. 291

    Transfer Board Mechanics

    图解 16.4：移位滑板（Transfer Board）轮椅至床/浴缸转移技术

    __ABBR_16__16.4 demonstrates the safe application of the transfer board by a wheelchair client: Panel A: Transfer from a wheelchair to a bed. The wheelchair is positioned at a 30 to 45 degree angle to the bed, wheels locked, armrest and footrest removed on the transfer side. One end of the transfer board is placed securely under the client's buttocks, bridging the gap to the bed mattress.

    图 16.4 详尽图解了轮椅案主独立运用移位滑板（Transfer board）实施过桥转移的力学技术规范： 图 A：从轮椅向病床转移：将轮椅以 30° 至 45° 锐角斜靠于床沿，双侧脚轮刹车制动器必须绝对牢牢锁死！彻底拆除靠床一侧的轮椅活动扶手与活动脚踏板。将移位滑板的一端稳妥压塞在案主臀部坐骨结节下方，另一端平整搭架在坚实的病床床垫上形成稳定斜桥。

    The client pushes down with arms and slides smoothly across the board. Panel B: Transfer from a wheelchair to a bathtub. The transfer board bridges from the wheelchair seat to a dedicated bath bench inside the tub, allowing safe entry without stepping over the tub rim.

    案主双手向下推撑轮椅座架与床沿，臀部顺着打蜡的光滑板面平稳横向滑移至病床上。图 B：从轮椅向浴缸安全转移：移位滑板横跨架设在轮椅坐垫与浴缸内部牢固固定的专用洗澡转移凳（Bath bench）之间。偏瘫或截瘫案主无需双腿支撑站立迈越湿滑高大的浴缸外壁边缘，即可平稳滑入浴缸就坐，彻底清除了浴室跌倒第一高危隐患。

    p. 292

    PROVIDING COMPASSIONATE CARE: Assisting With Rehabilitation and Restorative Care

    专栏：以同理心提供慈爱康复照护——DIPPS 人文关怀六大维度的临床深度践行
    • Dignity: Treat clients with unconditional positive respect. Clients do not need pity; they need encouragement, positive reinforcement, and celebration of small gains. Never show impatience when explanations yield slow results. Having little control over one's body is deeply agonizing. Acknowledge the six classic stages of grief and adaptation to disability: Shock, Denial, Anger, Depression, Reaction against independence, and Acceptance. Family and client may not progress through these stages at the same pace.

    • Independence: Independence is the ultimate goal. Encourage clients to perform ADLs to the absolute limit of their ability. Never rush them! Allow ample time to complete each task. Master their self-help assistive devices and reinforce techniques taught by the therapy team.

    • Individualized care: Tailor care strictly to the client's physical, cognitive, and psychosocial strengths and limitations. Adapt interventions to personal routines.

    • Preferences: Honor personal choices. Freedom of choice restores a sense of internal control.

    • Privacy: Many clients feel profound shame or embarrassment practicing basic skills (eating, walking, dressing) in front of others. Provide absolute visual and spatial privacy during skill practice, care procedures, and elimination. Maintain strict confidentiality.

    • Safety: Illness, muscle weakness, and mental fatigue dramatically elevate accident risks. Never push clients beyond safe physical limits; schedule mandatory rest intervals. Maintain body alignment and safe transfer mechanics. Crucial safety mandate in facility settings: Ensure that the emergency call bell and overbed table are positioned on the client's UNAFFECTED (strong) side at all times!
    • 尊严（Dignity）：给予案主无条件的尊重与接纳。失能案主需要的绝不是同情或可怜，而是发自内心的尊重、持续的肯定与对微小机能突破的热情赞美！当长者因认知受损无法理解指令时，严禁流露出半点焦躁或轻视！体会案主面对躯体失控时的深层绝望。深刻洞察案主及家属在遭遇残疾打击时必然经历的心理防御六大阶段：
    1. 震惊麻木（Shock）；2. 否认现实（Denial）；3. 暴躁愤怒（Anger）；4. 抑郁消沉（Depression）；5. 反抗自立（Reaction against independence，消极依赖退行）；6. 最终接纳与重塑（Acceptance）。案主与家属往往处于不同步的心理周期中，需给予差异化同理陪伴。

    • 独立性（Independence）：独立是康复的终极灵魂。鼓励案主在安全前提下自主完成个人自理活动（ADLs）。严禁催促抢步！留出充足时间让案主自行穿衣扣纽。熟练掌握案主专用的自理辅助用具，与治疗师保持步调一致。

    • 个性化照护（Individualized Care）：依据案主的认知储备、残余肌力、心理韧性及既往起居习惯制定照护节奏，彻底摒弃“一刀切”的机械化护理。

    • 个人偏好（Preferences）：充分尊重个人习惯与自决权，哪怕是极其微小的日程自主权，也能重新点燃长者对生命掌控的自信火种。

    • 隐私保护（Privacy）：在旁人众目睽睽之下笨拙地练习咀嚼吞咽、迈步蹒跚或扣钮穿衣，会引发长者强烈的羞耻与尴尬！训练练习与排泄护理时必须拉拢隔帘、关门营造私密庇护空间，恪守医疗信息保密誓言。

    • 安全第一（Safety）：肌力衰弱与中枢脑疲劳会急剧倍增跌倒创伤风险。严禁强行逼迫案主超负荷受训，强制设定穿插休息时间。全程贯彻优良身体力学与平稳转移。机构环境下的绝对生命安全底线：必须百分之百确保紧急呼叫铃（Call bell）与可移动床头餐桌时刻放置在案主未受损的健侧（Unaffected side）！确保长者在突发危急时健手一键呼救！
    p. 293

    OVERALL BENEFITS OF REHABILITATION AND RESTORATIVE CARE

    康复与恢复性照护对长者家庭及加拿大医疗体系的综合长远效益

    Rehabilitation and restorative care can be very beneficial to clients and their families. These benefits include slowing a client's decline of functioning, maintaining or improving functioning, restoring the client to the previous functional level as much as possible, and preserving the client's quality of life and independence. However, there are a number of systemic socioeconomic benefits that rehabilitation and restorative care provide to Canadians and the healthcare system:

    系统性的康复护理与恢复性照护为服务对象及其整个家庭带来了深远福祉：有效遏制全身机能发生雪崩式衰退、保全并挖掘残存代偿潜力、协助案主最大化找回病前独立机能，并持久捍卫其晚年生活品质与生命尊严。更具深远意义的是，康复与恢复性照护对整个加拿大社会经济与公共医疗体系（Medicare）展现了不可估量的系统性红利：

    • • Shorter or no hospital stays for clients: Rather than staying in an acute-care hospital for weeks or months, clients can transition home or to short-stay facilities in their communities. In Canada, reablement programs have been widely established for individuals who do not require acute medical beds but struggle to manage at home independently, allowing them to stay in their own homes longer. Respite programs provide temporary relief to family caregivers.
      显著缩短或消除住院周期：使案主无需在急性三甲医院中滞留数周乃至数月，而是迅速回归其原生社区或短期过渡机构。在加拿大各省，赋能自立计划（Reablement programs，重赋权方案）已成为公共卫生的前沿典范——专门面向那些已度过急性危重期、但出院后暂时无法独自料理生活或在居家环境中挣扎恢复体能的脆弱长者，通过多学科密集赋能服务使其能够继续长久居住在自己家中安享晚年。喘息照护计划（Respite programs）则为身心俱疲的家庭全职照料者提供临时替代托管照护，防范家庭系统崩溃。
    • • Telehealth in remote and northern regions: Health care providers provide remote clinical instructions and biomechanical assessments through videoconferencing, allowing clients in rural and northern communities to remain in their homes.
      边远原住民与北部地区远程医疗覆盖：在加拿大辽阔的北部极寒与偏远农村社区，高级治疗师利用高清视频会议远程医疗（Telehealth）开展动作评估与居家训练督导，彻底免除了长者跨越数千公里长途奔波就医的艰辛。
    • • Preserving true independence: Clients who live at home maintain functional autonomy and familiarity far superior to long-term institutionalization.
      最大化保全生命独立尊严：身处熟悉的家庭生活环境中，案主保留着高度的日常生活自决权，其神经突触重塑与生活机能恢复水准显著优于长期被动圈养在养老机构。
    • • Less disruption for families: Discharging clients closer to home enables families to visit frequently without draining financial resources on long-distance travel and lodging.
      极大降低对正常家庭生活的破坏：使长者重回家庭亲情环抱，子女亲属无需耗费巨额差旅住宿成本跨城市陪护探视，维系了健康稳定的家庭经济结构。
    • • Massive taxpayer cost savings: Acute hospital beds are extraordinarily expensive to taxpayers. Delivering high-quality restorative care in outpatient and home settings saves millions of healthcare dollars, allowing funds to be reallocated to other critical healthcare priorities.
      为公共财政节约天文数字般的医疗开支：在公费医疗体制下，急性综合医院病床的每日综合开销对纳税人而言是极其高昂的负担。将康复重心下沉至社区居家与日间门诊，能够为公共医疗基金节约数以亿计的宝贵财政资金，促使医疗资源重组再配置于急危重症等最核心领域。
    p. 294

    CHAPTER REVIEW: KEY POINTS

    第 16 章全真核心知识点权威总结回顾
    • • Rehabilitation care is the use of therapy, exercise, and other methods to restore a person to the highest possible level of functioning. It may address acute injuries (short-term) or chronic conditions (long-term), maintaining function or slowing functional decline.
      康复护理是通过物理治疗、针对性功能锻炼及辅助手段，促使案主恢复至最高可能生理机能的医疗过程。它既适用于急性外伤后的短期功能重建，也贯穿于慢性退行性疾病的长期管理中，起到延缓衰退、保留生活品质的核心作用。
    • • Restorative care is aimed at preventing health deterioration, maintaining or improving quality of life, and restoring previous functional levels as much as possible. It is primarily provided by nurses and support workers in daily care.
      恢复性照护旨在防止机体机能发生继发性恶化，维持并增进生命品质，并在最大限度内协助案主找回自主独立。这项照护主要由护士和支持工作者在日常饮食、洗漱、入厕及活动等基础护理场景中无缝开展。
    • • Every client has an individualized care plan with unique goals and multidisciplinary team members. Support workers have the most ongoing contact with clients, making their input at conferences and reports vital.
      每位服务对象都拥有高度定制化的个性化护理计划与康复目标。由于支持工作者在日常生活中与案主保持着最持久、最频繁的贴身接触，工作者对案主微小机能变化和情绪波动的观察汇报，构成了团队个案研讨会（Care Conferences）的最关键决策依据。
    • • Therapy and rehabilitation are essential to help clients reach their personal goal of independence. The care plan establishes the support worker's exact role in each step of functional training.
      系统性的功能疗法与适应性训练是助力案主迈向自立尊严的必由之路。护理计划严格界定了支持工作者在各个康复阶段中的协助边界与实操规范。
    • • Family members are vital members of the rehabilitation team. They must learn about the condition, acquire new caregiving skills, and receive continuous emotional and respite support from the healthcare team.
      家庭成员是康复团队不可或缺的基石核心。家属需要深入理解疾病病理，学习全新的沟通与协助技巧，并应当从医疗团队处持续获得心理疏导与喘息照护支持。
    • • Psychosocial elements deeply affect clients' reactions to their conditions. Emotional stages such as shock, denial, anger, depression, and gradual acceptance must be met with patience, compassion, and non-judgmental listening.
      社会心理因素深刻影响着案主对自身残疾的心理适应。从最初的震惊、否认、愤怒，到抑郁消沉乃至最终接纳，支持工作者必须以极大的同理心、深度的包容与倾听去陪伴案主走过心理阴霾。

    CRITICAL THINKING IN PRACTICE

    临床批判性思维修炼：中风偏瘫案主抗拒训练绝望盛怒危机处置

    __ABBR_3__ Lazar has right-sided weakness following a recent stroke. You are his support worker, assigned to help him with his care plan of restorative exercises after his discharge from the rehabilitation hospit__ABBR_13__ Today, __ABBR_3__ Lazar is reluctant to participate in any of his usual exercises and, instead, has angrily told you to leave his house.

    【临床批判性思维修炼】拉扎尔先生（Mr. Lazar）近期遭遇缺血性脑卒中（中风）导致右侧肢体瘫痪无力。你作为他的专属社区支持工作者，负责在他从康复医院出院后，协助其落实个性化恢复性锻炼计划。今天，拉扎尔先生对常规训练表现出极度抵触，愤怒地吼叫让你立即离开他的家，并沮丧哭诉：“反正我根本做不到，每次尝试都痛得要命，做这些到底还有什么意义？

    He also said, 'What is the point of doing all of this when I can't do it and it hurts to try?' You are unsure of what to do or say to him. Should you leave immediately, as he has asked you to? Should you call your supervisor?

    ！”面对长者的盛怒与绝望，你应当如何应对？你应当立刻顺从他的要求甩门离开，还是应当留在现场？你应当何时向上级主管护士汇报？

    Professional Clinical Response & Rationale: 1. Do NOT Leave Immediately: Leaving immediately abandons a vulnerable client in severe emotional distress and risks safety (__ABBR_0__, fall, despair, unmanaged pain). Acknowledge that anger and frustration are natural, documented stages of grief and adjustment to disability. 2.

    【专家临床思维精析与标准实操规程】： 1. 绝对不可直接甩门离开：顺从案主的非理性愤怒立即摔门而去属于严重的“遗弃案主（Abandonment）”职业失范行为！必须清醒认识到：愤怒、暴躁与消沉是突发残疾案主在经历心理哀伤反应时的经典生理防御阶段（Shock → Denial → Anger → Depression → Acceptance），长者的怒火实质是对身体失控的巨大恐惧与尊严坍塌的外化发泄，绝非针对支持工作者个人。2. 运用同理心倾听与降温沟通：保持语调平稳轻柔，降低身体姿态至与案主平视，给予充分共情与接纳：“拉扎尔先生，我完全理解您的痛苦与精疲力竭。

    Apply Empathetic De-escalation & Active Listening: Remain calm, calm your voice, and validate his feelings: '__ABBR_3__ Lazar, I hear how exhausting and painful this has been for you, and it is completely understandable that you feel frustrated today.' Sit down at eye level, remove pressure to perform the exercises immediately, and offer him a brief rest period. 3. Explore Pain & Comfort Barriers: Inquire gently about his physical pain: 'Where does it hurt most today? Did you take your prescribed pain relief before our session?' Often, non-compliance stems from untreated acute physical pain. 4.

    面对中风的打击，换作任何人都会感到无比沮丧与愤怒，您有权利表达您的不甘与委屈。”立即免除案主即刻训练的心理压力，倒一杯温水，允许其宣泄情绪。3. 排查躯体疼痛与耐受障碍：深入探查抗拒背后的真实物理原因：“拉扎尔先生，您刚才提到一动就痛，请告诉我具体是哪个关节或肌肉疼痛最剧烈？今天在训练前是否按时服用了止痛药物？”临床上，长者的抗拒往往源于未得到有效控制的躯体剧痛。

    Call Supervisor & Document: Reassure the client that his choices are respected today. Step into another room to call your supervisor. Report his severe frustration, pain complaints, and refusal of exercises. The supervisor can consult the physiotherapist to reassess pain management or adapt the exercise intensity. Document the verbatim dialogue, client affect, vital signs, and supervisor directives objectively.

    4. 汇报主管护士与专业调整：在安抚案主情绪后，明确告知其今天的决定受到尊重。随后致电主管护士，详尽汇报案主的剧烈疼痛、绝望心理及暂停训练情况。主管护士将协调物理治疗师（PT）重新评估运动负荷并调整止痛处方。最后在护理记录单上客观、中立地记录案主原话、情绪反应及主管指示，严密闭环证据链。
